benchmark_models/stochastic_volatility_centred_sliced_latent_path_Stan_math.stan (79 lines)
// Stochastic volatility, CENTRED: the log volatilities h are the parameters (the same posterior over
// (mu, phi, sigma, h) as the non-centred model with h_std; the sampler moves in other coordinates). Every term
// depends on h[t] and h[t - 1] only, so each chunk of reduce_sum_static holds its own observations and
// transitions; outside the chunks there are only h[1]'s stationary term and the transitions across chunk
// boundaries (one per boundary). The deterministic binary partitions match Stan Math's simple partitioner for
// reduce_sum_static. Parameter count and order do not depend on chunk_size.

functions {
    array[] int fn_deterministic_leaf_starts(data int first, data int last, data int grainsize) {
        int length_of_range = last - first + 1;
        if (length_of_range <= grainsize) return { first };
        int middle = first + length_of_range %/% 2;
        return append_array(fn_deterministic_leaf_starts(first, middle - 1, grainsize),
                            fn_deterministic_leaf_starts(middle, last, grainsize));
    }

    real fn_density_of_latent_path_slice_lpdf(array[] real h_slice, int start, int end, data array[] real y,
                                              data array[] int leaf_first, data array[] int leaf_of_time,
                                              real mu, real phi, real sigma) {
        int n = end - start + 1;
        if (start != leaf_first[leaf_of_time[start]]) {
            reject("Unexpected deterministic reduce_sum_static boundary: ", start);
        }
        vector[n] h_chunk = to_vector(h_slice);
        real log_density = normal_lupdf(to_vector(y[start:end]) | 0, exp(h_chunk / 2));
        if (n > 1) {
            log_density += normal_lupdf(h_chunk[2:n] | mu + phi * (h_chunk[1:(n - 1)] - mu), sigma);
        }
        return log_density;
    }
}

data {
    int<lower=1> T;
    array[T] real y;
    int<lower=1> N;
    int<lower=1> chunk_size;
}

transformed data {
    if (N != T) reject("N must equal the number of time points T.");
    int n_leaves = size(fn_deterministic_leaf_starts(1, T, chunk_size));
    array[n_leaves] int leaf_first = fn_deterministic_leaf_starts(1, T, chunk_size);
    array[T] int leaf_of_time;
    for (b in 1:n_leaves) {
        int leaf_last = b < n_leaves ? leaf_first[b + 1] - 1 : T;
        leaf_of_time[leaf_first[b]:leaf_last] = rep_array(b, leaf_last - leaf_first[b] + 1);
    }
    //// (the first time point of every chunk but the first, and the time point before it: the transitions that
    ////  cross a chunk boundary, the only latent terms outside the chunks)
    array[n_leaves - 1] int first_of_later_leaves = leaf_first[2:n_leaves];
    array[n_leaves - 1] int last_of_earlier_leaves;
    for (b in 2:n_leaves) last_of_earlier_leaves[b - 1] = leaf_first[b] - 1;
}

parameters {
    array[T] real h;
    real mu;
    real<lower=-1, upper=1> phi;
    real<lower=0> sigma;
}

model {
    phi ~ uniform(-1, 1);
    sigma ~ normal(0, 0.5);
    mu ~ normal(0, 2);
    //// the stationary first state and the transitions that cross a chunk boundary (n_leaves - 1 terms)
    h[1] ~ normal(mu, sigma / sqrt(1 - square(phi)));
    if (n_leaves > 1) {
        target += normal_lupdf(to_vector(h[first_of_later_leaves]) |
                              mu + phi * (to_vector(h[last_of_earlier_leaves]) - mu), sigma);
    }
    target += reduce_sum_static(fn_density_of_latent_path_slice_lupdf, h, chunk_size,
                                 y, leaf_first, leaf_of_time, mu, phi, sigma);
}

generated quantities {
    array[T] real volatility = to_array_1d(exp(to_vector(h) / 2));
}

benchmark_models/stochastic_volatility_centred_sliced_latent_path_hand_written_BayesMVP_AVX.stan (89 lines)
// Stochastic volatility, CENTRED: the log volatilities h are the parameters (the same posterior over
// (mu, phi, sigma, h) as the non-centred model with h_std; the sampler moves in other coordinates). Every term
// depends on h[t] and h[t - 1] only, so each chunk of reduce_sum_static holds its own observations and
// transitions; outside the chunks there are only h[1]'s stationary term and the transitions across chunk
// boundaries (one per boundary). The deterministic binary partitions match Stan Math's simple partitioner for
// reduce_sum_static. Parameter count and order do not depend on chunk_size.
// AVX version: each chunk's two normal terms are BayesMVP's nico_normal_affine_location_and_log_scale_lpdf
// (one node each, all SIMD): y[t] ~ normal(0, exp(0 + 0.5 h[t])) and h[t] ~ normal(mu (1 - phi) + phi h[t - 1],
// exp(log(sigma) + 0 h[t - 1])).

functions {
    real bmvp_simd_lanes();
    real nico_normal_affine_location_and_log_scale_lpdf(vector y, real a0, real a1, vector x, real b0, real b1,
                                                        vector w);
    array[] int fn_deterministic_leaf_starts(data int first, data int last, data int grainsize) {
        int length_of_range = last - first + 1;
        if (length_of_range <= grainsize) return { first };
        int middle = first + length_of_range %/% 2;
        return append_array(fn_deterministic_leaf_starts(first, middle - 1, grainsize),
                            fn_deterministic_leaf_starts(middle, last, grainsize));
    }

    real fn_density_of_latent_path_slice_lpdf(array[] real h_slice, int start, int end, data array[] real y,
                                              data array[] int leaf_first, data array[] int leaf_of_time,
                                              real mu, real phi, real sigma) {
        int n = end - start + 1;
        if (start != leaf_first[leaf_of_time[start]]) {
            reject("Unexpected deterministic reduce_sum_static boundary: ", start);
        }
        vector[n] h_chunk = to_vector(h_slice);
        real log_density = nico_normal_affine_location_and_log_scale_lupdf(to_vector(y[start:end]) | 0, 0,
                                                                            h_chunk, 0, 0.5, h_chunk);
        if (n > 1) {
            log_density += nico_normal_affine_location_and_log_scale_lupdf(h_chunk[2:n] | mu * (1 - phi), phi,
                                                                            h_chunk[1:(n - 1)], log(sigma), 0,
                                                                            h_chunk[1:(n - 1)]);
        }
        return log_density;
    }
}

data {
    int<lower=1> T;
    array[T] real y;
    int<lower=1> N;
    int<lower=1> chunk_size;
}

transformed data {
    if (N != T) reject("N must equal the number of time points T.");
    int n_leaves = size(fn_deterministic_leaf_starts(1, T, chunk_size));
    array[n_leaves] int leaf_first = fn_deterministic_leaf_starts(1, T, chunk_size);
    array[T] int leaf_of_time;
    for (b in 1:n_leaves) {
        int leaf_last = b < n_leaves ? leaf_first[b + 1] - 1 : T;
        leaf_of_time[leaf_first[b]:leaf_last] = rep_array(b, leaf_last - leaf_first[b] + 1);
    }
    //// (the first time point of every chunk but the first, and the time point before it: the transitions that
    ////  cross a chunk boundary, the only latent terms outside the chunks)
    array[n_leaves - 1] int first_of_later_leaves = leaf_first[2:n_leaves];
    array[n_leaves - 1] int last_of_earlier_leaves;
    for (b in 2:n_leaves) last_of_earlier_leaves[b - 1] = leaf_first[b] - 1;
}

parameters {
    array[T] real h;
    real mu;
    real<lower=-1, upper=1> phi;
    real<lower=0> sigma;
}

model {
    phi ~ uniform(-1, 1);
    sigma ~ normal(0, 0.5);
    mu ~ normal(0, 2);
    //// the stationary first state and the transitions that cross a chunk boundary (n_leaves - 1 terms)
    h[1] ~ normal(mu, sigma / sqrt(1 - square(phi)));
    if (n_leaves > 1) {
        target += nico_normal_affine_location_and_log_scale_lupdf(to_vector(h[first_of_later_leaves]) |
                              mu * (1 - phi), phi, to_vector(h[last_of_earlier_leaves]), log(sigma), 0,
                              to_vector(h[last_of_earlier_leaves]));
    }
    target += reduce_sum_static(fn_density_of_latent_path_slice_lupdf, h, chunk_size,
                                 y, leaf_first, leaf_of_time, mu, phi, sigma);
}

generated quantities {
    real simd_lanes = bmvp_simd_lanes();
}

benchmark_models/latent_diffusion_survival_unchunked_no_loops_over_N_with_Stan_fused_functions.stan (139 lines)
// latent_diffusion_survival_unchunked_no_loops_over_N_with_Stan_fused_functions.stan
// Proportional hazards model of survival after diagnosis (e.g. a cancer registry) whose log baseline hazard is a
// latent Ornstein-Uhlenbeck diffusion, with covariates. For subject n at time t (years):
//
//     log h_n(t) = x(t) + covariates[n] * beta,
//     dx(t) = kappa (mu_x - x(t)) dt + diffusion_scale dW(t),   x(0) = x_0,
//
// i.e. a log baseline hazard that varies smoothly around its long-run level mu_x and returns to it with rate
// kappa per year (as kappa -> 0, the random walk used for the Cox baseline hazard in practice, e.g. INLA). On the
// M-step Euler grid of [0, t_max] (dt = t_max / M): x at the M + 1 grid points from the standard normal
// innovations w (non-centred; w is the nuisance block, declared first), and subject n's hazard linear in t within
// each grid cell, equal to exp(x_k + covariates[n] * beta) at the grid points. With g_k = exp(x_k) the baseline
// hazard at grid point k and C_k its cumulative (trapezoid) up to grid point k, for t[n] in cell k (lower grid
// point k, fraction f_n of the cell, time tau_n into it):
//
//     h_n(t[n]) = exp(covariates[n] * beta) ((1 - f_n) g_k + f_n g_(k+1)),
//     H_n(t[n]) = exp(covariates[n] * beta) (C_k + a_n g_k + b_n g_(k+1)),
//     a_n = tau_n (2 - f_n) / 2,   b_n = tau_n f_n / 2,
//
// so that the log likelihood is sum over the events of (covariates[n] * beta + log h_0(t[n])) minus
// sum over all subjects of exp(covariates[n] * beta) times the baseline cumulative hazard at t[n]: whole-vector
// operations on the subjects (one exp per subject, one log per event), the data weights a_n and b_n and the cells
// made once in transformed data. (Stan's poisson_log_glm would give the same value with log(H_0(t[n])) as its
// intercepts, at the cost of one more log per subject, so the direct form is used.)
// The Stan::math unchunked model, the reference of every other version: one pass over all N
// subjects. The one loop
// left is the Euler-Maruyama recursion of the path over the M grid steps (M = 50, the same for any N).
// No loop over N anywhere.


data {
    int<lower=1> N;                          // number of subjects
    int<lower=1> K;                          // number of covariates (standardised)
    int<lower=2> M;                          // number of Euler-Maruyama steps on [0, t_max]
    real<lower=0> t_max;                     // end of follow-up (years)
    matrix[N, K] covariates;                 // the subjects' covariates
    vector<lower=0, upper=t_max>[N] t;       // event or censoring time (years after diagnosis)
    array[N] int<lower=0, upper=1> event;    // 1 = event observed, 0 = right censored at t
}


transformed data {
    real dt = t_max / M;
    real sqrt_dt = sqrt(dt);
    int N_event = sum(event);
    vector[N] event_as_vector = to_vector(event);
    array[N_event] int event_index;          // subjects with an observed event
    array[N] int cell_index;                 // lower grid point of the cell containing t[n]
    array[N] int cell_index_upper;           // upper grid point of that cell
    vector[N] weight_of_lower_grid_point;    // a_n: the weight of g_k in the baseline cumulative hazard at t[n]
    vector[N] weight_of_upper_grid_point;    // b_n: the weight of g_(k+1)
    vector[N] cell_fraction;                 // f_n: the fraction of the cell at t[n], in [0, 1]
    if (min(t) <= 0) reject("Event and censoring times must be strictly positive.");
    {
      // grid point k (1-based) sits at time (k - 1) dt; the cell of t[n] is the largest k <= M with
      // (k - 1) dt <= t[n], i.e. floor(t[n] / dt) + 1, at most M
      vector[N] cell_as_real = fmin(M, floor(t / dt) + 1);
      vector[N] time_into_cell = t - (cell_as_real - 1) * dt;
      cell_index = to_int(to_array_1d(cell_as_real));
      cell_index_upper = to_int(to_array_1d(cell_as_real + 1));
      cell_fraction = fmin(1, time_into_cell / dt);
      weight_of_lower_grid_point = 0.5 * time_into_cell .* (2 - cell_fraction);
      weight_of_upper_grid_point = 0.5 * time_into_cell .* cell_fraction;
      // the subjects with an observed event, in the subjects' order: the first N_event subjects sorted by the
      // distinct keys n + (N + 1) (1 - event[n]), which put every event (key n) before every censored subject
      vector[N] event_first_keys = linspaced_vector(N, 1, N) + (N + 1) * (1 - event_as_vector);
      event_index = sort_indices_asc(event_first_keys)[1:N_event];
    }
    // the events' cells and cell fractions (the baseline hazard at an event time, linear within its cell)
    array[N_event] int event_cell_index = cell_index[event_index];
    array[N_event] int event_cell_index_upper = cell_index_upper[event_index];
    vector[N_event] event_cell_fraction = cell_fraction[event_index];
    vector[N_event] one_minus_event_cell_fraction = 1 - event_cell_fraction;
}


parameters {
    vector[M] w;                             // standard normal innovations of the path, declared first
    real x_0;                                // log baseline hazard at diagnosis (per year)
    real mu_x;                               // long-run log baseline hazard (per year)
    real<lower=0> kappa;                     // rate of return to mu_x (per year)
    real<lower=0> diffusion_scale;           // diffusion of the log baseline hazard (per square root of a year)
    vector[K] beta;                          // log hazard ratios of the covariates
}


transformed parameters {
    vector[M + 1] x_path;                    // log baseline hazard at the M + 1 grid points
    // (the Euler-Maruyama recursion x_(k+1) = x_k + kappa (mu_x - x_k) dt + diffusion_scale sqrt(dt) w_k, with the
    //  terms that do not depend on the path computed once, as one vector; M steps, the same for any N)
    {
      vector[M] increment_without_the_path = (diffusion_scale * sqrt_dt) * w + kappa * mu_x * dt;
      real one_minus_kappa_dt = 1 - kappa * dt;
      x_path[1] = x_0;
      for (k in 1:M) {
        x_path[k + 1] = one_minus_kappa_dt * x_path[k] + increment_without_the_path[k];
      }
    }
}


model {
    // priors: weakly informative on the scales of survival after a cancer diagnosis (hazards per year)
    x_0 ~ normal(log(0.2), 1.5);
    mu_x ~ normal(log(0.1), 1.5);
    kappa ~ lognormal(log(0.5), 1);
    diffusion_scale ~ normal(0, 1);
    beta ~ normal(0, 1);
    w ~ std_normal();

    // likelihood: the baseline hazard and its cumulative on the grid, which every subject shares; then, on the
    // whole vectors of subjects and events, the events' log hazards and every subject's cumulative hazard
    {
      vector[M + 1] baseline_hazard_grid = exp(x_path);
      vector[M + 1] cumulative_baseline_hazard_grid;
      cumulative_baseline_hazard_grid[1] = 0;
      cumulative_baseline_hazard_grid[2:(M + 1)] = cumulative_sum(0.5 * dt * (baseline_hazard_grid[1:M]
                                                                              + baseline_hazard_grid[2:(M + 1)]));
      vector[N] linear_predictor = covariates * beta;
      vector[N] cumulative_baseline_hazard_at_t = cumulative_baseline_hazard_grid[cell_index]
                                                  + weight_of_lower_grid_point .* baseline_hazard_grid[cell_index]
                                                  + weight_of_upper_grid_point
                                                    .* baseline_hazard_grid[cell_index_upper];
      target += dot_product(event_as_vector, linear_predictor);
      if (N_event > 0) {
        target += sum(log(one_minus_event_cell_fraction .* baseline_hazard_grid[event_cell_index]
                          + event_cell_fraction .* baseline_hazard_grid[event_cell_index_upper]));
      }
      target += -dot_product(exp(linear_predictor), cumulative_baseline_hazard_at_t);
    }
}


generated quantities {
    vector[M + 1] baseline_hazard_path = exp(x_path);
    vector[M + 1] baseline_survival_path;    // S_0(u) = exp(-H_0(u)) at the grid points (covariates at 0)
    baseline_survival_path = exp(-append_row(0, cumulative_sum(0.5 * dt * (baseline_hazard_path[1:M]
                                                                            + baseline_hazard_path[2:(M + 1)]))));
}

// latent_diffusion_survival_chunked_no_loops_over_N.stan
// The tape-chunked model latent_diffusion_survival_chunked.stan (below) without a loop over the subjects: its
// log density and its chunks are unchanged (each chunk's terms were already whole-vector operations over the
// chunk's events, and -H(t) was already gathered by grid cell into dot products of length M), and its loops over
// the subjects in transformed data are whole-vector operations: each subject's cell is floor(t[n] / dt) + 1
// (at most M; the same cells as the loop of latent_diffusion_survival.stan on every data case), the events are
// the first N_event subjects in the order of the distinct keys n + (N + 1) (1 - event[n]) (sort_indices_asc), the
// events before each subject are a cumulative sum, and the sums over the subjects of each grid cell are the
// product of the M x N matrix of the indicators of the subjects' cells with the vectors of the subjects' terms.
// In generated quantities, the survival path is exp(-H) at the grid points, with H the cumulative sum of the
// trapezoids (the same values up to rounding).
// The only loop left is the Euler-Maruyama recursion of the path x over the M grid points (transformed
// parameters): its step is not linear in x (sin(x)), so it cannot be written as a linear system or a cumulative
// sum, and its length is M (the same for every N), not the subjects.
//
// latent_diffusion_survival_chunked.stan
// Tape-chunked version of latent_diffusion_survival.stan: the same log density, with the subjects' likelihood
// terms (log h(t) at each observed event time, and -H(t) for every subject) summed over the subjects by
// reduce_sum_static, in chunks of chunk_size subjects (data), so that each chunk's autodiff tape is built,
// differentiated and released before the next one (the tape-chunking paper's chunking; N_chunks from
// NicoStan::fn_compute_initial_N_chunks()). The latent path x_path and the hazard and integrated hazard on the
// grid, which every subject shares, are computed once, outside reduce_sum_static, and passed to every chunk.
// Each chunk computes its subjects' terms with the whole-vector operations of latent_diffusion_survival.stan
// (event_index lists the events in the subjects' order, so a chunk's events are contiguous in it).
// The chunking data are NicoStan's for Stan models: N (the subjects, the units of the chunks) and chunk_size,
// which NicoStan sets to ceiling(N / N_chunks) in each phase (num_chunks_burnin, num_chunks_sampling).
//
// Inside the chunks (everything whose cost grows with the subjects): the path interpolated at the chunk's
// event times and the log hazards there, log(x(t)^2 + x_squared_hazard_offset), one vectorised operation over
// the chunk's events. Outside the chunks, only terms whose size does not grow with N: the path recursion over the
// M + 1 grid points (sequential in the grid, the same for any N), the hazard and integrated hazard on the grid,
// N_event * log(hazard_scale), and -H(t) summed over all subjects, which is gathered by grid cell into dot
// products of length M with data computed in transformed data (as in latent_diffusion_survival.stan). x_path,
// of length M + 1, is the only autodiff argument passed to the chunks.
//
// The model, as in latent_diffusion_survival.stan:
//
// Latent diffusion survival model (Roberts and Sangalli, 2010), in the form used by
// Beskos, Kalogeropoulos and Pazos (2013, Sections 5 and 6.3). All subjects share one
// hazard trajectory h(u) = hazard_scale * (x(u)^2 + x_squared_hazard_offset), driven by the latent diffusion
//     dX_u = -(drift_sin_coefficient * sin(X_u) + drift_constant) du + sigma_x dB_u,  X_0 = x_0,
// on the observation window [0, t_max]. Beskos et al. use hazard_scale = 1, drift
// coefficients (1.4, 1), sigma_x = 1 (unit diffusion coefficient), x_0 = 2 and t_max = 1,
// and treat these as known. Here the drift coefficients and the hazard scale are estimated
// jointly with the path; sigma_x and x_0 are fixed data.
//
// Hazard offset (not in Beskos et al.): Beskos et al. use
// h(x) = x^2 exactly (x_squared_hazard_offset = 0). Then log h at an event time is 2 log|x(t)|, which is -Inf
// at x(t) = 0, and h(x) = h(-x). The drift pulls X towards its stable point -0.795 (the drift-only path from
// x_0 = 2 reaches 0 at t = 1.07, and about 60% of simulated paths cross 0 before t = 1). Once the path gets
// near zero, the posterior splits into sign patterns of x at the event times,
// separated by those -Inf walls. Hamiltonian trajectories cannot cross the walls and diverge near them:
// cmdstanr at adapt_delta 0.9 gave 120 divergences and x_path R-hat 1.11 with the old model, and still 43
// divergences and x_path R-hat 1.53 with every parameter fixed at the Beskos et al. values. A small offset
// (default 0.01 in the simulator, i.e. the hazard never falls below 1% of hazard_scale) makes log h finite
// and smooth, so the sign patterns are connected and the sampler mixes over them. The hazard shape is x^2
// wherever |x| is not tiny. Setting the offset to 0 gives the exact Beskos et al. form (and its divergences).
//
// Discretisation: Euler-Maruyama on M equal steps of length dt = t_max / M, non-centred.
// The nuisance block w holds the M standard normal Brownian increments, and
//     x[k + 1] = x[k] + drift(x[k]) * dt + sigma_x * sqrt(dt) * w[k].
// The path is taken as linear between grid points. The hazard at an event time uses the
// linearly interpolated path value (not a snap to the nearest grid point). The integrated
// hazard is the trapezoid rule over the whole grid cells before t[n], plus a trapezoid over
// the partial cell from its lower grid point to t[n]. Right-censored times contribute only
// -H(t[n]); administrative censoring at t_max is the usual case.

functions {
    // real partial_sum_subjects_lpmf(array[] int subject_slice, int start, int end,
    //                                array[] int cell_index, array[] int cell_index_upper,
    //                                vector time_into_cell, vector cell_fraction,
    //                                array[] int event_index, array[] int events_before,
    //                                real x_squared_hazard_offset, vector x_path, vector hazard_grid,
    //                                vector cumulative_hazard_grid, real hazard_scale) {
    //     int n_subjects = end - start + 1;
    //     real lp = 0;
    //     // the chunk's subjects: the path at t[n] (linearly interpolated) and the hazard there
    //     vector[n_subjects] x_at_t = (1 - cell_fraction[start:end]) .* x_path[cell_index[start:end]]
    //                                 + cell_fraction[start:end] .* x_path[cell_index_upper[start:end]];
    //     vector[n_subjects] hazard_at_t = hazard_scale * (square(x_at_t) + x_squared_hazard_offset);
    //     // the chunk's events: event_index[e1:e2] (the events of subjects start to end)
    //     int e1 = events_before[start] + 1;
    //     int e2 = events_before[end + 1];
    //     // log h(t) at the chunk's observed event times; finite at x(t) = 0 whenever
    //     // x_squared_hazard_offset > 0.
    //     if (e2 >= e1) {
    //       array[e2 - e1 + 1] int event_position_in_chunk;
    //       for (k in 1:(e2 - e1 + 1)) {
    //         event_position_in_chunk[k] = event_index[e1 + k - 1] - start + 1;
    //       }
    //       lp += (e2 - e1 + 1) * log(hazard_scale)
    //             + sum(log(square(x_at_t[event_position_in_chunk]) + x_squared_hazard_offset));
    //     }
    //     // - H(t) for every subject of the chunk, events and censored alike.
    //     lp += -sum(cumulative_hazard_grid[cell_index[start:end]]
    //                + 0.5 * time_into_cell[start:end] .* (hazard_grid[cell_index[start:end]] + hazard_at_t));
    //     return lp;
    // }
    // the chunk's events (event_index[e1:e2], the events of subjects start to end): the path at their times,
    // linearly interpolated, and log(x(t)^2 + x_squared_hazard_offset), i.e. log h(t) minus log(hazard_scale);
    // finite at x(t) = 0 whenever x_squared_hazard_offset > 0
    real partial_sum_subjects_lpmf(array[] int subject_slice, int start, int end,
                                   data array[] int events_before, data array[] int event_cell_index,
                                   data array[] int event_cell_index_upper,
                                   data vector one_minus_event_cell_fraction, data vector event_cell_fraction,
                                   data real x_squared_hazard_offset, vector x_path) {
        real lp = 0;
        int e1 = events_before[start] + 1;
        int e2 = events_before[end + 1];
        if (e2 >= e1) {
          vector[e2 - e1 + 1] x_at_event_time = one_minus_event_cell_fraction[e1:e2]
                                                .* x_path[event_cell_index[e1:e2]]
                                                + event_cell_fraction[e1:e2]
                                                  .* x_path[event_cell_index_upper[e1:e2]];
          lp += sum(log(square(x_at_event_time) + x_squared_hazard_offset));
        }
        return lp;
    }
}


data {
    int<lower=1> N;                          // number of subjects
    int<lower=2> M;                          // number of Euler-Maruyama steps on [0, t_max]
    real<lower=0> t_max;                     // end of the observation window
    real x_0;                                // fixed initial value of the latent diffusion
    real<lower=0> sigma_x;                   // fixed diffusion coefficient (1 = unit diffusion)
    real<lower=0> x_squared_hazard_offset;   // h(u) = hazard_scale * (x(u)^2 + offset);
                                             // 0 = exact Beskos et al. form
    vector<lower=0, upper=t_max>[N] t;       // event or censoring time
    array[N] int<lower=0, upper=1> event;    // 1 = event observed, 0 = right censored at t
    int<lower=1> chunk_size;                 // subjects per chunk (reduce_sum_static)
}


transformed data {
    real dt = t_max / M;
    real sqrt_dt = sqrt(dt);
    int N_event = sum(event);
    array[N_event] int event_index;          // subjects with an observed event
    array[N] int cell_index;                 // lower grid point of the cell containing t[n]
    array[N] int cell_index_upper;           // upper grid point of that cell
    vector[N] time_into_cell;                // t[n] minus the time of that lower grid point
    vector[N] cell_fraction;                 // time_into_cell / dt, in [0, 1]
    // {
    //   int position = 1;
    //   for (n in 1:N) {
    //     int cell = 1;
    //     if (t[n] <= 0) reject("Event and censoring times must be strictly positive.");
    //     // Grid point k (1-based) sits at time (k - 1) * dt; the last cell is [(M - 1) dt, t_max].
    //     while (cell < M && t[n] >= cell * dt) cell += 1;
    //     cell_index[n] = cell;
    //     cell_index_upper[n] = cell + 1;
    //     time_into_cell[n] = t[n] - (cell - 1) * dt;
    //     cell_fraction[n] = fmin(1, time_into_cell[n] / dt);
    //     if (event[n] == 1) {
    //       event_index[position] = n;
    //       position += 1;
    //     }
    //   }
    // }
    // (the same, without a loop over the subjects)
    if (min(t) <= 0) reject("Event and censoring times must be strictly positive.");
    {
      // Grid point k (1-based) sits at time (k - 1) * dt; the last cell is [(M - 1) dt, t_max]: the cell of t[n]
      // is the largest k <= M with (k - 1) dt <= t[n], i.e. floor(t[n] / dt) + 1, at most M
      vector[N] cell_as_real = fmin(M, floor(t / dt) + 1);
      cell_index = to_int(to_array_1d(cell_as_real));
      cell_index_upper = to_int(to_array_1d(cell_as_real + 1));
      time_into_cell = t - (cell_as_real - 1) * dt;
      cell_fraction = fmin(1, time_into_cell / dt);
      // the subjects with an observed event, in the subjects' order: the first N_event subjects sorted by the
      // distinct keys n + (N + 1) (1 - event[n]), which put every event (key n) before every censored subject
      // (key n + N + 1)
      // event_index = sort_indices_asc(linspaced_vector(N, 1, N) + (N + 1) * (1 - to_vector(event)))[1:N_event];
      // (the keys as a vector of their own: sort_indices_asc() of an unnamed vector expression sorts by a copy
      //  of it that Stan math frees before the sort starts, so that the sort reads freed memory and event_index
      //  can be wrong)
      vector[N] event_first_keys = linspaced_vector(N, 1, N) + (N + 1) * (1 - to_vector(event));
      event_index = sort_indices_asc(event_first_keys)[1:N_event];
    }
    // the subjects, which reduce_sum_static slices into chunks, and the events of subjects 1, ..., i - 1, which
    // are the first events_before[i] entries of event_index (event_index lists the events in the subjects' order)
    array[N] int subject_index = linspaced_int_array(N, 1, N);
    // array[N + 1] int events_before = rep_array(0, N + 1);
    // for (n in 1:N) {
    //   events_before[n + 1] = events_before[n] + event[n];
    // }
    // (the same, without a loop over the subjects)
    array[N + 1] int events_before = append_array({0}, cumulative_sum(event));
    // the subjects' terms of -H(t[n]) gathered by grid cell (cell k = [(k - 1) dt, k dt], lower grid point k),
    // so that their sum over the subjects is a few dot products with vectors of length M: the subjects in cell k,
    // half their summed time_into_cell, and the weights of x_path[k]^2, x_path[k] * x_path[k + 1] and
    // x_path[k + 1]^2 in half their summed time_into_cell * x(t[n])^2, where
    // x(t[n]) = (1 - cell_fraction[n]) * x_path[k] + cell_fraction[n] * x_path[k + 1]
    vector[M] subjects_in_cell = rep_vector(0, M);
    vector[M] half_time_into_cell_summed_by_cell = rep_vector(0, M);
    vector[M] weight_of_x_lower_squared_by_cell = rep_vector(0, M);
    vector[M] weight_of_x_lower_times_x_upper_by_cell = rep_vector(0, M);
    vector[M] weight_of_x_upper_squared_by_cell = rep_vector(0, M);
    // for (n in 1:N) {
    //   int k = cell_index[n];
    //   subjects_in_cell[k] += 1;
    //   half_time_into_cell_summed_by_cell[k] += 0.5 * time_into_cell[n];
    //   weight_of_x_lower_squared_by_cell[k] += 0.5 * time_into_cell[n] * square(1 - cell_fraction[n]);
    //   weight_of_x_lower_times_x_upper_by_cell[k] += time_into_cell[n] * (1 - cell_fraction[n])
    //                                                 * cell_fraction[n];
    //   weight_of_x_upper_squared_by_cell[k] += 0.5 * time_into_cell[n] * square(cell_fraction[n]);
    // }
    // (the same sums, without a loop over the subjects: the M x N matrix of the indicators of the subjects'
    //  cells, 1 where cell_index[n] = k and 0 elsewhere, i.e. 1 - |cell_index[n] - k| floored at 0, times the
    //  vectors of the subjects' terms; a local of this block, so that it is not kept after transformed data)
    {
      matrix[M, N] subject_is_in_cell = fmax(0, 1 - abs(rep_matrix(to_row_vector(cell_index), M)
                                                        - rep_matrix(linspaced_vector(M, 1, M), N)));
      subjects_in_cell = subject_is_in_cell * rep_vector(1, N);
      half_time_into_cell_summed_by_cell = subject_is_in_cell * (0.5 * time_into_cell);
      weight_of_x_lower_squared_by_cell = subject_is_in_cell * (0.5 * time_into_cell
                                                                .* square(1 - cell_fraction));
      weight_of_x_lower_times_x_upper_by_cell = subject_is_in_cell * (time_into_cell .* (1 - cell_fraction)
                                                                      .* cell_fraction);
      weight_of_x_upper_squared_by_cell = subject_is_in_cell * (0.5 * time_into_cell .* square(cell_fraction));
    }
    real half_time_into_cell_summed_over_subjects = sum(half_time_into_cell_summed_by_cell);
    // the events' cells and cell fractions (the path at an event time is interpolated within its cell)
    array[N_event] int event_cell_index = cell_index[event_index];
    array[N_event] int event_cell_index_upper = cell_index_upper[event_index];
    vector[N_event] event_cell_fraction = cell_fraction[event_index];
    vector[N_event] one_minus_event_cell_fraction = 1 - event_cell_fraction;
}


parameters {
    vector[M] w;                             // standard normal Brownian increments, declared first
    real drift_sin_coefficient;              // drift: -(drift_sin_coefficient * sin(x) + drift_constant)
    real drift_constant;
    real<lower=0> hazard_scale;              // h(u) = hazard_scale * (x(u)^2 + x_squared_hazard_offset)
}


transformed parameters {
    vector[M + 1] x_path;                    // latent diffusion at the M + 1 grid points
    // x_path[1] = x_0;
    // for (k in 1:M) {
    //   x_path[k + 1] = x_path[k] - (drift_sin_coefficient * sin(x_path[k]) + drift_constant) * dt
    //                   + sigma_x * sqrt_dt * w[k];
    // }
    // The same recursion, with the terms that do not depend on the path computed once, as one vector:
    // sigma_x * sqrt(dt) * w[k] - drift_constant * dt. Only the sin(x_path[k]) term is sequential over the grid
    // (M steps, the same for any N).
    {
      vector[M] increment_without_sin_term = (sigma_x * sqrt_dt) * w - drift_constant * dt;
      real drift_sin_coefficient_times_dt = drift_sin_coefficient * dt;
      x_path[1] = x_0;
      for (k in 1:M) {
        x_path[k + 1] = x_path[k] - drift_sin_coefficient_times_dt * sin(x_path[k])
                        + increment_without_sin_term[k];
      }
    }
}


model {
    // priors
    // Drift priors: Beskos et al. treat the drift as known,
    // (1.4, 1). One path on [0, 1] carries little information about the drift (with the earlier normal(0, 2)
    // priors the posterior SDs were about 1.5, close to the prior), so the prior sets how far the sampler goes
    // along the drift_sin_coefficient / drift_constant ridge (posterior correlation about -0.7). With
    // normal(0, 2) and the hazard offset, cmdstanr (adapt_delta 0.8, N = 800) still gave 49 divergences, 30 of
    // them from the 5% of draws with drift_sin_coefficient <= -1.5 (drift_constant about 3 there), i.e. the far
    // tail of that ridge, where the Euler recursion is expanding. These priors relax "known drift" to
    // "drift known to within about 1"; with them that run had 0 divergences.
    // The hazard-scale prior (median 1) is unchanged.
    drift_sin_coefficient ~ normal(1.4, 1);
    drift_constant ~ normal(1, 1);
    hazard_scale ~ lognormal(0, 1);
    w ~ std_normal();

    // // likelihood: the hazard and the integrated hazard on the grid, which every subject shares, then the
    // // subjects' terms (reduce_sum_static over the subjects, in chunks of chunk_size)
    // {
    //   vector[M + 1] hazard_grid = hazard_scale * (square(x_path) + x_squared_hazard_offset);
    //   vector[M + 1] cumulative_hazard_grid;
    //   cumulative_hazard_grid[1] = 0;
    //   cumulative_hazard_grid[2:(M + 1)] = cumulative_sum(0.5 * dt * (hazard_grid[1:M]
    //                                                                  + hazard_grid[2:(M + 1)]));
    //   target += reduce_sum_static(partial_sum_subjects_lupmf, subject_index, chunk_size,
    //                               cell_index, cell_index_upper, time_into_cell, cell_fraction,
    //                               event_index, events_before, x_squared_hazard_offset,
    //                               x_path, hazard_grid, cumulative_hazard_grid, hazard_scale);
    // }
    // likelihood: the hazard and the integrated hazard on the grid, which every subject shares; log h(t) at the
    // observed event times, N_event * log(hazard_scale) and the subjects' terms log(x(t)^2 + offset)
    // (reduce_sum_static over the subjects, in chunks of chunk_size); then -H(t) summed over the subjects by grid
    // cell, as in latent_diffusion_survival.stan
    {
      vector[M + 1] hazard_grid = hazard_scale * (square(x_path) + x_squared_hazard_offset);
      vector[M + 1] cumulative_hazard_grid;
      cumulative_hazard_grid[1] = 0;
      cumulative_hazard_grid[2:(M + 1)] = cumulative_sum(0.5 * dt * (hazard_grid[1:M] + hazard_grid[2:(M + 1)]));
      target += N_event * log(hazard_scale);
      target += reduce_sum_static(partial_sum_subjects_lupmf, subject_index, chunk_size,
                                  events_before, event_cell_index, event_cell_index_upper,
                                  one_minus_event_cell_fraction, event_cell_fraction, x_squared_hazard_offset,
                                  x_path);
      // - H(t) for every subject, events and censored alike, summed by grid cell: the subjects' integrated
      // hazards up to their cell's lower grid point, their trapezoids' lower sides (hazard_grid[k]) and upper
      // sides (the hazard at t[n], hazard_scale * (x(t[n])^2 + x_squared_hazard_offset))
      target += -(dot_product(subjects_in_cell, cumulative_hazard_grid[1:M])
                  + dot_product(half_time_into_cell_summed_by_cell, hazard_grid[1:M])
                  + hazard_scale * (dot_product(weight_of_x_lower_squared_by_cell, square(x_path[1:M]))
                                    + dot_product(weight_of_x_lower_times_x_upper_by_cell,
                                                  x_path[1:M] .* x_path[2:(M + 1)])
                                    + dot_product(weight_of_x_upper_squared_by_cell, square(x_path[2:(M + 1)]))
                                    + x_squared_hazard_offset * half_time_into_cell_summed_over_subjects));
    }
}


generated quantities {
    vector[M + 1] hazard_path = hazard_scale * (square(x_path) + x_squared_hazard_offset);
    vector[M + 1] survival_path;             // S(u) = exp(-H(u)) at the grid points
    // survival_path[1] = 1;
    // for (k in 1:M) {
    //   survival_path[k + 1] = survival_path[k] * exp(-0.5 * dt * (hazard_path[k] + hazard_path[k + 1]));
    // }
    // (the same values up to rounding, without a loop: exp(-H) with H the cumulative sum of the trapezoids)
    survival_path = exp(-append_row(0, cumulative_sum(0.5 * dt * (hazard_path[1:M] + hazard_path[2:(M + 1)]))));
}

// latent_diffusion_survival_chunked_no_loops_over_N_hand_written_BayesMVP_AVX.stan
// Hand-written BayesMVP AVX version of latent_diffusion_survival_chunked_no_loops_over_N.stan:
// every elementwise call on a vector written as BayesMVP's fast_ function (declared in the functions block as
// NicoStan's writer declares them), every scalar call on Stan math; one text for both AVX2 and AVX-512
// (compiled with each backend's flags and user header).
//
// The tape-chunked model latent_diffusion_survival_chunked.stan (below) without a loop over the subjects: its
// log density and its chunks are unchanged (each chunk's terms were already whole-vector operations over the
// chunk's events, and -H(t) was already gathered by grid cell into dot products of length M), and its loops over
// the subjects in transformed data are whole-vector operations: each subject's cell is floor(t[n] / dt) + 1
// (at most M; the same cells as the loop of latent_diffusion_survival.stan on every data case), the events are
// the first N_event subjects in the order of the distinct keys n + (N + 1) (1 - event[n]) (sort_indices_asc), the
// events before each subject are a cumulative sum, and the sums over the subjects of each grid cell are the
// product of the M x N matrix of the indicators of the subjects' cells with the vectors of the subjects' terms.
// In generated quantities, the survival path is exp(-H) at the grid points, with H the cumulative sum of the
// trapezoids (the same values up to rounding).
// The only loop left is the Euler-Maruyama recursion of the path x over the M grid points (transformed
// parameters): its step is not linear in x (sin(x)), so it cannot be written as a linear system or a cumulative
// sum, and its length is M (the same for every N), not the subjects.
//
// latent_diffusion_survival_chunked.stan
// Tape-chunked version of latent_diffusion_survival.stan: the same log density, with the subjects' likelihood
// terms (log h(t) at each observed event time, and -H(t) for every subject) summed over the subjects by
// reduce_sum_static, in chunks of chunk_size subjects (data), so that each chunk's autodiff tape is built,
// differentiated and released before the next one (the tape-chunking paper's chunking; N_chunks from
// NicoStan::fn_compute_initial_N_chunks()). The latent path x_path and the hazard and integrated hazard on the
// grid, which every subject shares, are computed once, outside reduce_sum_static, and passed to every chunk.
// Each chunk computes its subjects' terms with the whole-vector operations of latent_diffusion_survival.stan
// (event_index lists the events in the subjects' order, so a chunk's events are contiguous in it).
// The chunking data are NicoStan's for Stan models: N (the subjects, the units of the chunks) and chunk_size,
// which NicoStan sets to ceiling(N / N_chunks) in each phase (num_chunks_burnin, num_chunks_sampling).
//
// Inside the chunks (everything whose cost grows with the subjects): the path interpolated at the chunk's
// event times and the log hazards there, log(x(t)^2 + x_squared_hazard_offset), one vectorised operation over
// the chunk's events. Outside the chunks, only terms whose size does not grow with N: the path recursion over the
// M + 1 grid points (sequential in the grid, the same for any N), the hazard and integrated hazard on the grid,
// N_event * log(hazard_scale), and -H(t) summed over all subjects, which is gathered by grid cell into dot
// products of length M with data computed in transformed data (as in latent_diffusion_survival.stan). x_path,
// of length M + 1, is the only autodiff argument passed to the chunks.
//
// The model, as in latent_diffusion_survival.stan:
//
// Latent diffusion survival model (Roberts and Sangalli, 2010), in the form used by
// Beskos, Kalogeropoulos and Pazos (2013, Sections 5 and 6.3). All subjects share one
// hazard trajectory h(u) = hazard_scale * (x(u)^2 + x_squared_hazard_offset), driven by the latent diffusion
//     dX_u = -(drift_sin_coefficient * sin(X_u) + drift_constant) du + sigma_x dB_u,  X_0 = x_0,
// on the observation window [0, t_max]. Beskos et al. use hazard_scale = 1, drift
// coefficients (1.4, 1), sigma_x = 1 (unit diffusion coefficient), x_0 = 2 and t_max = 1,
// and treat these as known. Here the drift coefficients and the hazard scale are estimated
// jointly with the path; sigma_x and x_0 are fixed data.
//
// Hazard offset (not in Beskos et al.): Beskos et al. use
// h(x) = x^2 exactly (x_squared_hazard_offset = 0). Then log h at an event time is 2 log|x(t)|, which is -Inf
// at x(t) = 0, and h(x) = h(-x). The drift pulls X towards its stable point -0.795 (the drift-only path from
// x_0 = 2 reaches 0 at t = 1.07, and about 60% of simulated paths cross 0 before t = 1). Once the path gets
// near zero, the posterior splits into sign patterns of x at the event times,
// separated by those -Inf walls. Hamiltonian trajectories cannot cross the walls and diverge near them:
// cmdstanr at adapt_delta 0.9 gave 120 divergences and x_path R-hat 1.11 with the old model, and still 43
// divergences and x_path R-hat 1.53 with every parameter fixed at the Beskos et al. values. A small offset
// (default 0.01 in the simulator, i.e. the hazard never falls below 1% of hazard_scale) makes log h finite
// and smooth, so the sign patterns are connected and the sampler mixes over them. The hazard shape is x^2
// wherever |x| is not tiny. Setting the offset to 0 gives the exact Beskos et al. form (and its divergences).
//
// Discretisation: Euler-Maruyama on M equal steps of length dt = t_max / M, non-centred.
// The nuisance block w holds the M standard normal Brownian increments, and
//     x[k + 1] = x[k] + drift(x[k]) * dt + sigma_x * sqrt(dt) * w[k].
// The path is taken as linear between grid points. The hazard at an event time uses the
// linearly interpolated path value (not a snap to the nearest grid point). The integrated
// hazard is the trapezoid rule over the whole grid cells before t[n], plus a trapezoid over
// the partial cell from its lower grid point to t[n]. Right-censored times contribute only
// -H(t[n]); administrative censoring at t_max is the usual case.

functions {
    real bmvp_simd_lanes();
    vector nico_exp(vector x);
    vector nico_log(vector x);
    real nico_normal_lpdf(vector y, real mu, real sigma);
    // real partial_sum_subjects_lpmf(array[] int subject_slice, int start, int end,
    //                                array[] int cell_index, array[] int cell_index_upper,
    //                                vector time_into_cell, vector cell_fraction,
    //                                array[] int event_index, array[] int events_before,
    //                                real x_squared_hazard_offset, vector x_path, vector hazard_grid,
    //                                vector cumulative_hazard_grid, real hazard_scale) {
    //     int n_subjects = end - start + 1;
    //     real lp = 0;
    //     // the chunk's subjects: the path at t[n] (linearly interpolated) and the hazard there
    //     vector[n_subjects] x_at_t = (1 - cell_fraction[start:end]) .* x_path[cell_index[start:end]]
    //                                 + cell_fraction[start:end] .* x_path[cell_index_upper[start:end]];
    //     vector[n_subjects] hazard_at_t = hazard_scale * (square(x_at_t) + x_squared_hazard_offset);
    //     // the chunk's events: event_index[e1:e2] (the events of subjects start to end)
    //     int e1 = events_before[start] + 1;
    //     int e2 = events_before[end + 1];
    //     // log h(t) at the chunk's observed event times; finite at x(t) = 0 whenever
    //     // x_squared_hazard_offset > 0.
    //     if (e2 >= e1) {
    //       array[e2 - e1 + 1] int event_position_in_chunk;
    //       for (k in 1:(e2 - e1 + 1)) {
    //         event_position_in_chunk[k] = event_index[e1 + k - 1] - start + 1;
    //       }
    //       lp += (e2 - e1 + 1) * log(hazard_scale)
    //             + sum(log(square(x_at_t[event_position_in_chunk]) + x_squared_hazard_offset));
    //     }
    //     // - H(t) for every subject of the chunk, events and censored alike.
    //     lp += -sum(cumulative_hazard_grid[cell_index[start:end]]
    //                + 0.5 * time_into_cell[start:end] .* (hazard_grid[cell_index[start:end]] + hazard_at_t));
    //     return lp;
    // }
    // the chunk's events (event_index[e1:e2], the events of subjects start to end): the path at their times,
    // linearly interpolated, and log(x(t)^2 + x_squared_hazard_offset), i.e. log h(t) minus log(hazard_scale);
    // finite at x(t) = 0 whenever x_squared_hazard_offset > 0
    real partial_sum_subjects_lpmf(array[] int subject_slice, int start, int end,
                                   data array[] int events_before, data array[] int event_cell_index,
                                   data array[] int event_cell_index_upper,
                                   data vector one_minus_event_cell_fraction, data vector event_cell_fraction,
                                   data real x_squared_hazard_offset, vector x_path) {
        real lp = 0;
        int e1 = events_before[start] + 1;
        int e2 = events_before[end + 1];
        if (e2 >= e1) {
          vector[e2 - e1 + 1] x_at_event_time = one_minus_event_cell_fraction[e1:e2]
                                                .* x_path[event_cell_index[e1:e2]]
                                                + event_cell_fraction[e1:e2]
                                                  .* x_path[event_cell_index_upper[e1:e2]];
          lp += sum(nico_log(square(x_at_event_time) + x_squared_hazard_offset));
        }
        return lp;
    }
}


data {
    int<lower=1> N;                          // number of subjects
    int<lower=2> M;                          // number of Euler-Maruyama steps on [0, t_max]
    real<lower=0> t_max;                     // end of the observation window
    real x_0;                                // fixed initial value of the latent diffusion
    real<lower=0> sigma_x;                   // fixed diffusion coefficient (1 = unit diffusion)
    real<lower=0> x_squared_hazard_offset;   // h(u) = hazard_scale * (x(u)^2 + offset);
                                             // 0 = exact Beskos et al. form
    vector<lower=0, upper=t_max>[N] t;       // event or censoring time
    array[N] int<lower=0, upper=1> event;    // 1 = event observed, 0 = right censored at t
    int<lower=1> chunk_size;                 // subjects per chunk (reduce_sum_static)
}


transformed data {
    real dt = t_max / M;
    real sqrt_dt = sqrt(dt);
    int N_event = sum(event);
    array[N_event] int event_index;          // subjects with an observed event
    array[N] int cell_index;                 // lower grid point of the cell containing t[n]
    array[N] int cell_index_upper;           // upper grid point of that cell
    vector[N] time_into_cell;                // t[n] minus the time of that lower grid point
    vector[N] cell_fraction;                 // time_into_cell / dt, in [0, 1]
    // {
    //   int position = 1;
    //   for (n in 1:N) {
    //     int cell = 1;
    //     if (t[n] <= 0) reject("Event and censoring times must be strictly positive.");
    //     // Grid point k (1-based) sits at time (k - 1) * dt; the last cell is [(M - 1) dt, t_max].
    //     while (cell < M && t[n] >= cell * dt) cell += 1;
    //     cell_index[n] = cell;
    //     cell_index_upper[n] = cell + 1;
    //     time_into_cell[n] = t[n] - (cell - 1) * dt;
    //     cell_fraction[n] = fmin(1, time_into_cell[n] / dt);
    //     if (event[n] == 1) {
    //       event_index[position] = n;
    //       position += 1;
    //     }
    //   }
    // }
    // (the same, without a loop over the subjects)
    if (min(t) <= 0) reject("Event and censoring times must be strictly positive.");
    {
      // Grid point k (1-based) sits at time (k - 1) * dt; the last cell is [(M - 1) dt, t_max]: the cell of t[n]
      // is the largest k <= M with (k - 1) dt <= t[n], i.e. floor(t[n] / dt) + 1, at most M
      vector[N] cell_as_real = fmin(M, floor(t / dt) + 1);
      cell_index = to_int(to_array_1d(cell_as_real));
      cell_index_upper = to_int(to_array_1d(cell_as_real + 1));
      time_into_cell = t - (cell_as_real - 1) * dt;
      cell_fraction = fmin(1, time_into_cell / dt);
      // the subjects with an observed event, in the subjects' order: the first N_event subjects sorted by the
      // distinct keys n + (N + 1) (1 - event[n]), which put every event (key n) before every censored subject
      // (key n + N + 1)
      // event_index = sort_indices_asc(linspaced_vector(N, 1, N) + (N + 1) * (1 - to_vector(event)))[1:N_event];
      // (the keys as a vector of their own: sort_indices_asc() of an unnamed vector expression sorts by a copy
      //  of it that Stan math frees before the sort starts, so that the sort reads freed memory and event_index
      //  can be wrong)
      vector[N] event_first_keys = linspaced_vector(N, 1, N) + (N + 1) * (1 - to_vector(event));
      event_index = sort_indices_asc(event_first_keys)[1:N_event];
    }
    // the subjects, which reduce_sum_static slices into chunks, and the events of subjects 1, ..., i - 1, which
    // are the first events_before[i] entries of event_index (event_index lists the events in the subjects' order)
    array[N] int subject_index = linspaced_int_array(N, 1, N);
    // array[N + 1] int events_before = rep_array(0, N + 1);
    // for (n in 1:N) {
    //   events_before[n + 1] = events_before[n] + event[n];
    // }
    // (the same, without a loop over the subjects)
    array[N + 1] int events_before = append_array({0}, cumulative_sum(event));
    // the subjects' terms of -H(t[n]) gathered by grid cell (cell k = [(k - 1) dt, k dt], lower grid point k),
    // so that their sum over the subjects is a few dot products with vectors of length M: the subjects in cell k,
    // half their summed time_into_cell, and the weights of x_path[k]^2, x_path[k] * x_path[k + 1] and
    // x_path[k + 1]^2 in half their summed time_into_cell * x(t[n])^2, where
    // x(t[n]) = (1 - cell_fraction[n]) * x_path[k] + cell_fraction[n] * x_path[k + 1]
    vector[M] subjects_in_cell = rep_vector(0, M);
    vector[M] half_time_into_cell_summed_by_cell = rep_vector(0, M);
    vector[M] weight_of_x_lower_squared_by_cell = rep_vector(0, M);
    vector[M] weight_of_x_lower_times_x_upper_by_cell = rep_vector(0, M);
    vector[M] weight_of_x_upper_squared_by_cell = rep_vector(0, M);
    // for (n in 1:N) {
    //   int k = cell_index[n];
    //   subjects_in_cell[k] += 1;
    //   half_time_into_cell_summed_by_cell[k] += 0.5 * time_into_cell[n];
    //   weight_of_x_lower_squared_by_cell[k] += 0.5 * time_into_cell[n] * square(1 - cell_fraction[n]);
    //   weight_of_x_lower_times_x_upper_by_cell[k] += time_into_cell[n] * (1 - cell_fraction[n])
    //                                                 * cell_fraction[n];
    //   weight_of_x_upper_squared_by_cell[k] += 0.5 * time_into_cell[n] * square(cell_fraction[n]);
    // }
    // (the same sums, without a loop over the subjects: the M x N matrix of the indicators of the subjects'
    //  cells, 1 where cell_index[n] = k and 0 elsewhere, i.e. 1 - |cell_index[n] - k| floored at 0, times the
    //  vectors of the subjects' terms; a local of this block, so that it is not kept after transformed data)
    {
      matrix[M, N] subject_is_in_cell = fmax(0, 1 - abs(rep_matrix(to_row_vector(cell_index), M)
                                                        - rep_matrix(linspaced_vector(M, 1, M), N)));
      subjects_in_cell = subject_is_in_cell * rep_vector(1, N);
      half_time_into_cell_summed_by_cell = subject_is_in_cell * (0.5 * time_into_cell);
      weight_of_x_lower_squared_by_cell = subject_is_in_cell * (0.5 * time_into_cell
                                                                .* square(1 - cell_fraction));
      weight_of_x_lower_times_x_upper_by_cell = subject_is_in_cell * (time_into_cell .* (1 - cell_fraction)
                                                                      .* cell_fraction);
      weight_of_x_upper_squared_by_cell = subject_is_in_cell * (0.5 * time_into_cell
                                                                .* square(cell_fraction));
    }
    real half_time_into_cell_summed_over_subjects = sum(half_time_into_cell_summed_by_cell);
    // the events' cells and cell fractions (the path at an event time is interpolated within its cell)
    array[N_event] int event_cell_index = cell_index[event_index];
    array[N_event] int event_cell_index_upper = cell_index_upper[event_index];
    vector[N_event] event_cell_fraction = cell_fraction[event_index];
    vector[N_event] one_minus_event_cell_fraction = 1 - event_cell_fraction;
}


parameters {
    vector[M] w;                             // standard normal Brownian increments, declared first
    real drift_sin_coefficient;              // drift: -(drift_sin_coefficient * sin(x) + drift_constant)
    real drift_constant;
    real<lower=0> hazard_scale;              // h(u) = hazard_scale * (x(u)^2 + x_squared_hazard_offset)
}


transformed parameters {
    vector[M + 1] x_path;                    // latent diffusion at the M + 1 grid points
    // x_path[1] = x_0;
    // for (k in 1:M) {
    //   x_path[k + 1] = x_path[k] - (drift_sin_coefficient * sin(x_path[k]) + drift_constant) * dt
    //                   + sigma_x * sqrt_dt * w[k];
    // }
    // The same recursion, with the terms that do not depend on the path computed once, as one vector:
    // sigma_x * sqrt(dt) * w[k] - drift_constant * dt. Only the sin(x_path[k]) term is sequential over the grid
    // (M steps, the same for any N).
    {
      vector[M] increment_without_sin_term = (sigma_x * sqrt_dt) * w - drift_constant * dt;
      real drift_sin_coefficient_times_dt = drift_sin_coefficient * dt;
      x_path[1] = x_0;
      for (k in 1:M) {
        x_path[k + 1] = x_path[k] - drift_sin_coefficient_times_dt * sin(x_path[k])
                        + increment_without_sin_term[k];
      }
    }
}


model {
    // priors
    // Drift priors: Beskos et al. treat the drift as known,
    // (1.4, 1). One path on [0, 1] carries little information about the drift (with the earlier normal(0, 2)
    // priors the posterior SDs were about 1.5, close to the prior), so the prior sets how far the sampler goes
    // along the drift_sin_coefficient / drift_constant ridge (posterior correlation about -0.7). With
    // normal(0, 2) and the hazard offset, cmdstanr (adapt_delta 0.8, N = 800) still gave 49 divergences, 30 of
    // them from the 5% of draws with drift_sin_coefficient <= -1.5 (drift_constant about 3 there), i.e. the far
    // tail of that ridge, where the Euler recursion is expanding. These priors relax "known drift" to
    // "drift known to within about 1"; with them that run had 0 divergences.
    // The hazard-scale prior (median 1) is unchanged.
    drift_sin_coefficient ~ normal(1.4, 1);
    drift_constant ~ normal(1, 1);
    hazard_scale ~ lognormal(0, 1);
    w ~ nico_normal(0, 1);

    // // likelihood: the hazard and the integrated hazard on the grid, which every subject shares, then the
    // // subjects' terms (reduce_sum_static over the subjects, in chunks of chunk_size)
    // {
    //   vector[M + 1] hazard_grid = hazard_scale * (square(x_path) + x_squared_hazard_offset);
    //   vector[M + 1] cumulative_hazard_grid;
    //   cumulative_hazard_grid[1] = 0;
    //   cumulative_hazard_grid[2:(M + 1)] = cumulative_sum(0.5 * dt * (hazard_grid[1:M]
    //                                                                  + hazard_grid[2:(M + 1)]));
    //   target += reduce_sum_static(partial_sum_subjects_lupmf, subject_index, chunk_size,
    //                               cell_index, cell_index_upper, time_into_cell, cell_fraction,
    //                               event_index, events_before, x_squared_hazard_offset,
    //                               x_path, hazard_grid, cumulative_hazard_grid, hazard_scale);
    // }
    // likelihood: the hazard and the integrated hazard on the grid, which every subject shares; log h(t) at the
    // observed event times, N_event * log(hazard_scale) and the subjects' terms log(x(t)^2 + offset)
    // (reduce_sum_static over the subjects, in chunks of chunk_size); then -H(t) summed over the subjects by grid
    // cell, as in latent_diffusion_survival.stan
    {
      vector[M + 1] hazard_grid = hazard_scale * (square(x_path) + x_squared_hazard_offset);
      vector[M + 1] cumulative_hazard_grid;
      cumulative_hazard_grid[1] = 0;
      cumulative_hazard_grid[2:(M + 1)] = cumulative_sum(0.5 * dt * (hazard_grid[1:M] + hazard_grid[2:(M + 1)]));
      target += N_event * log(hazard_scale);
      target += reduce_sum_static(partial_sum_subjects_lupmf, subject_index, chunk_size,
                                  events_before, event_cell_index, event_cell_index_upper,
                                  one_minus_event_cell_fraction, event_cell_fraction, x_squared_hazard_offset,
                                  x_path);
      // - H(t) for every subject, events and censored alike, summed by grid cell: the subjects' integrated
      // hazards up to their cell's lower grid point, their trapezoids' lower sides (hazard_grid[k]) and upper
      // sides (the hazard at t[n], hazard_scale * (x(t[n])^2 + x_squared_hazard_offset))
      target += -(dot_product(subjects_in_cell, cumulative_hazard_grid[1:M])
                  + dot_product(half_time_into_cell_summed_by_cell, hazard_grid[1:M])
                  + hazard_scale * (dot_product(weight_of_x_lower_squared_by_cell, square(x_path[1:M]))
                                    + dot_product(weight_of_x_lower_times_x_upper_by_cell,
                                                  x_path[1:M] .* x_path[2:(M + 1)])
                                    + dot_product(weight_of_x_upper_squared_by_cell,
                                                  square(x_path[2:(M + 1)]))
                                    + x_squared_hazard_offset * half_time_into_cell_summed_over_subjects));
    }
}


generated quantities {
    real simd_lanes = bmvp_simd_lanes();
    vector[M + 1] hazard_path = hazard_scale * (square(x_path) + x_squared_hazard_offset);
    vector[M + 1] survival_path;             // S(u) = exp(-H(u)) at the grid points
    // survival_path[1] = 1;
    // for (k in 1:M) {
    //   survival_path[k + 1] = survival_path[k] * exp(-0.5 * dt * (hazard_path[k] + hazard_path[k + 1]));
    // }
    // (the same values up to rounding, without a loop: exp(-H) with H the cumulative sum of the trapezoids)
    survival_path = nico_exp(-append_row(0, cumulative_sum(0.5 * dt * (hazard_path[1:M]
                                                                       + hazard_path[2:(M + 1)]))));
}

benchmark_models/joint_longitudinal_survival_unchunked_no_loops_over_N_with_Stan_fused_functions.stan (161 lines)
// joint_longitudinal_survival_unchunked_no_loops_over_N_with_Stan_fused_functions.stan
// Unchunked Stan::math version of the joint longitudinal-survival model of the chunking paper's layout timings
// (joint_longitudinal_survival_chunked_no_loops_over_N_v5_automatic_reduce_sum_chunked, from its source
// joint_longitudinal_survival_chunked_no_loops_over_N_v5): the same log density as that source at N_chunks = 1,
// and as joint_longitudinal_survival.stan, as one pass over all N_subj subjects, without reduce_sum_static. The
// same data (N and chunk_size, when they are in the data, are not read; subj_long need not be sorted, as in
// joint_longitudinal_survival.stan) and the same unconstrained parameters, in the same order and with the same
// names, as joint_longitudinal_survival.stan: b_raw is its 2 x N_subj matrix, whose unconstrained coordinates
// are in the same order as those of the source's array[N_subj] row_vector[2] b_raw (subject i's 2 values, then
// subject i + 1's), which exists only so that reduce_sum_static can slice the subjects.
// Stan's fused functions:
//   - the longitudinal likelihood is Stan's fused normal GLM, Y_long ~ normal_id_glm(X_long, the random effects
//     b0[subj] + b1[subj] time as the intercept of each observation, beta_long, sigma_long), as in the source;
//   - the cumulative hazards, -lambda sum over the subjects and their Q quadrature points of the weight
//     quad_weights[q] T_surv[i] / 2 times exp(eta), are Stan's fused Poisson-log GLM with every outcome 0:
//     poisson_log_glm_lpmf(0 | theta) = -exp(theta) (lgamma(0 + 1) = 0), with
//     theta = log(lambda) + log(weight) + eta, the covariates X_long_quad_stacked and the coefficients
//     alpha_assoc beta_long, i.e. -sum(lambda weight exp(eta)), the same term; the log of the weights is data,
//     made once in transformed data (the quadrature weights and the survival times must hence be positive);
//   - the events' log hazards, as in the source: the data summed over the events (X_long_event summed, the
//     number of events, the event times) times the parameters, a few dot products.
// No loop over N anywhere (the loops left in transformed data are over the K_long covariates and the Q
// quadrature points).


data {
  int<lower=1> N_long;              // number of longitudinal observations
  int<lower=1> N_subj;              // number of subjects
  int<lower=1> K_long;              // number of longitudinal covariates
  matrix[N_long, K_long] X_long;    // longitudinal covariate matrix
  vector[N_long] Y_long;            // longitudinal outcomes
  array[N_long] int<lower=1,upper=N_subj> subj_long; // subject IDs for longitudinal data
  vector[N_long] time_long;         // measurement times

  int<lower=1> K_surv;              // number of survival covariates
  matrix[N_subj, K_surv] X_surv;    // survival covariate matrix
  vector<lower=0>[N_subj] T_surv;   // survival times
  array[N_subj] int<lower=0,upper=1> event; // event indicators

  int<lower=1> Q;                   // number of quadrature points
  vector[Q] quad_points;            // quadrature points
  vector[Q] quad_weights;           // quadrature weights
  matrix[N_subj, K_long] X_long_event; // longitudinal fixed-effect design at T_surv
  array[N_subj] matrix[Q, K_long] X_long_quad; // same design at each subject's quadrature times
}


transformed data {
  // the log of the quadrature weights below needs positive weights and survival times
  if (min(quad_weights) <= 0 || min(T_surv) <= 0) {
    reject("the quadrature weights and the survival times must be positive (the cumulative hazards are a ",
           "Poisson-log GLM with the log of the weights as data)");
  }
  // every subject's Q quadrature points, stacked (subject i in rows (i - 1) * Q + 1 to i * Q), as in the source:
  // column k of X_long_quad_stacked is covariate k at every subject's Q points, i.e. the Q x N_subj matrix of
  // covariate k, stacked column by column (to_vector); a loop over the covariates and the quadrature points only
  int N_quad = N_subj * Q;
  matrix[N_quad, K_long] X_long_quad_stacked;
  vector[Q] quad_time_fraction = (quad_points + 1) / 2;
  for (k in 1:K_long) {
    matrix[Q, N_subj] X_long_quad_of_covariate_k;
    for (q in 1:Q) {
      X_long_quad_of_covariate_k[q] = to_row_vector(X_long_quad[:, q, k]);
    }
    X_long_quad_stacked[:, k] = to_vector(X_long_quad_of_covariate_k);
  }
  // the log of the quadrature weight of each stacked point times half its subject's survival time (the Q x N_subj
  // outer product of quad_weights with T_surv / 2, stacked column by column), and the outcomes 0 of the GLM
  vector[N_quad] log_quad_weight_times_half_T = log(to_vector(quad_weights * (T_surv / 2)'));
  array[N_quad] int zeros_of_quad = rep_array(0, N_quad);
  // the event data summed over the subjects with an event, as in the source
  vector[N_subj] event_indicator = to_vector(event);
  int N_events = sum(event);
  vector[N_subj] event_time = event_indicator .* T_surv;
  vector[K_long] X_long_event_summed_over_events = X_long_event' * event_indicator;
  // (the subjects with an event, in increasing order, for the generated quantities: the first N_events indices
  //  of event sorted in decreasing order, then sorted)
  array[N_events] int event_index = sort_asc(sort_indices_desc(event)[1:N_events]);
}


parameters {
  matrix[2, N_subj] b_raw;          // standard normal nuisance block, declared first
  // Longitudinal submodel parameters
  vector[K_long] beta_long;         // fixed effects
  real<lower=0> sigma_long;         // residual error SD
  real<lower=0> sigma_b0;           // random intercept SD
  real<lower=0> sigma_b1;           // random slope SD
  real<lower=-1,upper=1> rho_b;     // correlation between random effects

  // Survival submodel parameters
  vector[K_surv] beta_surv;         // survival covariates effects
  real<lower=0> lambda;             // baseline hazard rate
  real alpha_assoc;                 // association parameter
}


model {
  // Priors
  beta_long ~ normal(0, 2);
  beta_surv ~ normal(0, 2);
  sigma_long ~ exponential(1);
  sigma_b0 ~ exponential(1);
  sigma_b1 ~ exponential(1);
  rho_b ~ uniform(-1, 1);
  // Baseline hazard prior on the example's time scale (median 0.2 per time unit).
  // lambda ~ lognormal(log(0.2), 1);
  lambda ~ lognormal(log(0.1), 1.5);
  alpha_assoc ~ normal(0, 1);

  // Equivalent non-centred form of the original correlated Gaussian effects.
  to_vector(b_raw) ~ std_normal();

  {
    vector[N_subj] b0 = sigma_b0 * b_raw[1]';
    vector[N_subj] b1 = sigma_b1 * (rho_b * b_raw[1]' + sqrt(1 - square(rho_b)) * b_raw[2]');

    // Longitudinal likelihood (Stan's fused normal GLM, the random effects as each observation's intercept)
    Y_long ~ normal_id_glm(X_long, b0[subj_long] + b1[subj_long] .* time_long, beta_long, sigma_long);

    // Survival likelihood: each subject's log hazard at time u is
    // log(lambda) + subject_part + X_long(u) alpha_assoc beta_long + u subject_slope
    vector[N_subj] subject_part = X_surv * beta_surv + alpha_assoc * b0;
    vector[N_subj] subject_slope = alpha_assoc * b1;
    // the events' log hazards (the data summed over the events times the parameters)
    target += N_events * log(lambda) + dot_product(X_long_event_summed_over_events, alpha_assoc * beta_long)
              + dot_product(event_indicator, subject_part) + dot_product(event_time, subject_slope);
    // minus the cumulative hazards by quadrature, all subjects at once (Stan's fused Poisson-log GLM; see the
    // header; subject i's Q points are column i of the Q x N_subj matrix, stacked)
    target += poisson_log_glm_lupmf(zeros_of_quad | X_long_quad_stacked,
                                    log(lambda) + log_quad_weight_times_half_T
                                    + to_vector(rep_matrix(subject_part', Q)
                                                + quad_time_fraction * (T_surv .* subject_slope)'),
                                    alpha_assoc * beta_long);
  }
}


generated quantities {
  vector[N_subj] b0 = sigma_b0 * b_raw[1]';
  vector[N_subj] b1 = sigma_b1 * (rho_b * b_raw[1]' + sqrt(1 - square(rho_b)) * b_raw[2]');
  vector[N_long] eta_long;          // longitudinal linear predictor
  vector[N_subj] hazard_subj;       // subject-specific hazards
  vector[N_long] y_pred;            // posterior predictions
  vector[N_subj] log_lik_surv;      // survival log-likelihood

  // (on the whole vectors, as in the source)
  eta_long = X_long * beta_long + b0[subj_long] + b1[subj_long] .* time_long;
  hazard_subj = lambda * exp(X_surv * beta_surv + alpha_assoc * (X_long_event * beta_long + b0 + b1 .* T_surv));
  y_pred = to_vector(normal_rng(eta_long, sigma_long));
  {
    vector[N_quad] hazard_quad
          = lambda * exp(to_vector(rep_matrix((X_surv * beta_surv)', Q))
                         + alpha_assoc * (X_long_quad_stacked * beta_long
                                          + to_vector(rep_matrix(b0', Q))
                                          + to_vector(quad_time_fraction * (T_surv .* b1)')));
    vector[N_subj] cum_hazard = (to_matrix(hazard_quad, Q, N_subj)' * quad_weights) .* T_surv / 2;
    log_lik_surv = -cum_hazard;
    log_lik_surv[event_index] = log(hazard_subj[event_index]) - cum_hazard[event_index];
  }
}

// joint_longitudinal_survival_chunked_no_loops_over_N.stan
// joint_longitudinal_survival_chunked.stan without any loop over the subjects or the observations: the same log
// density, with every calculation whose size grows with the subjects vectorised and inside the chunks of
// reduce_sum_static. More specifically:
//   - b_raw is declared as array[N_subj] row_vector[2] (subject i's b_raw[i, 1] and b_raw[i, 2]; the same
//     unconstrained parameters, in the same order, as matrix[2, N_subj]), as u_raw in
//     LC_MVP_bin_PartialLog_v5_reduce_sum_static.stan, so that the sliced argument of reduce_sum_static is the
//     parameter itself: one single name holding everything per subject, nothing built on the main tape, in place
//     of b_raw_by_subject and the loop over the subjects which filled it (the sliced argument is never an
//     expression: Stan math's reduce_sum holds the result of an expression by value and copies all of it at every
//     split of the subjects into chunks, i.e. O(N x N_chunks));
//   - in the chunks, the log hazards at the quadrature points are a Q x n_subjects matrix (subject i's Q points
//     in column i): the subject-level part repeated over the Q rows (rep_matrix), the longitudinal fixed effects
//     at the points, and the outer product of (quad_points + 1) / 2 with each subject's slope times T_surv, in
//     place of the loop over the chunk's quadrature points which gave each point its subject;
//   - the position in the chunk of each observation's subject is subj_long - (start - 1), as one vector
//     operation (to_int of a real vector), in place of the loop over the chunk's observations;
//   - transformed data: the counts of observations before each subject (observations_before) from one sort of
//     subj_long together with the points 0.5, 1.5, ..., N_subj + 0.5, and the stacked quadrature data as outer
//     products (loops over the Q quadrature points and the K_long covariates only), in place of the loops over
//     the observations and the subjects;
//   - generated quantities: the same quantities with whole-vector operations, in place of the loops over the
//     observations, the subjects and their quadrature points.
// The description of joint_longitudinal_survival_chunked.stan follows.
//
// joint_longitudinal_survival_chunked.stan
// Tape-chunked version of joint_longitudinal_survival.stan: the same log density, with both
// likelihoods summed over the subjects by reduce_sum_static, in chunks of chunk_size subjects (data), so that
// each chunk's autodiff tape is built, differentiated and released before the next one (the
// chunking paper's chunking;
// N_chunks from NicoStan::fn_compute_initial_N_chunks()). Each chunk computes its subjects' terms with the
// whole-vector operations of joint_longitudinal_survival.stan (its subjects' observations and quadrature points
// are contiguous); eta_long and hazard_subj, transformed parameters there, are reported as generated quantities
// (the same values).
// The chunking data are NicoStan's for Stan models: N (the subjects, the units of the chunks; it must equal
// N_subj) and chunk_size, which NicoStan sets to ceiling(N / N_chunks) in each phase (num_chunks_burnin,
// num_chunks_sampling).
//
// Inside the chunks (everything whose cost grows with the subjects): the standard normal prior of the chunk's
// subjects' b_raw; the chunk's random effects b0 and b1, from b_raw and sigma_b0, sigma_b1 and rho_b; the
// longitudinal linear predictor and likelihood of the chunk's observations; the log hazards at the chunk's
// quadrature points and their weighted sum (the chunk's cumulative hazards); and the random-effect and
// survival-covariate part of the chunk's events' log hazards. Outside the chunks, only terms of fixed size: the
// priors of the main parameters, N_events * log(lambda) and the events' longitudinal fixed-effect term, a dot
// product of X_long_event summed over the events (data) with alpha_assoc * beta_long. The sliced argument is
// b_raw_by_subject, the subjects' columns of b_raw (the same autodiff variables, so no new nodes on the main
// tape), so that each chunk copies only its own subjects' b_raw rather than all of it; b0 and b1, transformed
// parameters before (computed outside the chunks and copied whole into every chunk), are reported as generated
// quantities (the same values).

    //  quad_time_fraction: (quad_points + 1) / 2, the fraction of T_surv[i] at each quadrature point)
    real partial_sum_subjects_lpdf(array[] row_vector b_raw_slice, int start, int end, data int Q,
                                   data matrix X_long, data vector Y_long, data vector time_long,
                                   data array[] int subj_long, data array[] int observations_before,
