    //
    // (the version above, with its loops over the patients and their samples, commented out; the same function
    //  without them: the tri-exponential coefficients of every patient are one whole-vector calculation in the
    //  patients' order, with the rate differences of the stable-form patients set to 1 before the divisions (so
    //  that no division by a small difference is ever made) and their coefficients then set to 0, and so is the
    //  first form of k21 - beta (R + a set to 1 for the patients with a < 0, whose k21 - beta is then the second
    //  form); the index sets of the stable-form patients and of the patients with a < 0 come from
    //  number_of_values_below() and, only when there are values on both sides of the threshold,
    //  sort_indices_asc(); and the stable form is computed for all the samples of the stable-form patients at
    //  once)
    vector two_compartment_oral_concentrations(matrix log_theta, data real dose, data array[] int patient,
                                               data vector time, data array[] int first_sample,
                                               data array[] int last_sample, data real minimum_rate_separation) {
        int N = cols(log_theta);
        vector[N] k10 = nico_exp((log_theta[1] - log_theta[3])');
        vector[N] k12 = nico_exp((log_theta[2] - log_theta[3])');
        vector[N] k21 = nico_exp((log_theta[2] - log_theta[4])');
        vector[N] ka = nico_exp(log_theta[5]');
        vector[N] dose_ka_over_V1 = dose * nico_exp((log_theta[5] - log_theta[3])');
        vector[N] a = k10 + k12 - k21;
        vector[N] alpha_minus_beta = sqrt(square(a) + 4 * k12 .* k21);
        vector[N] alpha = 0.5 * (k10 + k12 + k21 + alpha_minus_beta);
        vector[N] beta = k10 .* k21 ./ alpha;
        vector[N] k21_minus_beta;
        vector[N] coefficient_alpha;
        vector[N] coefficient_beta;
        vector[N] coefficient_ka;
        vector[N] ka_minus_alpha = ka - alpha;
        vector[N] ka_minus_beta = ka - beta;
        // min(|ka - alpha|, |ka - beta|, alpha - beta): the stable form for the patients with this below
        // minimum_rate_separation (fmin() and abs() return the rates' differences themselves, or their negations)
        vector[N] smallest_rate_separation = fmin(fmin(abs(ka_minus_alpha), abs(ka_minus_beta)),
                                                  alpha_minus_beta);
        int n_stable_form = number_of_values_below(smallest_rate_separation, minimum_rate_separation);
        int n_a_negative = number_of_values_below(a, 0);
        array[N] int by_smallest_rate_separation = linspaced_int_array(N, 1, N);
        array[N] int by_a = linspaced_int_array(N, 1, N);
        if (n_stable_form > 0 && n_stable_form < N) {
            by_smallest_rate_separation = sort_indices_asc(smallest_rate_separation);
        }
        if (n_a_negative > 0 && n_a_negative < N) {
            by_a = sort_indices_asc(a);
        }
        array[n_stable_form] int stable_form = by_smallest_rate_separation[1:n_stable_form];
        array[n_a_negative] int a_negative = by_a[1:n_a_negative];
        // array[N - n_stable_form] int tri_exponential = by_smallest_rate_separation[(n_stable_form + 1):N];
        // array[N - n_a_negative] int a_not_negative = by_a[(n_a_negative + 1):N];
        // // k21 - beta = (R - a) / 2, written without cancellation for either sign of a (R = alpha - beta; at
        // // a = 0 both forms are R / 2):
        // k21_minus_beta[a_not_negative] = (2 * k12[a_not_negative]) .* k21[a_not_negative]
        //                                  ./ (alpha_minus_beta[a_not_negative] + a[a_not_negative]);
        // k21_minus_beta[a_negative] = 0.5 * (alpha_minus_beta[a_negative] - a[a_negative]);
        // coefficient_alpha = rep_vector(0, N);
        // coefficient_beta = rep_vector(0, N);
        // coefficient_ka = rep_vector(0, N);
        // // alpha - k21 = k12 k21 / (k21 - beta) (Vieta: (alpha - k21) (k21 - beta) = k12 k21)
        // coefficient_alpha[tri_exponential] = k12[tri_exponential] .* k21[tri_exponential]
        //                                      ./ k21_minus_beta[tri_exponential]
        //                                      ./ (ka_minus_alpha[tri_exponential]
        //                                          .* alpha_minus_beta[tri_exponential]);
        // coefficient_beta[tri_exponential] = k21_minus_beta[tri_exponential]
        //                                     ./ (ka_minus_beta[tri_exponential]
        //                                         .* alpha_minus_beta[tri_exponential]);
        // coefficient_ka[tri_exponential] = (k21[tri_exponential] - ka[tri_exponential])
        //                                   ./ (ka_minus_alpha[tri_exponential]
        //                                       .* ka_minus_beta[tri_exponential]);
        // (the same values for every patient in the patients' order, without gathering the tri-exponential
        //  patients, whose index set came out of sort_indices_asc() in the order of their rates' separations:
        //  the denominators of the stable-form patients, and R + a of the patients with a < 0, set to 1, so that
        //  their values, overwritten below, are finite and their autodiff nodes (with adjoints 0) give no NaN)
        vector[N] ka_minus_alpha_in_divisions = ka_minus_alpha;
        vector[N] ka_minus_beta_in_divisions = ka_minus_beta;
        vector[N] alpha_minus_beta_in_divisions = alpha_minus_beta;
        vector[N] alpha_minus_beta_plus_a_in_divisions = alpha_minus_beta + a;
        ka_minus_alpha_in_divisions[stable_form] = rep_vector(1, n_stable_form);
        ka_minus_beta_in_divisions[stable_form] = rep_vector(1, n_stable_form);
        alpha_minus_beta_in_divisions[stable_form] = rep_vector(1, n_stable_form);
        alpha_minus_beta_plus_a_in_divisions[a_negative] = rep_vector(1, n_a_negative);
        // k21 - beta = (R - a) / 2, written without cancellation for either sign of a (R = alpha - beta; at a = 0
        // both forms are R / 2):
        k21_minus_beta = (2 * k12) .* k21 ./ alpha_minus_beta_plus_a_in_divisions;
        k21_minus_beta[a_negative] = 0.5 * (alpha_minus_beta[a_negative] - a[a_negative]);
        // alpha - k21 = k12 k21 / (k21 - beta) (Vieta: (alpha - k21) (k21 - beta) = k12 k21)
        coefficient_alpha = k12 .* k21 ./ k21_minus_beta
                            ./ (ka_minus_alpha_in_divisions .* alpha_minus_beta_in_divisions);
        coefficient_beta = k21_minus_beta ./ (ka_minus_beta_in_divisions .* alpha_minus_beta_in_divisions);
        coefficient_ka = (k21 - ka) ./ (ka_minus_alpha_in_divisions .* ka_minus_beta_in_divisions);
        coefficient_alpha[stable_form] = rep_vector(0, n_stable_form);
        coefficient_beta[stable_form] = rep_vector(0, n_stable_form);
        coefficient_ka[stable_form] = rep_vector(0, n_stable_form);
        vector[num_elements(time)] concentration =
              dose_ka_over_V1[patient] .* (coefficient_alpha[patient] .* nico_exp(-time .* alpha[patient])
                                           + coefficient_beta[patient] .* nico_exp(-time .* beta[patient])
                                           + coefficient_ka[patient] .* nico_exp(-time .* ka[patient]));
        // the stable form (header), for all the samples of the stable-form patients at once (their
        // tri-exponential coefficients are 0, so their samples above are 0 and are replaced here):
        if (n_stable_form > 0) {
            int n_stable_form_samples = sum(last_sample[stable_form]) - sum(first_sample[stable_form])
                                        + n_stable_form;
            array[2, n_stable_form_samples] int samples_and_their_patients =
                  samples_of_patients(first_sample[stable_form], last_sample[stable_form]);
            array[n_stable_form_samples] int sample_on_stable_form = samples_and_their_patients[1];
            array[n_stable_form_samples] int patient_on_stable_form = stable_form[samples_and_their_patients[2]];
            concentration[sample_on_stable_form] =
                  dose_ka_over_V1[patient_on_stable_form]
                  .* (k21_minus_beta[patient_on_stable_form]
                      .* second_divided_difference_of_decay(alpha[patient_on_stable_form],
                                                            beta[patient_on_stable_form],
                                                            ka[patient_on_stable_form],
                                                            time[sample_on_stable_form])
                      + minus_first_divided_difference_of_decay(alpha[patient_on_stable_form],
                                                                ka[patient_on_stable_form],
                                                                time[sample_on_stable_form]));
        }
        return concentration;
    }
    //
    // The log likelihood of the samples of patients start to end (one chunk of reduce_sum_static): the patients'
    // log CL, log Q, log V1, log V2, log ka (one column per patient: mu + diag(omega) L_Omega z_i), then their
    // samples' predicted concentrations by two_compartment_oral_concentrations(), with the samples' patients and
    // each patient's first and last sample counted from the chunk's first sample (the samples are sorted by
    // patient, so the chunk's samples are first_sample[start] to last_sample[end]):
    //
    //
//  real partial_sum_patients_lpdf(array[] vector z_slice, int start, int end, vector mu,
//                                 matrix diag_omega_times_L_Omega, real sigma, data real dose,
//                                 data array[] int patient, data vector time, data array[] int first_sample,
//                                 data array[] int last_sample, data vector log_concentration_observed,
//                                 data real minimum_rate_separation) {
//      int n_patients = end - start + 1;
//      int s1 = first_sample[start];
//      int s2 = last_sample[end];
//      array[s2 - s1 + 1] int patient_in_chunk;
//      array[n_patients] int first_sample_in_chunk;
//      array[n_patients] int last_sample_in_chunk;
//      matrix[5, n_patients] z_chunk;
//      for (j in s1:s2) {
//          patient_in_chunk[j - s1 + 1] = patient[j] - start + 1;
//      }
//      for (k in 1:n_patients) {
//          first_sample_in_chunk[k] = first_sample[start + k - 1] - s1 + 1;
//          last_sample_in_chunk[k] = last_sample[start + k - 1] - s1 + 1;
//          z_chunk[:, k] = z_slice[k];
//      }
//      matrix[5, n_patients] log_theta = rep_matrix(mu, n_patients) + diag_omega_times_L_Omega * z_chunk;
//      // return normal_lupdf(log_concentration_observed[s1:s2] |
//      //                     log(two_compartment_oral_concentrations(log_theta, dose, patient_in_chunk,
//      //                                                             time[s1:s2], first_sample_in_chunk,
//      //                                                             last_sample_in_chunk,
//      //                                                             minimum_rate_separation)),
//      //                     sigma);
//      // (the chunk's patients' standard normal prior on their columns of z, inside the chunk, in place of
//      //  to_vector(z) ~ std_normal() over all N patients in the model block; then their samples' likelihood)
//      return std_normal_lupdf(to_vector(z_chunk))
//             + normal_lupdf(log_concentration_observed[s1:s2] |
//                            log(two_compartment_oral_concentrations(log_theta, dose, patient_in_chunk,
//                                                                    time[s1:s2], first_sample_in_chunk,
//                                                                    last_sample_in_chunk,
//                                                                    minimum_rate_separation)),
//                            sigma);
//  }
    //
    // (the version above, with its loops over the chunk's samples and patients, commented out; the same function
    //  without them: the slice of z is one row of 5 values per patient (to_array_2d(z') in the model block), and
    //  the samples' patients and each patient's first and last sample, counted within the chunk, are whole-array
    //  integer differences, with to_int())
    // real partial_sum_patients_lpdf(array[,] real z_slice, int start, int end, vector mu,
    // (the slice of z: one row_vector of 5 values per patient, as z is declared)
    real partial_sum_patients_lpdf(array[] row_vector z_slice, int start, int end, vector mu,
                                   matrix diag_omega_times_L_Omega, real sigma, data real dose,
                                   data array[] int patient, data vector time, data array[] int first_sample,
                                   data array[] int last_sample, data vector log_concentration_observed,
                                   data real minimum_rate_separation) {
        int n_patients = end - start + 1;
        int s1 = first_sample[start];
        int s2 = last_sample[end];
        array[s2 - s1 + 1] int patient_in_chunk = to_int(to_array_1d(to_vector(patient[s1:s2]) - (start - 1)));
        array[n_patients] int first_sample_in_chunk = to_int(to_array_1d(to_vector(first_sample[start:end])
                                                                         - (s1 - 1)));
        array[n_patients] int last_sample_in_chunk = to_int(to_array_1d(to_vector(last_sample[start:end])
                                                                        - (s1 - 1)));
        matrix[5, n_patients] z_chunk = to_matrix(z_slice)';
        matrix[5, n_patients] log_theta = rep_matrix(mu, n_patients) + diag_omega_times_L_Omega * z_chunk;
        // (the chunk's patients' standard normal prior on their columns of z, inside the chunk, in place of
        //  to_vector(z) ~ std_normal() over all N patients in the model block; then their samples' likelihood)
        return nico_normal_lupdf(to_vector(z_chunk) | 0, 1)
               + nico_normal_lupdf(log_concentration_observed[s1:s2] |
                                   nico_log(two_compartment_oral_concentrations(log_theta, dose,
                                                                                patient_in_chunk, time[s1:s2],
                                                                                first_sample_in_chunk,
                                                                                last_sample_in_chunk,
                                                                                minimum_rate_separation)),
                                   sigma);
    }
}
data {
    int<lower=1> N;                                    // number of patients
    int<lower=1> n_samples;                            // number of concentration samples (all patients)
    array[n_samples] int<lower=1, upper=N> patient;    // patient of each sample (samples sorted by patient)
    vector<lower=0>[n_samples] time;                   // sampling time after the dose (h), > 0
    vector<lower=0>[n_samples] concentration_observed; // observed plasma concentration (mg/L), > 0
    real<lower=0> dose;                                // the oral dose of every patient, at time 0 (mg)
    int<lower=1> chunk_size;                           // patients per chunk (reduce_sum_static)
}
transformed data {
    vector[n_samples] log_concentration_observed = nico_log(concentration_observed);
    // each patient's samples: first_sample[i] to last_sample[i]
    array[N] int first_sample = rep_array(0, N);
    array[N] int last_sample = rep_array(0, N);
    // the smallest rate difference of the tri-exponential (see the header): d t >= 0.01 at every sample
    real minimum_rate_separation = 0.01 / min(time);
    if (min(time) <= 0) reject("every sampling time must be > 0");
    // for (j in 1:n_samples) {
    //     if (j > 1 && patient[j] < patient[j - 1]) reject("the samples must be sorted by patient");
    //     if (first_sample[patient[j]] == 0) first_sample[patient[j]] = j;
    //     last_sample[patient[j]] = j;
    // }
    // for (i in 1:N) {
    //     if (first_sample[i] == 0) reject("patient ", i, " has no samples");
    // }
    // (the same checks and the same first_sample and last_sample without a loop: the steps of the samples'
    //  patients from one sample to the next must be 0 or 1, from patient 1 to patient N, i.e. sorted and every
    //  patient with samples; then a patient's first sample is a sample whose step from the one before is 1 (or
    //  the first sample), and its last sample one whose step to the next is 1 (or the last sample): the indices
    //  of the N ones of these 0 / 1 vectors, from sort_indices_desc(), sorted)
    vector[n_samples - 1] patient_step = to_vector(patient[2:n_samples]) - to_vector(patient[1:(n_samples - 1)]);
    if (n_samples > 1 && min(patient_step) < 0) reject("the samples must be sorted by patient");
    if (patient[1] != 1) reject("patient ", 1, " has no samples");
    if (patient[n_samples] != N) reject("patient ", N, " has no samples");
    if (n_samples > 1 && max(patient_step) > 1) {
        reject("a patient between ", patient[sort_indices_desc(patient_step)[1]], " and ",
               patient[sort_indices_desc(patient_step)[1] + 1], " has no samples");
    }
    first_sample = sort_asc(sort_indices_desc(append_row(1, patient_step))[1:N]);
    last_sample = sort_asc(sort_indices_desc(append_row(patient_step, 1))[1:N]);
}
parameters {
    // matrix[5, N] z;                                    // standard normal nuisance block, declared first
    array[N] row_vector[5] z;                          // standard normal nuisance block, declared first: patient
                                                       // i's 5 values in z[i] (the sliced argument of
                                                       // reduce_sum_static)
    real mu_CL;                                        // population mean of log CL (CL in L/h)
    real mu_Q;                                         // population mean of log Q (L/h)
    real mu_V1;                                        // population mean of log V1 (L)
    real mu_V2;                                        // population mean of log V2 (L)
    real<lower=two_compartment_log_alpha(mu_CL, mu_Q, mu_V1, mu_V2)> mu_ka; // population mean of log ka (1/h):
                                                       // ka_pop > alpha_pop (flip-flop, see the header)
    vector<lower=0>[5] omega;                          // between-patient SDs of log CL, log Q, log V1, log V2,
                                                       // log ka
    cholesky_factor_corr[5] L_Omega;                   // Cholesky factor of their correlation matrix
    real<lower=0> sigma;                               // residual SD of the log concentrations
}
model {
    vector[5] mu = [mu_CL, mu_Q, mu_V1, mu_V2, mu_ka]';
    // each patient's column of z (the sliced argument of reduce_sum_static: each chunk computes its patients'
    // log CL, log Q, log V1, log V2, log ka, non-centred, from their own columns)
    // array[N] vector[5] z_by_patient;
    // for (i in 1:N) {
    //     z_by_patient[i] = z[:, i];
    // }
    // (without the loop: to_array_2d(z'), one row of 5 values per patient, is the sliced argument below, built
    //  once into a named local variable, as is diag(omega) L_Omega: reduce_sum_static holds an expression given
    //  as an argument by value and copies it at every split of the patients, i.e. the whole O(N) slice about
    //  N_chunks times per gradient, but holds a named variable by reference)
    // array[N, 5] real z_by_patient = to_array_2d(z');
    // (z itself, declared one row of 5 values per patient, is the sliced argument below: nothing to build)
    matrix[5, 5] diag_omega_times_L_Omega = diag_pre_multiply(omega, L_Omega);

    // Priors
    mu_CL ~ normal(log(10), 0.25);
    mu_Q ~ normal(log(15), 0.5);
    mu_V1 ~ normal(log(35), 0.25);
    mu_V2 ~ normal(log(105), 0.5);
    mu_ka ~ normal(log(2.5), 1);
    omega ~ nico_normal(0, 0.5);
    L_Omega ~ lkj_corr_cholesky(2);
    sigma ~ normal(0, 1);

    // Equivalent non-centred form of log_theta[, i] ~ multi_normal(mu, Sigma).
    // to_vector(z) ~ std_normal();
    // (inside the chunks: partial_sum_patients_lpdf adds each chunk's std_normal_lupdf(to_vector(z_chunk)), the
    //  same term, so that this O(N) prior is no longer on the main autodiff tape)

    // Likelihood (reduce_sum_static over the patients, in chunks of chunk_size)
    // target += reduce_sum_static(partial_sum_patients_lupdf, z_by_patient, chunk_size, mu,
    //                             diag_pre_multiply(omega, L_Omega), sigma, dose, patient, time, first_sample,
    //                             last_sample, log_concentration_observed, minimum_rate_separation);
    // target += reduce_sum_static(partial_sum_patients_lupdf, to_array_2d(z'), chunk_size, mu,
    //                             diag_pre_multiply(omega, L_Omega), sigma, dose, patient, time, first_sample,
    //                             last_sample, log_concentration_observed, minimum_rate_separation);
    // target += reduce_sum_static(partial_sum_patients_lupdf, z_by_patient, chunk_size, mu,
    //                             diag_omega_times_L_Omega, sigma, dose, patient, time, first_sample,
    //                             last_sample, log_concentration_observed, minimum_rate_separation);
    target += reduce_sum_static(partial_sum_patients_lupdf, z, chunk_size, mu, diag_omega_times_L_Omega, sigma,
                                dose, patient, time, first_sample, last_sample, log_concentration_observed,
                                minimum_rate_separation);
}
generated quantities {
    real simd_lanes = bmvp_simd_lanes();
}

// hierarchical_logistic_regression_unchunked_no_loops_over_N_with_Stan_fused_functions.stan
// Unchunked Stan::math version of the hierarchical logistic model of the tape-chunking paper's layout timings
// (hierarchical_logistic_regression_chunked_no_loops_over_N_automatic_reduce_sum_chunked, from its source
// hierarchical_logistic_regression_chunked_no_loops_over_N): the same log density as
// hierarchical_logistic_regression.stan, as one pass over all N observations, without reduce_sum_static.
// The same data (chunk_size, when it is in the data, is not read).
// Its parameters are those of hierarchical_logistic_regression.stan, in the same order and with the same names:
// beta_raw as a K x 2 matrix (column 1: the K groups' raw intercepts; column 2: their raw slopes). The chunked
// file's array[K] row_vector[2] beta_raw (the same K x 2 values, group by group) exists only so that
// reduce_sum_static can slice the groups, and orders the same values row by row; a point-by-point check of the
// log density and gradient is hence made against hierarchical_logistic_regression.stan.
// The likelihood is Stan's fused logistic GLM: with the covariates [1, x] (made once in transformed data) and
// the coefficients mu (the population intercept and slope), the intercept of each observation is its group's
// deviation from mu, sigma[1] beta_raw[group, 1] + sigma[2] beta_raw[group, 2] x, i.e.
//     beta[group, 1] + beta[group, 2] x = x_with_ones * mu + (the deviations),
// the same linear predictor as hierarchical_logistic_regression.stan. The groups' deviations are made once per
// group (K values), then read at each observation's group.
// beta, the transformed parameter of hierarchical_logistic_regression.stan, is reported as a generated quantity
// (the same values).
// No loop over N anywhere.


data {
    int<lower=0> N;                    // number of observations
    int<lower=1> K;                    // number of groups
    array[N] int<lower=1, upper=K> group; // group indicator for each observation
    vector[N] x;                       // predictor variable
    array[N] int<lower=0, upper=1> y;  // binary outcome
}


transformed data {
    // the covariates with a first column of ones, so that mu is the coefficient vector of the GLM
    matrix[N, 2] x_with_ones = append_col(rep_vector(1, N), x);
}


parameters {
    matrix[K, 2] beta_raw;             // standard normal nuisance block, declared first
    vector[2] mu;                      // population means for [intercept, slope]
    vector<lower=0>[2] sigma;          // population standard deviations
}


model {
    // Priors
    mu ~ normal(0, 2);
    sigma ~ normal(0, 2);

    // Equivalent non-centred form of beta[, i] ~ normal(mu[i], sigma[i]).
    to_vector(beta_raw) ~ std_normal();

    // Likelihood (Stan's fused logistic GLM; see the header)
    {
      vector[K] deviation_of_intercept_of_group = sigma[1] * beta_raw[, 1];
      vector[K] deviation_of_slope_of_group = sigma[2] * beta_raw[, 2];
      y ~ bernoulli_logit_glm(x_with_ones,
                              deviation_of_intercept_of_group[group]
                              + deviation_of_slope_of_group[group] .* x,
                              mu);
    }
}


generated quantities {
    matrix[K, 2] beta;                 // group-specific intercepts and slopes
    vector[N] log_lik;
    vector[N] y_rep;

    for (i in 1:2) {
      beta[, i] = mu[i] + sigma[i] * beta_raw[, i];
    }

    // (on the whole vectors, as in the chunked file: each observation's bernoulli_logit_lpmf(y[n] | eta[n]) is
    //  log_inv_logit((2 y[n] - 1) eta[n]), and bernoulli_logit_rng draws the replicates in the same order)
    {
      vector[N] eta = beta[group, 1] + beta[group, 2] .* x;
      log_lik = log_inv_logit((2 * to_vector(y) - 1) .* eta);
      y_rep = to_vector(bernoulli_logit_rng(eta));
    }
}

// hierarchical_logistic_regression_chunked_no_loops_over_N.stan
// Tape-chunked version of hierarchical_logistic_regression.stan with no loop over the observations or the groups:
// the same log density, with everything whose size grows with N computed inside the chunks of
// reduce_sum_static, on whole vectors. The chunks are the groups (K of them, N / 12 at every data case), each
// with its observations, which are sorted by group once (transformed data, by sorting, with no loop). The
// nuisance block beta_raw is declared as an array of the K groups' rows, so that it is the sliced argument of
// reduce_sum_static itself (no copy of all K rows on the main tape, and each chunk copies only its own groups'
// rows); each chunk adds its groups' share of the nuisance block's standard normal prior, computes its groups'
// coefficients beta = mu + sigma * beta_raw (the transformed parameter of hierarchical_logistic_regression.stan,
// reported here as a generated quantity, the same values) and the likelihood of its groups' observations; only
// mu and sigma (4 values) are shared. The generated quantities are computed on whole vectors too.
// The unconstrained parameters are those of hierarchical_logistic_regression.stan in another order: beta_raw
// row by row (beta_raw[1, 1], beta_raw[1, 2], beta_raw[2, 1], ...) in place of column by column; the names are
// the same.
// The chunks: N_chunks = ceiling(N / chunk_size), from NicoStan's chunk_size of the observations (N, the units
// of the chunks), each of groups_per_chunk = ceiling(K / N_chunks) groups (the grainsize of reduce_sum_static
// over the groups).
//
// The header of the tape-chunked model this one comes from (the next 9 lines):
// hierarchical_logistic_regression_chunked.stan
// Tape-chunked version of hierarchical_logistic_regression.stan: the same log density, with the likelihood
// summed over the groups by reduce_sum_static. The observations are sorted by group once (transformed data), so
// that each group's observations are consecutive, and each group's coefficients, beta[k] (a row of the
// transformed parameter beta), are the sliced argument, so that each chunk copies only its own groups'
// coefficients (and not all K of them); each chunk's term is the original likelihood statement restricted to its
// groups' observations, vectorised over them. The chunks: N_chunks = ceiling(N / chunk_size), from NicoStan's

// hierarchical_logistic_regression_chunked.stan
// Tape-chunked version of hierarchical_logistic_regression.stan: the same log density, with the
// likelihood summed over the observations by reduce_sum_static, in chunks of chunk_size observations (data), so
// that each chunk's autodiff tape is built, differentiated and released before the next one (the
// chunking paper's tape
// chunking; N_chunks from NicoStan::fn_compute_initial_N_chunks()). Each chunk's term is the original
// likelihood statement restricted to the chunk's observations.
// The chunking data are NicoStan's for Stan models: N (the observations, the units of the chunks) and
// chunk_size, which NicoStan sets to ceiling(N / N_chunks) in each phase (num_chunks_burnin,

                                                              + beta_of_slice[position_in_slice, 2]
                                                                .* x_sorted[first:last]);
    }
}

    //  last of group k - 1. sort_indices_asc(sort_indices_asc(v)) is the position of each element of v in v
    //  sorted.)
    array[N + K] real groups_and_half_way_values = append_array(to_array_1d(to_vector(group)),
                                                                to_array_1d(linspaced_vector(K, 1.5, K + 0.5)));
    array[N + K] int position_when_sorted = sort_indices_asc(sort_indices_asc(groups_and_half_way_values));
    array[K] int last_of_group = to_int(to_array_1d(to_vector(position_when_sorted[(N + 1):(N + K)])
                                                    - linspaced_vector(K, 1, K)));

                                                                       + 1)));

// hierarchical_logistic_regression_chunked_no_loops_over_N_hand_written_BayesMVP_AVX.stan
// Hand-written AVX version of models_staging_no_loops_over_N_hierarchical_robust_t_IRT/hierarchical_logistic_regression_chunked_no_loops_over_N.stan: every log density and elementwise function on a
// vector or matrix is BayesMVP's fast_ function, declared in the functions block; calls on single
// reals stay on Stan math. One text for both instruction sets (NicoStan's AVX2 or AVX-512 make
// arguments).


// hierarchical_logistic_regression_chunked_no_loops_over_N.stan
// Tape-chunked version of hierarchical_logistic_regression.stan with no loop over the observations or the groups:
// the same log density, with everything whose size grows with N computed inside the chunks of
// reduce_sum_static, on whole vectors. The chunks are the groups (K of them, N / 12 at every data case), each
// with its observations, which are sorted by group once (transformed data, by sorting, with no loop). The
// nuisance block beta_raw is declared as an array of the K groups' rows, so that it is the sliced argument of
// reduce_sum_static itself (no copy of all K rows on the main tape, and each chunk copies only its own groups'
// rows); each chunk adds its groups' share of the nuisance block's standard normal prior, computes its groups'
// coefficients beta = mu + sigma * beta_raw (the transformed parameter of hierarchical_logistic_regression.stan,
// reported here as a generated quantity, the same values) and the likelihood of its groups' observations; only
// mu and sigma (4 values) are shared. The generated quantities are computed on whole vectors too.
// The unconstrained parameters are those of hierarchical_logistic_regression.stan in another order: beta_raw
// row by row (beta_raw[1, 1], beta_raw[1, 2], beta_raw[2, 1], ...) in place of column by column; the names are
// the same.
// The chunks: N_chunks = ceiling(N / chunk_size), from NicoStan's chunk_size of the observations (N, the units
// of the chunks), each of groups_per_chunk = ceiling(K / N_chunks) groups (the grainsize of reduce_sum_static
// over the groups).
//
// The header of the tape-chunked model this one comes from (the next 9 lines):
// hierarchical_logistic_regression_chunked.stan
// Tape-chunked version of hierarchical_logistic_regression.stan: the same log density, with the likelihood
// summed over the groups by reduce_sum_static. The observations are sorted by group once (transformed data), so
// that each group's observations are consecutive, and each group's coefficients, beta[k] (a row of the
// transformed parameter beta), are the sliced argument, so that each chunk copies only its own groups'
// coefficients (and not all K of them); each chunk's term is the original likelihood statement restricted to its
// groups' observations, vectorised over them. The chunks: N_chunks = ceiling(N / chunk_size), from NicoStan's
// chunk_size of the observations (N, the units of the chunks), each of groups_per_chunk = ceiling(K / N_chunks)
// groups (the grainsize of reduce_sum_static over the groups).
//
// The previous tape-chunked model (beta, all K rows, shared by every chunk) is kept below, commented out; its
// header was (the next 9 lines):
// hierarchical_logistic_regression_chunked.stan
// Tape-chunked version of hierarchical_logistic_regression.stan: the same log density, with the
// likelihood summed over the observations by reduce_sum_static, in chunks of chunk_size observations (data), so
// that each chunk's autodiff tape is built, differentiated and released before the next one (the
// chunking paper's tape
// chunking; N_chunks from NicoStan::fn_compute_initial_N_chunks()). Each chunk's term is the original
// likelihood statement restricted to the chunk's observations.
// The chunking data are NicoStan's for Stan models: N (the observations, the units of the chunks) and
// chunk_size, which NicoStan sets to ceiling(N / N_chunks) in each phase (num_chunks_burnin,
// num_chunks_sampling).

functions {
    real bmvp_simd_lanes();
    vector nico_log_inv_logit(vector x);
    real nico_normal_lpdf(vector y, real mu, real sigma);
    real nico_bernoulli_logit_lpmf(array[] int y, vector f);
    // real partial_sum_observations_lpmf(array[] int y_slice, int start, int end,
    //                                    array[] int group, vector x, matrix beta) {
    //     return bernoulli_logit_lupmf(y_slice | beta[group[start:end], 1]
    //                                            + beta[group[start:end], 2] .* x[start:end]);
    // }
    // // (the chunk's slice of the data copied once, as data, and indexed from the copy)
    // real partial_sum_observations_lpmf(array[] int y_slice, int start, int end,

    //     return bernoulli_logit_lupmf(y_slice | beta[group_slice, 1] + beta[group_slice, 2] .* x[start:end]);
    // }
    // the likelihood of the groups start to end, whose observations are first_of_group[start] to
    // last_of_group[end] in the order sorted by group: each observation's coefficients from beta_slice, by its
    // group's position in the slice
    // real partial_sum_groups(array[] row_vector beta_slice, int start, int end,
    //                         data array[] int y_sorted,
    //                         data vector x_sorted,
    //                         data array[] int group_sorted,
    //                         data array[] int first_of_group,
    //                         data array[] int last_of_group) {
    //     int first = first_of_group[start];
    //     int last = last_of_group[end];
    //     matrix[end - start + 1, 2] beta_of_slice = to_matrix(beta_slice);
    //     array[last - first + 1] int position_in_slice;
    //     for (n in first:last) {
    //         position_in_slice[n - first + 1] = group_sorted[n] - start + 1;
    //     }
    //     return bernoulli_logit_lpmf(y_sorted[first:last] | beta_of_slice[position_in_slice, 1]
    //                                                         + beta_of_slice[position_in_slice, 2]
    //                                                           .* x_sorted[first:last]);
    // }
    //
    // The log density of the groups start to end (one chunk of reduce_sum_static), with no loop: the groups'
    // share of the nuisance block's standard normal prior (to_vector(beta_raw) ~ std_normal()), their
    // coefficients beta = mu + sigma * beta_raw, and the likelihood of their observations, first_of_group[start]
    // to last_of_group[end] in the order sorted by group, each observation's coefficients taken by its group's
    // position in the slice (group_sorted - start + 1, computed on the whole vector of the slice's observations)
    //
    real partial_sum_groups_lpdf(array[] row_vector beta_raw_slice, int start, int end,
                                 vector mu,
                                 vector sigma,
                                 data array[] int y_sorted,
                                 data vector x_sorted,
                                 data array[] int group_sorted,
                                 data array[] int first_of_group,
                                 data array[] int last_of_group) {
        int first = first_of_group[start];
        int last = last_of_group[end];
        matrix[end - start + 1, 2] beta_raw_of_slice = to_matrix(beta_raw_slice);
        matrix[end - start + 1, 2] beta_of_slice;
        for (i in 1:2) {
            beta_of_slice[, i] = mu[i] + sigma[i] * beta_raw_of_slice[, i];
        }
        array[last - first + 1] int position_in_slice = to_int(to_array_1d(to_vector(group_sorted[first:last])
                                                                           - (start - 1)));
        return nico_normal_lupdf(to_vector(beta_raw_of_slice) | 0, 1)
               + nico_bernoulli_logit_lupmf(y_sorted[first:last] | beta_of_slice[position_in_slice, 1]
                                                              + beta_of_slice[position_in_slice, 2]
                                                                .* x_sorted[first:last]);
    }
}

Robust Student-t regression

unchunked, with Stan's fused functions

benchmark_models/robust_Student_t_regression_unchunked_no_loops_over_N_with_Stan_fused_functions.stan (60 lines)
// robust_Student_t_regression_unchunked_no_loops_over_N_with_Stan_fused_functions.stan
// Unchunked Stan::math version of robust_Student_t_regression_chunked_no_loops_over_N_v2 (the Stan math file of
// the tape-chunking paper's layout timings): the same log density as that file at N_chunks = 1, and as
// robust_Student_t_regression.stan, as one pass over all N observations, without reduce_sum_static. The same
// data (chunk_size, when it is in the data, is not read) and the same unconstrained parameters, in the same
// order and with the same names (alpha, beta, sigma), as both files.
// Stan has no fused Student-t GLM: the likelihood is Stan's vectorised student_t on the whole vector of
// responses, with alpha folded into the coefficients of one product per observation ([1, X] times
// append_row(alpha, beta), the covariates' first column of ones made once in transformed data), as in v2.
// mu, the transformed parameter of robust_Student_t_regression.stan, is reported as a generated quantity (the
// same values), so that no N-sized value is saved for the log density.
// No loop over N anywhere.


data {
    int<lower=1> N;                    // number of observations
    int<lower=1> K;                    // number of predictors
    matrix[N, K] X;                    // design matrix (without intercept)
    vector[N] y;                       // response variable
    real<lower=1> nu;                  // degrees of freedom (fixed at 4)
}


transformed data {
    // the covariates with a first column of ones, so that alpha is the first coefficient of the product
    matrix[N, K + 1] X_with_ones = append_col(rep_vector(1, N), X);
}


parameters {
    real alpha;                        // intercept
    vector[K] beta;                    // regression coefficients
    real<lower=0> sigma;               // scale parameter
}


model {
    // Priors
    alpha ~ normal(0, 10);
    beta ~ normal(0, 2.5);
    sigma ~ exponential(1);

    // Likelihood with t-distributed errors (alpha + X * beta = [1, X] * append_row(alpha, beta))
    y ~ student_t(nu, X_with_ones * append_row(alpha, beta), sigma);
}


generated quantities {
    // (mu: the transformed parameter of robust_Student_t_regression.stan, the same values)
    vector[N] mu = alpha + X * beta;   // linear predictor
    vector[N] log_lik;
    vector[N] y_rep;

    // (on the whole vectors, as in the chunked file: each observation's log likelihood,
    //  student_t_lpdf(y[n] | nu, mu[n], sigma), in closed form, and the replicates drawn by
    //  student_t_rng(nu, mu, sigma) on the whole vector, in the same order)
    log_lik = lgamma((nu + 1) / 2) - lgamma(nu / 2) - 0.5 * log(nu * pi()) - log(sigma)
              - (nu + 1) / 2 * log1p(square((y - mu) / sigma) / nu);
    y_rep   = to_vector(student_t_rng(nu, mu, sigma));
}

// num_chunks_sampling).

functions {

    //                                    matrix X, real nu, real alpha, vector beta, real sigma) {
    //     return student_t_lupdf(y_slice | nu, alpha + X[start:end] * beta, sigma);
    // }
    // (X and nu declared as data, as they are)
    real partial_sum_observations_lpdf(array[] real y_slice, int start, int end,
                                       data matrix X_with_ones, data real nu, real alpha, vector beta,
                                       real sigma) {
        // return student_t_lupdf(y_slice | nu, alpha + X[start:end] * beta, sigma);
        // (the same values, with alpha folded into the coefficients: alpha + X * beta =
        //  [1, X] * append_row(alpha, beta), so that each observation's location takes one product, in place
        //  of a product and an addition per observation)
        return student_t_lupdf(y_slice | nu, X_with_ones[start:end] * append_row(alpha, beta), sigma);
    }
}


data {
    int<lower=1> N;                    // number of observations
    int<lower=1> K;                    // number of predictors
    matrix[N, K] X;                    // design matrix (without intercept)
    vector[N] y;                       // response variable
    real<lower=1> nu;                  // degrees of freedom (fixed at 4)
    int<lower=1> chunk_size;           // observations per chunk (reduce_sum_static)
}


transformed data {
    array[N] real y_array = to_array_1d(y);   // the responses, the sliced argument of reduce_sum_static
    // the covariates with a first column of ones, so that alpha is the first coefficient of the products
    matrix[N, K + 1] X_with_ones = append_col(rep_vector(1, N), X);
}


parameters {
    real alpha;                        // intercept
    vector[K] beta;                    // regression coefficients
    real<lower=0> sigma;               // scale parameter
}


model {
    // Priors
    alpha ~ normal(0, 10);
    beta ~ normal(0, 2.5);
    sigma ~ exponential(1);

    // Likelihood with t-distributed errors (reduce_sum_static over the observations, in chunks of chunk_size;
    // each chunk's linear predictor is alpha + X * beta at its observations)
    // target += reduce_sum_static(partial_sum_observations_lupdf, y_array, chunk_size, X, nu, alpha, beta,
    //                             sigma);
    target += reduce_sum_static(partial_sum_observations_lupdf, y_array, chunk_size, X_with_ones, nu, alpha, beta,
                                sigma);
}


generated quantities {
    // (mu: the transformed parameter of robust_Student_t_regression.stan, the same values)
    vector[N] mu = alpha + X * beta;   // linear predictor
    vector[N] log_lik;
    vector[N] y_rep;

    // for (n in 1:N) {
    //   log_lik[n] = student_t_lpdf(y[n] | nu, mu[n], sigma);
    //   y_rep[n]   = student_t_rng(nu, mu[n], sigma);
    // }
    // (on the whole vectors: each observation's log likelihood, student_t_lpdf(y[n] | nu, mu[n], sigma), is
    //  lgamma((nu + 1) / 2) - lgamma(nu / 2) - log(nu pi) / 2 - log(sigma)
    //  - (nu + 1) / 2 log1p(((y[n] - mu[n]) / sigma)^2 / nu), and student_t_rng(nu, mu, sigma) draws the
    //  replicates in the same order, each as student_t_rng(nu, mu[n], sigma))
    log_lik = lgamma((nu + 1) / 2) - lgamma(nu / 2) - 0.5 * log(nu * pi()) - log(sigma)
              - (nu + 1) / 2 * log1p(square((y - mu) / sigma) / nu);
    y_rep   = to_vector(student_t_rng(nu, mu, sigma));
}

        //  of a product and an addition per observation)
        return nico_student_t_lupdf(y_slice | nu, X_with_ones[start:end] * append_row(alpha, beta), sigma);
    }

benchmark_models/graded_response_IRT_unchunked_no_loops_over_N_with_Stan_fused_functions.stan (85 lines)
// graded_response_IRT_unchunked_no_loops_over_N_with_Stan_fused_functions.stan
// Unchunked Stan::math version of the graded response model of the tape-chunking paper's layout timings
// (graded_response_IRT_chunked_no_loops_over_N_automatic_reduce_sum_chunked, from its source
// graded_response_IRT_chunked_no_loops_over_N): the same log density as that source at N_chunks = 1, and as
// graded_response_IRT.stan, as one pass over all N persons, without reduce_sum_static. The same data
// (chunk_size, when it is in the data, is not read) and the same unconstrained parameters, in the same order and
// with the same names (theta, a, c), as both files; theta is a vector, as in graded_response_IRT.stan (the
// source's array[N] real theta, the same N values in the same order, exists only so that reduce_sum_static can
// slice the persons).
// The model is defined for complete data (every person answers every item once), as in the source: the
// responses are sorted by item, and then by person, once in transformed data (by sorting, with no loop), and the
// data are checked to be complete, so that item j's responses are the N responses y_by_item[(j - 1) N + 1] to
// y_by_item[j N], those of persons 1 to N in turn.
// The likelihood is Stan's fused ordered-logistic GLM, item by item: the abilities theta as the one column of x
// (an N x 1 matrix of the same values), the item's discrimination as its coefficient and the item's own
// cut-points; the loop is over the J items, whose number does not grow with N (one GLM per item, since each item
// has its own cut-points, and the GLM takes one cut-point vector).
// No loop over N anywhere.
//
// The model, as in graded_response_IRT.stan:
// Samejima's graded response model (GRM) for ordinal item responses, in its slope-intercept form on the
// logistic metric: N persons each answer every one of J items with one of K ordered categories 1, ..., K. For
// person n and item j, P(Y_nj >= k) = inv_logit(a_j theta_n - c_j,k-1), k = 2, ..., K, with the person's
// ability theta_n, the item's discrimination a_j > 0 and its ordered cutpoints c_j,1 < ... < c_j,K-1.
// Priors: a_j ~ lognormal(0, 0.5); every cutpoint c_jk ~ N(0, 5^2); theta_n ~ N(0, 1).


data {
    int<lower=1> N;                                  // number of persons
    int<lower=1> J;                                  // number of items
    int<lower=2> K;                                  // number of ordered response categories
    int<lower=1> n_responses;                        // number of responses (N J: complete data)
    array[n_responses] int<lower=1, upper=N> person; // person of each response (responses sorted by person)
    array[n_responses] int<lower=1, upper=J> item;   // item of each response
    array[n_responses] int<lower=1, upper=K> y;      // response category of each response
}


transformed data {
    // the responses sorted by item, and then by person, by the key item (N + 1) + person of each response; for
    // complete data the keys are distinct and, sorted, are those of (item 1, person 1), ..., (item 1, person N),
    // (item 2, person 1), ..., (item J, person N) (as in the chunked source)
    vector[n_responses] key_of_response = to_vector(item) * (N + 1) + to_vector(person);
    array[n_responses] int order_by_item = sort_indices_asc(key_of_response);
    array[n_responses] int y_by_item = y[order_by_item];
    if (n_responses != N * J) {
        reject("the model is defined for complete data: n_responses must be N J = ", N * J,
               "; got n_responses = ", n_responses);
    }
    {
        matrix[N, J] key_of_each_person_and_item = rep_matrix(linspaced_row_vector(J, 1, J) * (N + 1), N)
                                                   + rep_matrix(linspaced_vector(N, 1, N), J);
        vector[n_responses] key_of_complete_data = to_vector(key_of_each_person_and_item);
        if (max(abs(key_of_response[order_by_item] - key_of_complete_data)) > 0) {
            reject("the model is defined for complete data: every person must answer every item once");
        }
    }
}


parameters {
    vector[N] theta;                                 // abilities: standard normal nuisance block, declared first
    vector<lower=0>[J] a;                            // item discriminations
    array[J] ordered[K - 1] c;                       // item cutpoints (logit scale), ordered within each item
}


model {
    // Priors
    a ~ lognormal(0, 0.5);
    for (j in 1:J) {
        c[j] ~ normal(0, 5);
    }

    // The abilities: the nuisance block's standard normal prior
    theta ~ std_normal();

    // Likelihood (Stan's fused ordered-logistic GLM, item by item; see the header)
    {
        matrix[N, 1] theta_as_matrix = to_matrix(theta);
        for (j in 1:J) {
            y_by_item[((j - 1) * N + 1):(j * N)] ~ ordered_logistic_glm(theta_as_matrix, a[j:j], c[j]);
        }
    }
}

//
// graded_response_IRT_chunked_no_loops_over_N.stan
// Tape-chunked version of graded_response_IRT.stan with no loop over the persons or the responses: the same log
// density, with everything whose size grows with N computed inside the chunks of reduce_sum_static, on whole
// vectors. The abilities theta are declared as an array, so that they are the sliced argument of
// reduce_sum_static itself (no copy of all N abilities on the main tape, and each chunk copies only its own
// persons' theta); the item parameters a and c (J + J (K - 1) values) are shared. Each chunk adds its persons'
// share of the abilities' standard normal prior (theta ~ std_normal()) and, item by item (J = 20 items, a
// number that does not grow with N), one ordered logistic statement on the item's responses of the chunk's
// persons. The model is defined for complete data (every person answers every item once; see below), so these
// responses are one contiguous block of the responses sorted by item, and then by person, in the order of the
// chunk's abilities: each statement takes the chunk's abilities as they are, with no index of the responses'
// persons. The responses are sorted by item once (transformed data, by sorting, with no loop), and the data are
// checked to be complete. The abilities theta are the same unconstrained parameters, in the same order and with
// the same names, as in graded_response_IRT.stan.
// The chunking data are NicoStan's for Stan models: N (the persons, the units of the chunks; already in the data)
// and chunk_size, which NicoStan sets to ceiling(N / N_chunks) in each phase (num_chunks_burnin,
// num_chunks_sampling).
//
// The header of the tape-chunked model this one comes from (the next 14 lines):
// Tape-chunked version of graded_response_IRT.stan: the same log density, with the likelihood of the responses
// summed over the persons by reduce_sum_static, in chunks of chunk_size persons (data), so that each chunk's
// autodiff tape is built, differentiated and released before the next one (the chunking paper's
// chunking; N_chunks
// from NicoStan::fn_compute_initial_N_chunks()). Each chunk's term is the original likelihood statement
// restricted to the responses of the chunk's persons (the responses are sorted by person, so the chunk's
// responses are contiguous: first_response[start] to last_response[end]), with the responses' persons counted
// from the chunk's first person. The abilities theta are the sliced argument of reduce_sum_static
// (to_array_1d(theta)), so that each chunk copies only its own persons' theta, and not the whole person block,
// onto its tape; the item parameters a and c (J + J (K - 1) values) are shared. Each chunk also adds its
// persons' share of the abilities' standard normal prior (theta ~ std_normal()), so that nothing per person is
// computed outside reduce_sum_static.
// The chunking data are NicoStan's for Stan models: N (the persons, the units of the chunks; already in the data)
// and chunk_size, which NicoStan sets to ceiling(N / N_chunks) in each phase (num_chunks_burnin,
// num_chunks_sampling).
//
// The model, as in graded_response_IRT.stan:
//
// Samejima's graded response model (GRM; Samejima 1969, Psychometrika Monograph Supplement 17) for ordinal item
// responses, in its slope-intercept form on the logistic metric: N persons each answer every one of J items
// with one of K ordered categories 1, ..., K (complete data; the responses are sorted by person, so that each
// person's J responses are contiguous). For person n and item j,
//   P(Y_nj >= k) = inv_logit(a_j theta_n - c_j,k-1),  k = 2, ..., K,
// with the person's ability theta_n, the item's discrimination a_j > 0 and its ordered cutpoints
// c_j,1 < ... < c_j,K-1 (logit scale; the thresholds on the ability scale are b_jk = c_jk / a_j), i.e.
//   y ~ ordered_logistic(a[item] .* theta[person], c[item])
// (Stan's vectorised ordered logistic, with the cutpoint vector of each response's item).
//
// The abilities theta (N) are the nuisance block, declared first (NicoStan samples the first declared block,
// with its standard normal prior, by diffusion-pathspace HMC); their N(0, 1) prior fixes the location and the
// scale of the latent trait, and a_j > 0 its sign. The main block is a (J) and c (J x (K - 1)), i.e. J K
// unconstrained coordinates (100 for J = 20 items with K = 5 categories).
//
// Priors: a_j ~ lognormal(0, 0.5) (median 1, 95% prior interval 0.38 to 2.66: weakly informative over the usual
// range of discriminations on the logistic metric, about 0.5 to 2.5); every cutpoint c_jk ~ N(0, 5^2), on the
// ordered vector of each item (weak for an intercept on the logit scale: c_jk = a_j b_jk lies within about -6 to
// 6 for discriminations up to 2.5 and thresholds within -2.5 to 2.5); theta_n ~ N(0, 1).

    //

    // once): item j's responses of persons start to end are y_by_item[(j - 1) N + start] to

    // abilities, so that the item's statement takes the chunk's abilities as they are, a[j] * theta_chunk, with
    // no index of the responses' persons; the loop is over the J items, whose number does not grow with N
    // (the chunk's persons' share of the abilities' standard normal prior, theta ~ std_normal(), is added here)
    //
    real partial_sum_persons_by_item_of_complete_data_lpdf(array[] real theta_slice, int start, int end,
                                                           vector a, array[] vector c,
                                                           data array[] int y_by_item, int N) {
        int J = num_elements(a);
        vector[end - start + 1] theta_chunk = to_vector(theta_slice);
        real log_likelihood = 0;

    // distinct and, sorted, are those of (item 1, person 1), ..., (item 1, person N), (item 2, person 1), ...,

// vector or matrix is BayesMVP's fast_ function, declared in the functions block; calls on single
// reals stay on Stan math. One text for both instruction sets (NicoStan's AVX2 or AVX-512 make
// arguments).

// graded_response_IRT_chunked_no_loops_over_N.stan
// Tape-chunked version of graded_response_IRT.stan with no loop over the persons or the responses: the same log
// density, with everything whose size grows with N computed inside the chunks of reduce_sum_static, on whole
// vectors. The abilities theta are declared as an array, so that they are the sliced argument of
// reduce_sum_static itself (no copy of all N abilities on the main tape, and each chunk copies only its own
// persons' theta); the item parameters a and c (J + J (K - 1) values) are shared. Each chunk adds its persons'
// share of the abilities' standard normal prior (theta ~ std_normal()) and, item by item (J = 20 items, a
// number that does not grow with N), one ordered logistic statement on the item's responses of the chunk's
// persons. The model is defined for complete data (every person answers every item once; see below), so these
// responses are one contiguous block of the responses sorted by item, and then by person, in the order of the
// chunk's abilities: each statement takes the chunk's abilities as they are, with no index of the responses'
// persons. The responses are sorted by item once (transformed data, by sorting, with no loop), and the data are
// checked to be complete. The abilities theta are the same unconstrained parameters, in the same order and with
// the same names, as in graded_response_IRT.stan.
// The chunking data are NicoStan's for Stan models: N (the persons, the units of the chunks; already in the data)
// and chunk_size, which NicoStan sets to ceiling(N / N_chunks) in each phase (num_chunks_burnin,
// num_chunks_sampling).

// summed over the persons by reduce_sum_static, in chunks of chunk_size persons (data), so that each chunk's
// autodiff tape is built, differentiated and released before the next one (the chunking paper's
// chunking; N_chunks
// from NicoStan::fn_compute_initial_N_chunks()). Each chunk's term is the original likelihood statement
// restricted to the responses of the chunk's persons (the responses are sorted by person, so the chunk's
// responses are contiguous: first_response[start] to last_response[end]), with the responses' persons counted
// from the chunk's first person. The abilities theta are the sliced argument of reduce_sum_static
// (to_array_1d(theta)), so that each chunk copies only its own persons' theta, and not the whole person block,
// onto its tape; the item parameters a and c (J + J (K - 1) values) are shared. Each chunk also adds its
// persons' share of the abilities' standard normal prior (theta ~ std_normal()), so that nothing per person is
// computed outside reduce_sum_static.
// The chunking data are NicoStan's for Stan models: N (the persons, the units of the chunks; already in the data)
// and chunk_size, which NicoStan sets to ceiling(N / N_chunks) in each phase (num_chunks_burnin,
// num_chunks_sampling).
//
// The model, as in graded_response_IRT.stan:
//
// Samejima's graded response model (GRM; Samejima 1969, Psychometrika Monograph Supplement 17) for ordinal item
// responses, in its slope-intercept form on the logistic metric: N persons each answer every one of J items
// with one of K ordered categories 1, ..., K (complete data; the responses are sorted by person, so that each
// person's J responses are contiguous). For person n and item j,
//   P(Y_nj >= k) = inv_logit(a_j theta_n - c_j,k-1),  k = 2, ..., K,
// with the person's ability theta_n, the item's discrimination a_j > 0 and its ordered cutpoints
// c_j,1 < ... < c_j,K-1 (logit scale; the thresholds on the ability scale are b_jk = c_jk / a_j), i.e.
//   y ~ ordered_logistic(a[item] .* theta[person], c[item])
// (Stan's vectorised ordered logistic, with the cutpoint vector of each response's item).
//

// with its standard normal prior, by diffusion-pathspace HMC); their N(0, 1) prior fixes the location and the
// scale of the latent trait, and a_j > 0 its sign. The main block is a (J) and c (J x (K - 1)), i.e. J K
// unconstrained coordinates (100 for J = 20 items with K = 5 categories).
//
// Priors: a_j ~ lognormal(0, 0.5) (median 1, 95% prior interval 0.38 to 2.66: weakly informative over the usual
// range of discriminations on the logistic metric, about 0.5 to 2.5); every cutpoint c_jk ~ N(0, 5^2), on the
// ordered vector of each item (weak for an intercept on the logit scale: c_jk = a_j b_jk lies within about -6 to
// 6 for discriminations up to 2.5 and thresholds within -2.5 to 2.5); theta_n ~ N(0, 1).

    // (the chunk's persons' share of the abilities' standard normal prior, theta ~ std_normal(), is added here)

    real partial_sum_persons_by_item_of_complete_data_lpdf(array[] real theta_slice, int start, int end,

                                                           data array[] int y_by_item, int N) {
        int J = num_elements(a);
        vector[end - start + 1] theta_chunk = to_vector(theta_slice);
        real log_likelihood = 0;

unchunked, with Stan's fused functions

benchmark_models/Gaussian_process_regression_unchunked_no_loops_over_N_with_Stan_fused_functions.stan (114 lines)
// Gaussian_process_regression_unchunked_no_loops_over_N_with_Stan_fused_functions.stan
// Unchunked Stan::math version of Gaussian_process_regression_chunked (the Stan math file of the
// chunking paper's layout
// timings): the same log density as that file at N_chunks = 1, and as Gaussian_process_regression.stan, without
// reduce_sum_static. The same data (chunk_size, when it is in the data, is not read) and the same unconstrained
// parameters, in the same order and with the same names (lengthscale, sigma_f, sigma_n), as both files.
// Stan's fused functions: gp_exp_quad_cov for the covariance matrix, add_diag for its two diagonal terms (no
// N x N diagonal matrix), cholesky_decompose, and multi_normal_cholesky for the likelihood (the triangular
// solve, the log determinant and the density in one node), as in Gaussian_process_regression.stan and
// Gaussian_process_regression_chunked_with_multi_normal_cholesky; its zero mean is made once in transformed data.
// The model block is that of Gaussian_process_regression.stan, which already has no loop over N; the one loop
// over the observations of that file, in gp_pred_rng() of its generated quantities, is replaced by add_diag, as
// in the chunked file (the same values).
// No loop over N anywhere.


functions {
    vector gp_pred_rng(array[] real x2,
                       vector y1,
                       array[] real x1,
                       real sigma_f,
                       real lengthscale_f,
                       real sigma,
                       real fixed_nugget_sd,
                       real jitter) {
      int N1 = rows(y1);
      int N2 = size(x2);
      vector[N2] f2;
      {
        matrix[N1, N1] L_K;
        vector[N1] K_div_y1;
        matrix[N1, N2] k_x1_x2;
        matrix[N1, N2] v_pred;
        vector[N2] f2_mu;
        matrix[N2, N2] cov_f2;
        matrix[N1, N1] K;

        // (the diagonal terms square(sigma) + square(fixed_nugget_sd), added in the same order by add_diag,
        //  without the loop over the observations, as in the chunked file)
        K = add_diag(add_diag(gp_exp_quad_cov(x1, sigma_f, lengthscale_f), square(sigma)),
                     square(fixed_nugget_sd));
        L_K = cholesky_decompose(K);
        K_div_y1 = mdivide_left_tri_low(L_K, y1);
        K_div_y1 = mdivide_right_tri_low(K_div_y1', L_K)';
        k_x1_x2 = gp_exp_quad_cov(x1, x2, sigma_f, lengthscale_f);
        f2_mu = (k_x1_x2' * K_div_y1);
        v_pred = mdivide_left_tri_low(L_K, k_x1_x2);
        cov_f2 = gp_exp_quad_cov(x2, sigma_f, lengthscale_f) - v_pred' * v_pred;
        f2 = multi_normal_rng(f2_mu, add_diag(cov_f2, rep_vector(jitter, N2)));
      }
      return f2;
    }
}


data {
    int<lower=2> N;          // at least two observations for standardisation
    vector[N] x;             // input locations
    vector[N] y;             // target variable
    int<lower=1> N_pred;     // number of prediction points
    vector[N_pred] x_pred;   // prediction input locations
}


transformed data {
    // Normalize data
    real x_mean = mean(x);
    real y_mean = mean(y);
    real x_sd = sd(x);
    real y_sd = sd(y);

    if (x_sd <= 0 || y_sd <= 0) {
      reject("Gaussian_process requires non-constant x and y for standardisation.");
    }

    array[N] real x_norm = to_array_1d((x - x_mean) / x_sd);
    array[N_pred] real x_pred_norm = to_array_1d((x_pred - x_mean) / x_sd);
    vector[N] y_norm = (y - y_mean) / y_sd;

    // real fixed_nugget_sd = 0.05; // independent diagonal noise in standardised outcome units, not a shared
    real fixed_nugget_sd = 1e-4;  // a numerical jitter only (a variance of 1e-8 on the diagonal)
                                 // intercept
    vector[N] zeros = rep_vector(0, N);   // the mean of multi_normal_cholesky
}


parameters {
    real<lower=0> lengthscale;   // lengthscale parameter
    real<lower=0> sigma_f;       // signal standard deviation
    real<lower=0> sigma_n;       // noise standard deviation
}


model {
    // Covariance matrix (both diagonal terms added by add_diag) and its Cholesky factor
    matrix[N, N] L_K = cholesky_decompose(add_diag(gp_exp_quad_cov(x_norm, sigma_f, lengthscale),
                                                   square(fixed_nugget_sd) + square(sigma_n)));

    // Priors
    lengthscale ~ inv_gamma(5, 5);
    sigma_f ~ std_normal();
    sigma_n ~ std_normal();

    // Likelihood (Stan's fused multivariate normal on the Cholesky factor)
    y_norm ~ multi_normal_cholesky(zeros, L_K);
}

    // Predictions scaled back to original scale
    vector[N_pred] f_pred = gp_pred_rng(x_pred_norm, y_norm, x_norm,
                                        sigma_f, lengthscale, sigma_n, fixed_nugget_sd, 1e-9) * y_sd + y_mean;
    real sigma = sigma_n * y_sd;

// Gaussian_process_regression_chunked.stan
// Tape-chunked version of Gaussian_process_regression.stan (Gaussian process regression, marginal likelihood):
// the same log density, with the likelihood written as the sum over the observations of its terms and summed by
// reduce_sum_static, in chunks of chunk_size observations (data), so that each chunk's autodiff tape is built,
// differentiated and released before the next one (the tape-chunking paper's chunking; N_chunks from
// NicoStan::fn_compute_initial_N_chunks()).
// The likelihood of Gaussian_process_regression.stan, multi_normal_cholesky_lpdf(y_norm | 0, L_K), equals
//     sum over the observations n of  std_normal_lpdf(z[n]) - log(L_K[n, n]),   with z = L_K \ y_norm,
// since log det(L_K * L_K') = 2 * sum(log(diagonal(L_K))) and y_norm' * inverse(L_K * L_K') * y_norm = z' * z.
// Each chunk computes these terms of its observations with whole-vector operations; its observations' z and
// diagonal of L_K are the sliced argument of reduce_sum_static, packed per observation as the rows of an
// N x 2 array (column 1: z; column 2: the diagonal of L_K), so that no O(N) parameter is shared by the chunks.
// What stays on the outer tape, as whole-matrix operations (no loop over the observations), and why it cannot be
// split over the observations by reduce_sum_static, which returns only the sum of its chunks' values:
//   (1) the covariance matrix K = gp_exp_quad_cov(x_norm, sigma_f, lengthscale) plus its two diagonal terms:
//       the N x N input of the Cholesky factorisation, which needs all of it at once, and no chunk can return a
//       block of K to the outer tape;
//   (2) the Cholesky factorisation L_K of K: every column of L_K depends on every column before it;
//   (3) the forward substitution z = L_K \ y_norm: z[n] depends on z[1:(n - 1)], i.e. the block of z of each
//       chunk needs the blocks of every chunk before it.
// The priors on lengthscale, sigma_f and sigma_n (3 values) are also on the outer tape.
// The chunking data are NicoStan's for Stan models: N (the observations, the units of the chunks; already in the
// data) and chunk_size, which NicoStan sets to ceiling(N / N_chunks) in each phase (num_chunks_burnin,
// num_chunks_sampling).


// gaussian_process.stan


functions {
    vector gp_pred_rng(array[] real x2,
                       vector y1,
                       array[] real x1,
                       real sigma_f,
                       real lengthscale_f,
                       real sigma,
                       real fixed_nugget_sd,
                       real jitter) {
      int N1 = rows(y1);
      int N2 = size(x2);
      vector[N2] f2;
      {
        matrix[N1, N1] L_K;
        vector[N1] K_div_y1;
        matrix[N1, N2] k_x1_x2;
        matrix[N1, N2] v_pred;
        vector[N2] f2_mu;
        matrix[N2, N2] cov_f2;
        matrix[N1, N1] K;

        // K = gp_exp_quad_cov(x1, sigma_f, lengthscale_f);
        // for (n in 1:N1) {
        //   K[n, n] = K[n,n] + square(sigma) + square(fixed_nugget_sd);
        // }
        // (the same diagonal terms, added in the same order by add_diag, without the loop over the observations)
        K = add_diag(add_diag(gp_exp_quad_cov(x1, sigma_f, lengthscale_f), square(sigma)),
                     square(fixed_nugget_sd));
        L_K = cholesky_decompose(K);
        K_div_y1 = mdivide_left_tri_low(L_K, y1);
        K_div_y1 = mdivide_right_tri_low(K_div_y1', L_K)';
        k_x1_x2 = gp_exp_quad_cov(x1, x2, sigma_f, lengthscale_f);
        f2_mu = (k_x1_x2' * K_div_y1);
        v_pred = mdivide_left_tri_low(L_K, k_x1_x2);
        cov_f2 = gp_exp_quad_cov(x2, sigma_f, lengthscale_f) - v_pred' * v_pred;
        f2 = multi_normal_rng(f2_mu, add_diag(cov_f2, rep_vector(jitter, N2)));
      }
      return f2;
    }

    // the likelihood terms of the chunk's observations (start to end): std_normal_lpdf(z[n]) - log(L_K[n, n]),
    // from the chunk's rows of the packed N x 2 array (column 1: z; column 2: the diagonal of L_K)
    real partial_sum_observations_lpdf(array[,] real z_and_L_K_diagonal_slice, int start, int end) {
        vector[end - start + 1] z_slice = to_vector(z_and_L_K_diagonal_slice[:, 1]);
        vector[end - start + 1] L_K_diagonal_slice = to_vector(z_and_L_K_diagonal_slice[:, 2]);
        return std_normal_lupdf(z_slice) - sum(log(L_K_diagonal_slice));
    }
}


data {
    int<lower=2> N;          // at least two observations for standardisation
    vector[N] x;             // input locations
    vector[N] y;             // target variable
    int<lower=1> N_pred;     // number of prediction points
    vector[N_pred] x_pred;   // prediction input locations
    int<lower=1> chunk_size; // observations per chunk (reduce_sum_static)
}


transformed data {
    // Normalize data
    real x_mean = mean(x);
    real y_mean = mean(y);
    real x_sd = sd(x);
    real y_sd = sd(y);

    if (x_sd <= 0 || y_sd <= 0) {
      reject("Gaussian_process requires non-constant x and y for standardisation.");
    }

    array[N] real x_norm = to_array_1d((x - x_mean) / x_sd);
    array[N_pred] real x_pred_norm = to_array_1d((x_pred - x_mean) / x_sd);
    vector[N] y_norm = (y - y_mean) / y_sd;

    // real fixed_nugget_sd = 0.05; // independent diagonal noise in standardised outcome units, not a shared intercept
    real fixed_nugget_sd = 1e-4;  // a numerical jitter only (a variance of 1e-8 on the diagonal)
    // vector[N] zeros = rep_vector(0, N);
    // (zeros: the mean of multi_normal_cholesky in Gaussian_process_regression.stan; the terms of the chunks
    //  below take the mean 0 directly)
}


parameters {
    real<lower=0> lengthscale;   // lengthscale parameter
    real<lower=0> sigma_f;       // signal standard deviation
    real<lower=0> sigma_n;       // noise standard deviation
}


model {
    // Covariance matrix (both diagonal terms added by add_diag, without the N x N diag_matrix whose
    // addition made N^2 more autodiff variables; NicoStan's example, Gaussian_process.stan, kept below,
    // commented out)
    matrix[N, N] L_K = cholesky_decompose(add_diag(gp_exp_quad_cov(x_norm, sigma_f, lengthscale),
                                                   square(fixed_nugget_sd) + square(sigma_n)));
    // matrix[N, N] K = gp_exp_quad_cov(x_norm, sigma_f, lengthscale) +
    //                  diag_matrix(rep_vector(square(fixed_nugget_sd), N));
    // matrix[N, N] L_K = cholesky_decompose(add_diag(K, square(sigma_n)));

    // Priors
    lengthscale ~ inv_gamma(5, 5);
    sigma_f ~ std_normal();
    sigma_n ~ std_normal();

    // Likelihood
    // y_norm ~ multi_normal_cholesky(zeros, L_K);
    // (the same log density: the forward substitution z = L_K \ y_norm on the outer tape, then the terms
    //  std_normal_lpdf(z[n]) - log(L_K[n, n]) summed by reduce_sum_static over the observations, in chunks of
    //  chunk_size; z and the diagonal of L_K packed per observation as the rows of an N x 2 array, the sliced
    //  argument; see the header)
    {
      vector[N] z = mdivide_left_tri_low(L_K, y_norm);
      array[N, 2] real z_and_L_K_diagonal = to_array_2d(append_col(z, diagonal(L_K)));
      target += reduce_sum_static(partial_sum_observations_lupdf, z_and_L_K_diagonal, chunk_size);
    }
}


generated quantities {
    // Predictions scaled back to original scale
    vector[N_pred] f_pred = gp_pred_rng(x_pred_norm, y_norm, x_norm,
                                        sigma_f, lengthscale, sigma_n, fixed_nugget_sd, 1e-9) * y_sd + y_mean;
    real sigma = sigma_n * y_sd;
}

benchmark_models/Gaussian_process_classification_unchunked_no_loops_over_N_with_Stan_fused_functions.stan (48 lines)
// Gaussian_process_classification_unchunked_no_loops_over_N_with_Stan_fused_functions.stan
// Unchunked Stan::math version of Gaussian_process_classification_chunked (the Stan math file of
// the chunking paper's
// layout timings): the same log density as that file at N_chunks = 1, and as
// Gaussian_process_classification.stan, without reduce_sum_static. The same data (chunk_size, when it is in the data, is not read) and the same
// unconstrained parameters, in the same order and with the same names (eta, mu, lengthscale, sigma_f), as both
// files.
// Stan's fused functions: gp_exp_quad_cov for the covariance matrix, add_diag for its 1e-8 jitter,
// cholesky_decompose, and Stan's fused logistic GLM for the likelihood: the latent log-odds f = mu + L_K * eta
// are the GLM's linear predictor, with the Cholesky factor L_K as its covariates, mu as its intercept and the
// nuisance block eta as its coefficients, i.e. y ~ bernoulli_logit_glm(L_K, mu, eta), the same density as
// y ~ bernoulli_logit(mu + L_K * eta) in one node (the product, the likelihood and their gradients), in place of
// the N x N product and the N log-odds on the autodiff tape. (In the chunked file f is made on the main tape and
// sliced; the GLM needs the whole of L_K, so it has no chunked form without L_K shared by every chunk.)
// The covariance has only a 1e-8 jitter on its diagonal (its condition number can be about 1e10), so the
// gradient of the GLM's product can differ from that of L_K * eta by more than rounding at some points; its
// check is against the reference's own sensitivity to a tiny move of the point.
// No loop over N anywhere.
//
// Gaussian process classification: a Bernoulli-logit outcome y (e.g. disease status) whose log-odds is a latent
// Gaussian process f of an input x (e.g. a standardised biomarker), with a squared-exponential covariance
// (lengthscale, sigma_f) and a constant mean mu, non-centred: f = mu + L_K * eta, eta ~ N(0, I).


data {
    int<lower=1> N;                           // number of observations
    array[N] real x;                          // input (e.g. a standardised biomarker)
    array[N] int<lower=0, upper=1> y;         // binary outcome (e.g. disease status)
}


parameters {
    vector[N] eta;                            // standard normal nuisance block, declared first
    real mu;                                  // constant mean of the latent log-odds
    real<lower=0> lengthscale;                // lengthscale of the squared-exponential covariance
    real<lower=0> sigma_f;                    // marginal standard deviation of the latent log-odds
}


model {
    matrix[N, N] L_K = cholesky_decompose(add_diag(gp_exp_quad_cov(x, sigma_f, lengthscale), 1e-8));
    mu ~ normal(0, 1);
    lengthscale ~ inv_gamma(5, 5);
    sigma_f ~ normal(0, 1.5);
    eta ~ std_normal();
    // (y ~ bernoulli_logit(mu + L_K * eta), with Stan's fused logistic GLM; see the header)
    y ~ bernoulli_logit_glm(L_K, mu, eta);
}
