Run_network_meta_analysis_of_test_accuracy_Xu_fixed_cutpoints_with_MetaOrdDTA_and_NicoStan.R (173 lines)
##
## ==== Run_network_meta_analysis_of_test_accuracy_Xu_fixed_cutpoints_with_MetaOrdDTA_and_NicoStan.R ===========
##
## ---- MetaOrdDTA's network meta-analysis (NMA) of the accuracy of several ordinal diagnostic tests with multiple
##      thresholds (Nyaga et al.'s NMA model, with Xu et al.'s fixed cutpoints: one set of cutpoints per test and
##      disease class, shared by every study), fitted by NicoStan to simulated data:
##        - 4 ordinal anxiety screening tests (GAD-2, GAD-7, HADS and BAI), 80 studies, each with 1 to 3 of them;
##        - at each threshold of each test, the number of non-diseased and of diseased patients above it, with
##          the thresholds a study did not report coded -1 ("missing thresholds", which the model handles);
##        - simulated with MetaOrdDTA's own simulator (R_fn_sim_NMA_data_with_covariates_varying()), from a
##          realistic design.
## ---- MetaOrdDTA prepares the data and the priors (exactly as it gives them to Stan), and NicoStan fits its Stan
##      model, unchanged. Step by step:
##        (a) how the priors are set;
##        (b) how the nuisance parameters are given;
##        (c) the initial values of the burn-in chains;
##        (d) the layouts (no reduce_sum() here, hence one thread per chain and no chunks);
##        (e) the fit and its summaries.
##
## Usage:  Rscript Run_network_meta_analysis_of_test_accuracy_Xu_fixed_cutpoints_with_MetaOrdDTA_and_NicoStan.R
##         (or source() it; the settings and the priors are in the two blocks below; MetaOrdDTA is needed)
##
##
## ------- Settings:  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
##
{
      seed                          <-  123
      n_burnin                      <-  500
      n_iter                        <-  500
      n_chains_burnin               <-  4
}
##
##
## ------- The priors (MetaOrdDTA's defaults for this model, written out so that they can be changed):  ----------
##
{
      ## (a normal prior on each test's mean location in each class, beta_mu: mean 0, SD 1)
      prior_mean_of_each_beta_mu         <-  0
      prior_SD_of_each_beta_mu           <-  1
      ## (half-normal priors on the between-study SDs: beta_sigma, shared by the tests, and beta_tau, per test)
      prior_SD_of_each_beta_sigma        <-  1
      prior_SD_of_each_beta_tau          <-  1
      ## (an LKJ prior on the between-study correlation of the two classes, within its bounds)
      prior_LKJ_eta_of_beta_corr         <-  2
      ## (the induced Dirichlet prior on the cutpoints of each test and class, with every alpha equal to 1)
      prior_Dirichlet_alpha              <-  1
}
##
##
## ------- The simulated data:  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
##
simulated_NMA_data <-  readRDS(system.file("examples", "data",
                                           paste0("simulated_network_meta_analysis_of_four_ordinal_screening_",
                                                  "tests_with_missing_thresholds.rds"),
                                           package = "NicoStan"))
## (x[[t]][[c]]: test t, class c (1 = non-diseased, 2 = diseased), one row per study; its first column is the
##  number of patients of the class, the others the number above each threshold, -1 when it was not reported)
x <-  lapply(simulated_NMA_data$x, unname)
indicator_index_test_in_study <-  simulated_NMA_data$indicator_index_test_in_study
n_studies <-  simulated_NMA_data$n_studies
message(paste0("\033[36m", "Simulated NMA data: ", n_studies, " studies; studies per test (",
               paste0(simulated_NMA_data$names_of_the_index_tests, collapse = ", "), "): ",
               paste0(colSums(indicator_index_test_in_study), collapse = ", "), "\033[0m"))
##
##
## ---- MetaOrdDTA's data list and priors for this model (Xu, fixed cutpoints, intercept only), exactly as it
##      gives them to Stan; nothing is compiled or fitted by MetaOrdDTA here: ----------------------------------
##
model_MetaOrdDTA <-  MetaOrdDTA::MetaOrd_model$new(x                              = x,
                                                   indicator_index_test_in_study  = indicator_index_test_in_study,
                                                   intercept_only                 = TRUE,
                                                   network                        = TRUE,
                                                   model_parameterisation         = "Xu",
                                                   random_thresholds              = FALSE,
                                                   Dirichlet_random_effects_type  = "fixed",
                                                   n_chains                       = n_chains_burnin,
                                                   compile                        = FALSE)
##
## ---- (a) The priors: the Stan model's model block sets them, and their values are passed to it as data:
##
##          beta_mu[t][c, ] ~ normal(prior_beta_mu_mean[t][c, ], prior_beta_mu_SD[t][c, ]);
##          beta_sigma[c] ~ normal(0, prior_beta_sigma_SD[c]);           (half-normal: beta_sigma >= 0)
##          to_vector(beta_tau_raw) ~ normal(0, to_vector(prior_beta_tau_SD));   (half-normal)
##          beta_L_Omega ~ lkj_corr_cholesky(prior_beta_corr_LKJ);
##          Ind_Dir_ord_prob ~ induced_dirichlet_given_C(C_vec_t, prior_dirichlet_alpha[c][t, ], ...);
##      (to change a prior's form, edit the model block; to change its values, edit the priors block above)
priors <-  model_MetaOrdDTA$priors
for (t in seq_along(priors$prior_beta_mu_mean)) {
      priors$prior_beta_mu_mean[[t]][] <-  prior_mean_of_each_beta_mu
      priors$prior_beta_mu_SD[[t]][] <-  prior_SD_of_each_beta_mu
}
priors$prior_beta_sigma_SD[] <-  prior_SD_of_each_beta_sigma
priors$prior_beta_tau_SD[] <-  prior_SD_of_each_beta_tau
priors$prior_beta_corr_LKJ <-  prior_LKJ_eta_of_beta_corr
## (one matrix per class, tests x categories, as the Stan model declares it: array[2] matrix[...] (older
##  MetaOrdDTA installs give a single matrix here))
n_thr_max <-  model_MetaOrdDTA$internal_obj$outs_data$stan_data_list$n_thr_max
alpha_of_each_class <-  matrix(prior_Dirichlet_alpha, nrow = length(x), ncol = n_thr_max + 1)
priors$prior_dirichlet_alpha <-  list(alpha_of_each_class, alpha_of_each_class)
## (the data list, then the priors, with the names given twice kept once, as MetaOrdDTA does)
Stan_data_list <-  MetaOrdDTA:::R_fn_remove_duplicates_from_list(c(model_MetaOrdDTA$internal_obj$outs_data$
                                                                       stan_data_list,
                                                                   priors))
## (the model's 0 / 1 switches as numbers: MetaOrdDTA keeps them as TRUE / FALSE, which cmdstanr writes as
##  1 / 0, whereas the JSON NicoStan writes for BridgeStan keeps true / false, which Stan's int data refuse)
for (name_of_switch in c("softplus", "hetero_sigma", "compound_symmetry")) {
      Stan_data_list[[name_of_switch]] <-  as.integer(Stan_data_list[[name_of_switch]])
}
##
## ---- MetaOrdDTA's Stan model (unchanged) and the folder of its #include files, copied to a writable folder
##      (NicoStan compiles it next to its .stan file):
Stan_model_folder <-  file.path(tempdir(), "MetaOrdDTA_NMA_Xu_fixed_cutpoints")
dir.create(Stan_model_folder, showWarnings = FALSE)
Stan_model_file_path <-  file.path(Stan_model_folder, "DTA_NMA_Nyaga_Xu_FIXEDthr.stan")
file.copy(from = system.file("stan_models", "stan_models_NMA", "DTA_NMA_Nyaga_Xu_FIXEDthr.stan",
                             package = "MetaOrdDTA"),
          to = Stan_model_file_path, overwrite = TRUE)
Stan_functions_folder <-  system.file("stan_functions", package = "MetaOrdDTA")
##
## ---- (b) The nuisance parameters: the two blocks of standard-normal between-study values of the Stan model,
##          matrix[2, n_studies] beta_eta_z;               (each study's effect in each class)
##          array[2] vector[n_total_obs] beta_delta_z_vec;  (each study-test pair's effect in each class)
##      with n_total_obs the number of study-test pairs, given to NicoStan by name with nuisance_params (NicoStan
##      never chooses the nuisance blocks itself). NicoStan writes the model's version with the two blocks held
##      by NicoStan (DTA_NMA_Nyaga_Xu_FIXEDthr_reduce_sum_chunked.stan, next to the model; the rest of the model
##      unchanged), and samples them with diffusion-pathspace HMC (diffusion_HMC = TRUE in $sample()), and the
##      main parameters with standard HMC.
n_total_obs <-  sum(indicator_index_test_in_study)
n_nuisance <-  2 * n_studies + 2 * n_total_obs
model_NicoStan <-  NicoStan::Nico_model$new(Model_type            = "Stan",
                                            Stan_data_list        = Stan_data_list,
                                            Stan_model_file_path  = Stan_model_file_path,
                                            stanc_args            = list(paste0("--include-paths=",
                                                                                Stan_functions_folder)),
                                            nuisance_params       = c("beta_eta_z", "beta_delta_z_vec"),
                                            ## n_nuisance_override   = n_nuisance,
                                            sample_nuisance       = TRUE)
message(paste0("\033[36m", "Nuisance parameters given to NicoStan: ", n_nuisance, " (2 x ", n_studies,
               " studies + 2 x ", n_total_obs, " study-test pairs)", "\033[0m"))
##
## ---- (c) The initial values of the burn-in chains, by name (the nuisance blocks at 0, i.e. every study at the
##      average; the cutpoints' raw values at 0; the SDs and the correlation small):
n_index_tests <-  length(x)
initial_values_NicoStan <-  rep(list(list(beta_eta_z        = matrix(0, nrow = 2, ncol = n_studies),
                                          beta_delta_z_vec  = list(rep(0, n_total_obs), rep(0, n_total_obs)),
                                          beta_mu           = rep(list(matrix(0, nrow = 2, ncol = 1)),
                                                                  n_index_tests),
                                          C_raw_vec         = list(rep(0, sum(Stan_data_list$n_thr)),
                                                                   rep(0, sum(Stan_data_list$n_thr))),
                                          beta_sigma        = c(0.25, 0.25),
                                          beta_tau_raw      = matrix(0.25, nrow = n_index_tests, ncol = 2),
                                          beta_corr         = 0)),
                                n_chains_burnin)
##
## ---- (d) The layouts: this model has no reduce_sum() (its N is the number of studies, which is small), so
##      every chain runs on one thread, without chunks (n_threads_WCP = 1, num_chunks = 1), and NicoStan runs one
##      chain per CPU in the sampling. For a model whose likelihood is in reduce_sum() chunks, see worked example
##      3, where NicoStan finds the optimal within-chain threads (WCP) and N_chunks of the burn-in and of the
##      sampling by itself, from the L2 and L3 caches of the computer.
##
## ---- (e) The fit.
##      Note: if you leave the layouts out (or set them to NULL), NicoStan will find them for you, as long as
##      your model uses reduce_sum() or is a built-in BayesMVP model.
model_NicoStan$sample(init_lists_per_chain     = initial_values_NicoStan,
                      n_burnin                 = n_burnin,
                      n_iter                   = n_iter,
                      n_chains_burnin          = n_chains_burnin,
                      burnin_algorithm         = "CHESSR",
                      diffusion_HMC            = TRUE,
                      partitioned_HMC          = FALSE,
                      seed                     = seed)
fit_summary <-  model_NicoStan$summary(save_log_lik_trace = FALSE)
print(fit_summary$get_summary_main(), n = 50)

Run_one_class_MVOP_with_the_fused_GHK_log_likelihood_and_BayesMVP.R (346 lines)
##
## ==== Run_one_class_MVOP_with_the_fused_GHK_log_likelihood_and_BayesMVP.R ====================================
##
## ---- The one-class multivariate ordered probit (MVOP) model, fitted to the real NHANES data twice:
##
##      (1) as a Stan model with NicoSIMD's fused GHK log likelihood
##          (models/one_class_MVOP_with_the_fused_GHK_log_likelihood.stan), by NicoStan, on any CPU with AVX-512,
##          AVX2 or NEON (e.g. Apple Silicon Macs, through SIMDe);
##      (2) by BayesMVP's built-in MVOP model, whose gradients are derived by hand (manual gradients).
##      Both have the same priors (BayesMVP's MVOP priors, with the values below), hence the same posterior;
##      their posterior means of the correlation matrix are printed side by side at the end.
##
## ---- Each part shows, step by step:
##
##        (a) how the priors are set;
##        (b) how the nuisance parameters are given;
##        (c) the initial values of the burn-in chains;
##        (d) how the package finds the optimal within-chain threads (WCP) and N_chunks of the burn-in and of the
##            sampling by itself, from the L2 and L3 caches of the computer it runs on (the tape-chunking paper's equations, then
##            a short timed check of the layouts around them), and how they are carried into $sample();
##        (e) the fit and its summaries.
## ---- The data: the 9575 US adults of NHANES I (the NHANES data of the hexbin package), with 4 outcomes, each
##      with its OWN covariates, and every missing result coded -1 (handled by the GHK method):
##        iron deficiency (transferrin saturation below 16%), low albumin (below 3.5 g/dL) and cancer (binary);
##        anaemia (ordinal: the WHO categories of haemoglobin for each sex, none / mild / moderate / severe).
##
## Usage:  Rscript Run_one_class_MVOP_with_the_fused_GHK_log_likelihood_and_BayesMVP.R
##         (or source() it; the settings and the priors are in the two blocks below; BayesMVP is needed for
##          part (2) only)
##
##
## ------- Settings:  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
##
{
      seed                          <-  123
      n_burnin                      <-  500
      n_iter                        <-  500
      n_chains_burnin               <-  4
      fit_with_BayesMVP_too         <-  TRUE
}
##
##
## ------- The priors (the same in both parts, hence the same posterior):  ---------------------------------------
##
{
      ## (an LKJ prior on the correlation matrix Omega of the latent values; 2 is BayesMVP's default)
      prior_LKJ_eta                         <-  2
      ## (a normal prior on every coefficient: mean 0; SD 2.5 for the intercepts, since the outcomes are rare
      ##  (e.g. low albumin in 0.6% of people, i.e. an intercept near -2.5 on the probit scale), and SD 1 for
      ##  every other coefficient)
      prior_mean_of_each_coefficient        <-  0
      prior_SD_of_each_intercept            <-  2.5
      prior_SD_of_each_other_coefficient    <-  1
      ## (the induced Dirichlet prior on the cutpoints of each ordinal outcome, with every alpha equal to 1)
      prior_Dirichlet_alpha                 <-  1
      ## (the bounds of the first cutpoint, and of the logs of the gaps between the cutpoints)
      C_raw_lower                           <-  -10
      C_raw_upper                           <-  2.5
}
##
##
## ------- The outcomes and covariates of the real NHANES data:  -------------------------------------------------
##
utils::data(NHANES, package = "hexbin")
N <-  nrow(NHANES)
female <-  as.numeric(NHANES$Sex == "F")
##
## ---- Anaemia (the WHO categories for each sex): 1 = none, 2 = mild, 3 = moderate, 4 = severe:
##
cut_off_of_anaemia <-  ifelse(female == 1, 12, 13)
anaemia <-  ifelse(NHANES$Hemoglobin >= cut_off_of_anaemia, 1,
                   ifelse(NHANES$Hemoglobin >= 11, 2,
                          ifelse(NHANES$Hemoglobin >= 8, 3, 4)))
##
## ---- The binary outcomes (first), then anaemia; every missing result coded -1:
##
iron_deficiency <-  as.numeric(NHANES$Transferin < 16)
low_albumin <-  as.numeric(NHANES$Albumin < 3.5)
cancer <-  as.numeric(NHANES$Cancer.Incidence == "Yes")
y <-  cbind(iron_deficiency, low_albumin, cancer, anaemia)
y[is.na(y)] <-  -1
storage.mode(y) <-  "integer"
n_tests <-  ncol(y)
test_is_binary <-  c(1, 1, 1, 0)
n_categories_of_test <-  c(2, 2, 2, 4)
##
## ---- The covariates (age per 10 years from 50, weight per 10 kg from 75 kg (BMI is missing for most people),
##      smoking against never smoked, and the 0 / 1 codes of education and race):
X_all <-  cbind(intercept                 = 1,
                age_per_10_years_from_50  = (NHANES$Age - 50) / 10,
                female                    = female,
                weight_per_10_kg_from_75  = (NHANES$Weight - 75) / 10,
                current_smoker            = as.numeric(NHANES$Smoke == "Current"),
                past_smoker               = as.numeric(NHANES$Smoke == "Past"),
                smoking_unknown           = as.numeric(NHANES$Smoke == "Unknown"),
                education                 = NHANES$Ed,
                race                      = NHANES$Race)
stopifnot(!anyNA(X_all))
n_covariates_max <-  ncol(X_all)
##
## ---- Each outcome's own covariates (in the first columns of its X matrix, the rest 0):
##
smoking <-  c("current_smoker", "past_smoker", "smoking_unknown")
covariates_of_each_outcome <-  list(
      iron_deficiency = c("intercept", "age_per_10_years_from_50", "female", "weight_per_10_kg_from_75",
                          "race", "education"),
      low_albumin     = c("intercept", "age_per_10_years_from_50", "female", "weight_per_10_kg_from_75",
                          smoking, "education"),
      cancer          = c("intercept", "age_per_10_years_from_50", "female", "weight_per_10_kg_from_75",
                          smoking, "race"),
      anaemia         = c("intercept", "age_per_10_years_from_50", "female", "weight_per_10_kg_from_75",
                          smoking, "race", "education"))
X_of_each_outcome <-  list()
for (t in 1:n_tests) {
      covariates_t <-  covariates_of_each_outcome[[t]]
      X_t <-  matrix(0, nrow = N, ncol = n_covariates_max)
      X_t[, seq_along(covariates_t)] <-  X_all[, covariates_t]
      X_of_each_outcome[[t]] <-  X_t
}
n_covariates_of_test <-  as.numeric(lengths(covariates_of_each_outcome))
message(paste0("\033[36m", "NHANES: N = ", N, "; missing results of each outcome: ",
               paste0(colSums(y == -1), collapse = ", "), "\033[0m"))
##
## ---- The priors of the coefficients, as matrices (covariates x outcomes; the intercepts in the first row):
##
prior_beta_mean <-  matrix(prior_mean_of_each_coefficient, nrow = n_covariates_max, ncol = n_tests)
prior_beta_sd <-  matrix(prior_SD_of_each_other_coefficient, nrow = n_covariates_max, ncol = n_tests)
prior_beta_sd[1, ] <-  prior_SD_of_each_intercept
##
## ---- The initial values of the cutpoints of anaemia (the first cutpoint, then the logs of the 2 gaps):
##
C_raw_initial <-  c(1.0, log(0.5), log(1.5))
##
##
## ------- (1) The Stan model with NicoSIMD's fused GHK log likelihood, by NicoStan:  ----------------------------
##
## ---- NicoSIMD gives the user header and build arguments of this CPU (AVX-512, AVX2, or NEON on 64-bit ARM):
##
NicoSIMD_build <-  NicoSIMD::fn_include_folder_Stan_user_header_and_build_arguments_of_NicoSIMD_for_this_CPU()
message(paste0("\033[36m", "NicoSIMD's functions on this CPU: ", NicoSIMD_build$instruction_set, "\033[0m"))
##
## ---- The Stan model, copied to a writable folder (it is compiled next to its .stan file):
##
Stan_model_file_path <-  file.path(tempdir(), "one_class_MVOP_with_the_fused_GHK_log_likelihood.stan")
file.copy(from = system.file("examples", "models", "one_class_MVOP_with_the_fused_GHK_log_likelihood.stan",
                             package = "NicoStan"),
          to = Stan_model_file_path, overwrite = TRUE)
##
## ---- (1a) The priors: the Stan model's model block sets them, and their values are passed to it as data:
##
##          beta_vec ~ normal(prior_beta_mean_vec, prior_beta_sd_vec);   (prior_beta_mean, prior_beta_sd)
##          L_Omega ~ lkj_corr_cholesky(prior_LKJ_eta);                   (prior_LKJ_eta)
##          target += induced_Dirichlet_probit_lpdf(the cutpoints of each ordinal outcome |
##                                                  rep_vector(prior_Dirichlet_alpha, ...), ...);
##      (to change a prior's form, edit the model block; to change its values, edit the priors block above)
Stan_data_list <-  list(N                      = N,
                        n_tests                = n_tests,
                        test_is_binary         = test_is_binary,
                        n_categories_of_test   = n_categories_of_test,
                        y                      = y,
                        n_covariates_max       = n_covariates_max,
                        n_covariates_of_test   = n_covariates_of_test,
                        X                      = X_of_each_outcome,
                        ## (the priors' values)
                        prior_beta_mean        = prior_beta_mean,
                        prior_beta_sd          = prior_beta_sd,
                        prior_LKJ_eta          = prior_LKJ_eta,
                        prior_Dirichlet_alpha  = prior_Dirichlet_alpha,
                        C_raw_lower            = C_raw_lower,
                        C_raw_upper            = C_raw_upper,
                        ## (Phi_type 1: the exact normal CDF; the bounds of the log-scale tails)
                        Phi_type               = 1,
                        overflow_threshold     = 7.5,
                        underflow_threshold    = -7.5,
                        ## (NicoStan's reduce_sum data: N and chunk_size, which NicoStan sets for each layout)
                        chunk_size             = N)
##
## ---- (1b) The nuisance parameters: u_raw, the N x n_tests GHK values (one per subject and outcome), declared in
##      the parameters block of the Stan model,
##          array[N] row_vector[n_tests] u_raw;
##      and given to NicoStan by name with nuisance_params (any number of nuisance blocks may be given, e.g.
##      nuisance_params = c("z_intercept", "z_slope")). NicoStan samples them with diffusion-pathspace HMC
##      (diffusion_HMC = TRUE in $sample()), and the main parameters with standard HMC; as u_raw is the sliced
##      argument of the model's reduce_sum_static, NicoStan holds its values inside the chunks
##      (reduce_sum_chunked). (NicoStan never chooses the nuisance blocks itself: they are always named.)
model_NicoStan <-  NicoStan::Nico_model$new(Model_type            = "Stan",
                                            Stan_data_list        = Stan_data_list,
                                            Stan_model_file_path  = Stan_model_file_path,
                                            Stan_cpp_user_header  = NicoSIMD_build$Stan_user_header,
                                            make_args             = NicoSIMD_build$make_args,
                                            nuisance_params       = "u_raw",
                                            sample_nuisance       = TRUE)
##
## ---- (1c) The initial values of the burn-in chains (u_raw as an N x n_tests matrix, one row per subject):
##
initial_values_NicoStan <-  rep(list(list(u_raw     = matrix(0, nrow = N, ncol = n_tests),
                                          beta_vec  = rep(0, sum(n_covariates_of_test)),
                                          L_Omega   = diag(n_tests),
                                          C_raw     = C_raw_initial)), n_chains_burnin)
##
## ---- (1d) The optimal within-chain threads (WCP) and N_chunks of the burn-in and of the sampling, found by
##      NicoStan from the L2 and L3 caches of this computer (Cache-aware chunking dramatically improves parallel scaling for HMC: Application to multivariate probit model (in preparation) equations), then checked by timing a few
##      layouts around them (the tape-chunking paper's check), within a budget of 2000 of the model's own gradient evaluations:
layouts_NicoStan <-
      NicoStan::fn_compute_burnin_and_sampling_layouts_of_Stan_model_within_a_budget_of_lp_grad_calls(
            model_so_file    = model_NicoStan$init_object$model_so_file,
            Stan_data_list   = Stan_data_list,
            init_object      = model_NicoStan$init_object,
            n_chains_burnin  = n_chains_burnin)
message(paste0("\033[36m", "NicoStan's layouts (found in ",
               round(layouts_NicoStan$seconds_spent_choosing_the_burnin_and_sampling_layouts, 1), " s):",
               " burn-in ", n_chains_burnin, " chains x ", layouts_NicoStan$n_threads_WCP_burnin,
               " threads per chain, N_chunks = ", layouts_NicoStan$num_chunks_burnin,
               "; sampling ", layouts_NicoStan$n_chains_sampling, " chains x ",
               layouts_NicoStan$n_threads_WCP_sampling, " threads per chain, N_chunks = ",
               layouts_NicoStan$num_chunks_sampling, "\033[0m"))
##
## ---- (1e) The fit, with these layouts carried over into $sample().
##      Note: if you leave these out (or set them to NULL), NicoStan will find them for you, as long as your
##      model uses reduce_sum() (with N and chunk_size in its data) or is a built-in BayesMVP model.
model_NicoStan$sample(init_lists_per_chain     = initial_values_NicoStan,
                      n_burnin                 = n_burnin,
                      n_iter                   = n_iter,
                      n_chains_burnin          = n_chains_burnin,
                      burnin_algorithm         = "CHESSR",
                      diffusion_HMC            = TRUE,
                      partitioned_HMC          = FALSE,
                      n_threads_WCP_burnin     = layouts_NicoStan$n_threads_WCP_burnin,
                      num_chunks_burnin        = layouts_NicoStan$num_chunks_burnin,
                      n_chains_sampling        = layouts_NicoStan$n_chains_sampling,
                      n_threads_WCP_sampling   = layouts_NicoStan$n_threads_WCP_sampling,
                      num_chunks_sampling      = layouts_NicoStan$num_chunks_sampling,
                      seed                     = seed)
fit_summary_NicoStan <-  model_NicoStan$summary(save_log_lik_trace = FALSE)
print(fit_summary_NicoStan$get_summary_main(), n = 50)
print(fit_summary_NicoStan$get_summary_transformed(), n = 50)
##
##
## ------- (2) The same model by BayesMVP's built-in MVOP (manual gradients):  -----------------------------------
##
if (fit_with_BayesMVP_too) {
      ##
      ## ---- (2a) The priors: BayesMVP's MVOP takes them in model_args_list (each a list with one element per
      ##      latent class; one class here): prior_coeffs_mean_mat and prior_coeffs_sd_mat (covariates x
      ##      outcomes), lkj_cholesky_eta (one per class), prior_dirichlet_alpha (categories x ordinal outcomes),
      ##      and the bounds C_raw_lower and C_raw_upper; the same values as in part (1):
      model_args_list <-  list(y                             = y,
                               n_cat_per_ord_test            = 4,
                               X                             = list(X_of_each_outcome),
                               n_covariates_per_outcome_mat  = matrix(n_covariates_of_test, nrow = 1),
                               ## (the priors)
                               prior_coeffs_mean_mat         = list(prior_beta_mean),
                               prior_coeffs_sd_mat           = list(prior_beta_sd),
                               lkj_cholesky_eta              = matrix(prior_LKJ_eta, nrow = 1, ncol = 1),
                               prior_dirichlet_alpha         = list(matrix(prior_Dirichlet_alpha, nrow = 4,
                                                                           ncol = 1)),
                               C_raw_lower                   = C_raw_lower,
                               C_raw_upper                   = C_raw_upper,
                               ## (Phi_type "Phi": the exact normal CDF)
                               Phi_type                      = "Phi")
      ##
      ## ---- (2b) The nuisance parameters: BayesMVP's MVOP has them built in (u_raw, the N x n_tests GHK values);
      ##      sample_nuisance = TRUE samples them with diffusion-pathspace HMC, as in part (1):
      model_BayesMVP <-  BayesMVP::MVP_model$new(Model_type       = "MVOP",
                                                 model_args_list  = model_args_list,
                                                 sample_nuisance  = TRUE)
      ##
      ## ---- (2c) The same initial values (BayesMVP's cutpoints are unconstrained by tanh, between the bounds):
##
      C_unc_initial <-  atanh(2 * (C_raw_initial - C_raw_lower) / (C_raw_upper - C_raw_lower) - 1)
      initial_values_BayesMVP <-  rep(list(list(u_raw                    = matrix(0, nrow = N, ncol = n_tests),
                                                beta                     = list(prior_beta_mean),
                                                Omega_unconstrained_vec  = list(rep(0, choose(n_tests, 2))),
                                                C_unc_vec                = list(C_unc_initial))),
                                      n_chains_burnin)
      ##
      ## ---- (2d) The optimal within-chain threads (WCP) and N_chunks of the burn-in and of the sampling,
      ##      found by BayesMVP from the L2 and L3 caches of this computer (the tape-chunking paper's equations for a manual
      ##      gradient), then checked by timing a few layouts around them (the tape-chunking paper's check):
      burnin_layout_BayesMVP <-  BayesMVP::fn_compute_burnin_n_threads_WCP_and_num_chunks_for_BayesMVP_model(
                                       Model_type       = "MVOP",
                                       init_object      = model_BayesMVP$init_object,
                                       n_chains_burnin  = n_chains_burnin)
      sampling_layout_BayesMVP <-
            BayesMVP::fn_compute_sampling_n_chains_n_threads_WCP_and_num_chunks_for_BayesMVP_model(
                  Model_type   = "MVOP",
                  init_object  = model_BayesMVP$init_object)
      message(paste0("\033[36m", "BayesMVP's layouts: burn-in ", n_chains_burnin, " chains x ",
                     burnin_layout_BayesMVP$n_threads_WCP_burnin, " threads per chain, N_chunks = ",
                     burnin_layout_BayesMVP$num_chunks_burnin, " (found in ",
                     round(burnin_layout_BayesMVP$seconds_spent_choosing, 1), " s); sampling ",
                     sampling_layout_BayesMVP$n_chains_sampling, " chains x ",
                     sampling_layout_BayesMVP$n_threads_WCP_sampling, " threads per chain, N_chunks = ",
                     sampling_layout_BayesMVP$num_chunks_sampling, " (found in ",
                     round(sampling_layout_BayesMVP$seconds_spent_choosing, 1), " s)", "\033[0m"))
      ##
      ## ---- (2e) The fit, with these layouts carried over into $sample().
      ##      Note: if you leave these out (or set them to NULL), NicoStan will find them for you, as long as your
      ##      model uses reduce_sum() (with N and chunk_size in its data) or is a built-in BayesMVP model.
      model_BayesMVP$sample(init_lists_per_chain     = initial_values_BayesMVP,
                            n_burnin                 = n_burnin,
                            n_iter                   = n_iter,
                            n_chains_burnin          = n_chains_burnin,
                            burnin_algorithm         = "CHESSR",
                            diffusion_HMC            = TRUE,
                            partitioned_HMC          = FALSE,
                            n_threads_WCP_burnin     = burnin_layout_BayesMVP$n_threads_WCP_burnin,
                            num_chunks_burnin        = burnin_layout_BayesMVP$num_chunks_burnin,
                            n_chains_sampling        = sampling_layout_BayesMVP$n_chains_sampling,
                            n_threads_WCP_sampling   = sampling_layout_BayesMVP$n_threads_WCP_sampling,
                            num_chunks_sampling      = sampling_layout_BayesMVP$num_chunks_sampling,
                            seed                     = seed,
                            reorder_cols_MVP         = FALSE)
      fit_summary_BayesMVP <-  model_BayesMVP$summary(save_log_lik_trace = FALSE)
      print(fit_summary_BayesMVP$get_summary_main(), n = 50)
      ##
      ## ---- The posterior means of the correlation matrix, side by side (they should agree within MCMC error):
##
      ##      the rows of the summaries named Omega[..., t1, t2], whatever their first indices
      fn_posterior_mean_of_the_correlation_matrix <-  function(summary_tibble,
                                                               n_tests) {

              rows_of_Omega <-  grepl(pattern = "^Omega\\[", x = summary_tibble$parameter)
              indices_of_each_row <-  regmatches(summary_tibble$parameter[rows_of_Omega],
                                                 gregexpr(pattern = "[0-9]+",
                                                          text = summary_tibble$parameter[rows_of_Omega]))
              posterior_mean_of_Omega <-  matrix(NA, nrow = n_tests, ncol = n_tests)
              for (r in seq_along(indices_of_each_row)) {
                    t1_t2 <-  as.numeric(utils::tail(indices_of_each_row[[r]], 2))
                    posterior_mean_of_Omega[t1_t2[1], t1_t2[2]] <-  summary_tibble$mean[rows_of_Omega][r]
              }
              dimnames(posterior_mean_of_Omega) <-  list(colnames(y), colnames(y))
              return(posterior_mean_of_Omega)
      }

      summary_of_NicoStan <-  rbind(fit_summary_NicoStan$get_summary_main(),
                                    fit_summary_NicoStan$get_summary_transformed(),
                                    fit_summary_NicoStan$get_summary_generated_quantities())
      summary_of_BayesMVP <-  rbind(fit_summary_BayesMVP$get_summary_main(),
                                    fit_summary_BayesMVP$get_summary_transformed(),
                                    fit_summary_BayesMVP$get_summary_generated_quantities())
      message("\033[32m", "Posterior means of the correlation matrix, NicoStan (fused GHK):", "\033[0m")
      print(round(fn_posterior_mean_of_the_correlation_matrix(summary_of_NicoStan, n_tests), 3))
      message("\033[32m", "Posterior means of the correlation matrix, BayesMVP (manual gradients):", "\033[0m")
      print(round(fn_posterior_mean_of_the_correlation_matrix(summary_of_BayesMVP, n_tests), 3))
}

#### =====================================================================================================================================
## robust_t4: three sample sizes, common data/initial values, and main-parameter efficiency benchmarks.
## Source this file in R or run with Rscript. Edit the settings below for the research run.
##
model <-  "robust_t4"
N_values <-  c(250, 1000, 3000)
profile <-  Sys.getenv("NICOSTAN_EXAMPLE_PROFILE", unset = "analysis")
burnin_algorithm <-  "CHESSR"
##
## Resolve this example folder without changing the working directory.
.example_sources <-  as.character(unlist(lapply(sys.frames(), function(frame) frame$ofile)))
if (!length(.example_sources)) .example_sources <-  sub("^--file=", "", commandArgs()[startsWith(commandArgs(), "--file=")])
if (!length(.example_sources)) stop("Source this file or run it with Rscript.")
.example_directory <-  dirname(normalizePath(tail(.example_sources, 1), mustWork = TRUE))
## Select a separate library only when explicitly requested.
.example_library <-  Sys.getenv("NICOSTAN_EXAMPLE_R_LIB", unset = "")
if (nzchar(.example_library)) {

        if ("NicoStan" %in% loadedNamespaces() &&
            normalizePath(getNamespaceInfo(asNamespace("NicoStan"), "path")) !=
            normalizePath(file.path(.example_library, "NicoStan"), mustWork = FALSE)) {
                stop("Restart R before selecting a different NicoStan library.")
        }
        .libPaths(c(.example_library, .libPaths()))
}

source(file.path(.example_directory, "NicoStan_examples.R"))
source(file.path(.example_directory, "NicoStan_benchmarks.R"))
##
## On AVX-512 hardware this gives CmdStanR, NicoStan, and NicoStan + AVX-512.
## On AVX2-only hardware the third arm uses AVX2 and is labelled accordingly.
benchmark_arms <-  NicoStan_benchmark_arms()
if (identical(NicoStan_benchmark_cpu_has_isa("AVX512"), FALSE)) {
        benchmark_arms <-  benchmark_arms[benchmark_arms$math_backend != "AVX512", ]
        if (isTRUE(NicoStan_benchmark_cpu_has_isa("AVX2"))) {
                avx2 <-  NicoStan_benchmark_arms(include_avx2 = TRUE)
                benchmark_arms <-  rbind(benchmark_arms, avx2[avx2$math_backend == "AVX2", ])
        }
        message("AVX-512 is unavailable on this CPU; the arm table records the supported comparisons.")
}
benchmark_result <-  NicoStan_benchmark_run(models = model, N_grid = setNames(list(N_values), model),
    arms = benchmark_arms, include_avx2 = any(benchmark_arms$math_backend == "AVX2"), profile = profile,
    burnin_algorithm = burnin_algorithm, validate = profile == "smoke",
    output_dir = file.path(getwd(), paste0("NicoStan_benchmark_", model)),
    model_dir = file.path(.example_directory, "models"))
benchmark_result$comparison$efficiency

## Synthetic four-class LC-MVOP example for NicoStan.
##
## This runtime example uses text fixtures, the bundled Stan sources, and the
## portable AVX headers. It never reads or copies clinical data.

four_class_example_paths <- function(
    analysis_directory = file.path(getwd(), "Alg_paper_analysis"),
    example_directory = NULL) {

    if (!is.null(example_directory)) {
        example_directory <- normalizePath(example_directory, mustWork = FALSE)
        model_directory <- file.path(example_directory, "models")
        fixture_directory <- file.path(example_directory, "fixture")
        return(list(
            example_directory = example_directory,
            paper3_directory = dirname(dirname(example_directory)),
            validation_directory = dirname(example_directory),
            fixture_directory = fixture_directory,
            runtime_directory = model_directory,
            source_Stan_math = file.path(model_directory, "four_class_Stan_math.stan"),
            source_avx = file.path(model_directory, "four_class_avx.stan"),
            source_fused = file.path(model_directory, "four_class_avx_fused.stan"),
            fixture_file = file.path(fixture_directory, "fixture.R"),
            fixture_json = file.path(fixture_directory, "data_current.json"),
            init_directory = file.path(fixture_directory, "initial_values")
        ))
    }
    paper3_directory <- normalizePath(file.path(analysis_directory, "paper_3_general_sampler"),
                                      mustWork = FALSE)
    validation_directory <- file.path(paper3_directory, "validation")
    fixture_directory <- file.path(validation_directory, "four_class_fixture")
    runtime_directory <- file.path(validation_directory, "four_class_runtime")
    list(
        example_directory = file.path(paper3_directory, "four_class"),
        paper3_directory = paper3_directory,
        validation_directory = validation_directory,
        fixture_directory = fixture_directory,
        runtime_directory = runtime_directory,
        source_Stan_math = file.path(runtime_directory, "four_class_Stan_math.stan"),
        source_avx = file.path(runtime_directory, "four_class_avx.stan"),
        source_fused = file.path(runtime_directory, "four_class_avx_fused.stan"),
        fixture_file = file.path(fixture_directory, "fixture.R"),
        fixture_json = file.path(fixture_directory, "data_current.json"),
        init_directory = file.path(fixture_directory, "initial_values_current")
    )
}


four_class_add_current_data_fields <- function(stan_data) {

    stopifnot(is.list(stan_data), identical(as.integer(stan_data$n_class), 4L))
    ## Current four-class source requires these fields even when the optional OR
    ## parameterisation and generated-quantity diagnostics are disabled.
    defaults <- list(
        ref_cutoff_category_A = 2,
        ref_cutoff_category_B = 2,
        use_OR_prior = 0,
        log_OR_shared = 1,
        prior_mu_logit_A_mean = -2,
        prior_mu_logit_A_sd = 1,
        prior_mu_logit_B_mean = -2,
        prior_mu_logit_B_sd = 1,
        prior_sigma_logit_sd = 0.5,
        prior_log_OR_mean = 0,
        prior_log_OR_sd = 1,
        use_cond_prior = 0,
        prior_logit_Q_mean = -1,
        prior_logit_Q_sd = 1
    )
    for (nm in names(defaults)) if (is.null(stan_data[[nm]])) stan_data[[nm]] <- defaults[[nm]]
    ## These are declared as vectors in Stan.  Explicit dim attributes are
    ## required for the one-element cases because a bare R vector can otherwise
    ## be unboxed by the JSON writer.
    stan_data$pop_weight <- array(as.numeric(stan_data$pop_weight),
                                  dim = length(stan_data$pop_weight))
    stan_data$standardisation_index <- array(as.integer(stan_data$standardisation_index),
                                             dim = length(stan_data$standardisation_index))
    stan_data$standardisation_weight <- array(as.numeric(stan_data$standardisation_weight),
                                              dim = length(stan_data$standardisation_weight))
    stan_data$grid_standardisation_position <- array(as.integer(stan_data$grid_standardisation_position),
                                                     dim = length(stan_data$grid_standardisation_position))
    stan_data$grid_standardisation_weight <- array(as.numeric(stan_data$grid_standardisation_weight),
                                                   dim = length(stan_data$grid_standardisation_weight))
    stopifnot(length(stan_data$pop_weight) == stan_data$n_pops,
              length(stan_data$standardisation_index) == stan_data$n_standardisation,
              length(stan_data$standardisation_weight) == stan_data$n_standardisation,
              length(stan_data$grid_standardisation_position) == stan_data$n_grid_standardisation,
              length(stan_data$grid_standardisation_weight) == stan_data$n_grid_standardisation)
    stan_data
}


four_class_write_json <- function(stan_data, json_file) {

    if (!requireNamespace("cmdstanr", quietly = TRUE)) stop("cmdstanr is required")
    dir.create(dirname(json_file), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
    cmdstanr::write_stan_json(data = stan_data, file = json_file)
    invisible(json_file)
}


four_class_read_fixture <- function(fixture_file) {

    if (!file.exists(fixture_file)) stop("Synthetic fixture not found: ", fixture_file)
    if (identical(tolower(tools::file_ext(fixture_file)), "r"))
        return(dget(fixture_file))
    stop("Portable fixtures must be supplied as fixture.R text files")
}

four_class_model_data_string <- function(data_json) {

    paste(readLines(data_json, warn = FALSE), collapse = "")
}


four_class_external_model_cache <- function(stan_file, paths, output_directory = NULL,
                                             build_signature = NULL) {

    if (!requireNamespace("digest", quietly = TRUE)) stop("digest is required")
    example_directory <- normalizePath(paths$example_directory, mustWork = FALSE)
    if (is.null(output_directory) ||
        normalizePath(output_directory, mustWork = FALSE) == example_directory ||
        startsWith(normalizePath(output_directory, mustWork = FALSE),
                   paste0(example_directory, .Platform$file.sep))) {
        output_directory <- file.path(tempdir(), "NicoStan_four_class_results")
    }
    dir.create(output_directory, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
    source_hash <- digest::digest(file = normalizePath(stan_file), algo = "sha256")
    signature <- if (is.null(build_signature)) "Stan_math" else substr(build_signature, 1, 12)
    cached_file <- file.path(output_directory,
                             paste0(tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(stan_file)),
                                    "_", substr(source_hash, 1L, 12L), "_", signature, ".stan"))
    if (!file.exists(cached_file) ||
        !identical(digest::digest(file = cached_file, algo = "sha256"), source_hash)) {
        stopifnot(file.copy(normalizePath(stan_file), cached_file, overwrite = TRUE))
    }
    list(stan_file = normalizePath(cached_file), output_directory = normalizePath(output_directory),
         source_sha256 = source_hash)
}


four_class_external_output_file <- function(output_rds, cache) {

    if (is.null(output_rds) ||
        startsWith(normalizePath(output_rds, mustWork = FALSE),
                   paste0(normalizePath(cache$output_directory), .Platform$file.sep)))
        return(output_rds)
    file.path(cache$output_directory, basename(output_rds))
}


four_class_assert_simd_lanes <- function(fit, expected_lanes = 8) {

    bs_model <- fit$init_object$bs_model
    gq_names <- bs_model$param_names(include_tp = TRUE, include_gq = TRUE)
    if (!"simd_lanes" %in% gq_names)
        stop("The AVX model has no generated-quantity SIMD lane probe")
    constrained <- bs_model$param_constrain(rep(0, bs_model$param_unc_num()),
                                             include_tp = TRUE, include_gq = TRUE,
                                             rng = bs_model$new_rng(seed = 2026))
    lane_index <- match("simd_lanes", gq_names)
    lane <- unname(constrained[lane_index])
    if (!is.finite(lane) || abs(lane - expected_lanes) > 1e-8)
        stop("AVX SIMD lane probe returned ", lane, "; expected ", expected_lanes)
    as.numeric(lane)
}


check_four_class_bridge_parity <- function(
    paths = four_class_example_paths(),
    data_json = paths$fixture_json,
    avx_header = NULL) {

    if (!requireNamespace("bridgestan", quietly = TRUE)) stop("bridgestan is required")
    if (!file.exists(paths$source_Stan_math) || !file.exists(paths$source_avx)) stop("Stan::math/AVX source missing")
    data_string <- four_class_model_data_string(data_json)
    load_model <- function(stan_file, data_string, stanc_args = NULL, make_args = NULL) {

        so_file <- paste0(tools::file_path_sans_ext(normalizePath(stan_file)), "_model.so")
        if (!file.exists(so_file)) {
            so_file <- bridgestan::compile_model(normalizePath(stan_file),
                                                 stanc_args = stanc_args,
                                                 make_args = make_args)
        }
        bridgestan::StanModel$new(lib = normalizePath(so_file), data = data_string, seed = 123)
    }

    if (is.null(avx_header)) stop("Supply the BayesMVP AVX header for the AVX comparison")
    if (!file.exists(avx_header)) stop("AVX header not found: ", avx_header)
    compare_one_data <- function(data_string, label) {

        stan_math <- load_model(paths$source_Stan_math, data_string)
        avx <- load_model(paths$source_avx, data_string, stanc_args = "--allow-undefined",
                          make_args = c("STAN_THREADS=true",
                                        paste0("USER_HEADER=", normalizePath(avx_header))))
        set.seed(2026)
        points <- c(list(rep(0, stan_math$param_unc_num())),
                    lapply(seq_len(3), function(ii) rnorm(stan_math$param_unc_num(), sd = 0.2)))
        errors <- lapply(points, function(theta) {

            p <- stan_math$log_density_gradient(theta, propto = FALSE, jacobian = TRUE)
            a <- avx$log_density_gradient(theta, propto = FALSE, jacobian = TRUE)
            finite <- is.finite(p$val) && is.finite(a$val) && all(is.finite(p$gradient)) &&
                      all(is.finite(a$gradient))
            list(log_density_absolute_error = abs(p$val - a$val),
                 maximum_scaled_gradient_error = if (finite) max(abs(p$gradient - a$gradient) /
                                                                  pmax(1, abs(p$gradient))) else NA_real_,
                 finite = finite)
        })

        result <- list(
            label = label,
            unconstrained_dimension = stan_math$param_unc_num(),
            maximum_log_density_absolute_error = max(vapply(errors, `[[`, numeric(1),
                                                          "log_density_absolute_error")),
            maximum_scaled_gradient_error = max(vapply(errors, `[[`, numeric(1),
                                                     "maximum_scaled_gradient_error")),
            finite = all(vapply(errors, `[[`, logical(1), "finite"))
        )
        stopifnot(result$finite, result$maximum_log_density_absolute_error < 1e-5,
                  result$maximum_scaled_gradient_error < 1e-5)
        result
    }

    results <- list(default_normal = compare_one_data(data_string, "Phi_type=1"))
    ## The approximation branch is the one where AVX and Stan are expected to
    ## differ slightly.  It exercises the custom nico_Phi_approx/log kernels.
    approximation_data <- sub('"Phi_type"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*1',
                              '"Phi_type": 2', data_string, perl = TRUE)
    results$approximation <- compare_one_data(approximation_data, "Phi_type=2")
    results
}


run_four_class_nicostan_smoke <- function(
    paths = four_class_example_paths(),
    fixture_file = paths$fixture_file,
    stan_file = paths$source_Stan_math,
    math_backend = c("Stan", "AVX512", "AVX2"),
    avx_header = file.path(dirname(dirname(paths$paper3_directory)), "R_packages", "BayesMVP",
                           "inst", "BayesMVP", "inst", "include", "BayesMVP",
                           "stan_external_functions.hpp"),
    chains = 2, warmup = 60, iterations = 80, adapt_delta = 0.9, seed = 2026,
    metric_type_main = "Empirical", metric_shape_main = "diag",
    M_decay_type = "inverse", phi_type = NULL,
    output_rds = file.path(paths$runtime_directory, "nicostan_Stan_math_smoke.rds")) {

    math_backend <- match.arg(math_backend)
    if (!requireNamespace("NicoStan", quietly = TRUE)) stop("NicoStan is required")
    fixture <- four_class_read_fixture(fixture_file)
    fixture$data <- four_class_add_current_data_fields(fixture$data)
    if (!is.null(phi_type)) fixture$data$Phi_type <- as.integer(phi_type)
    if (!file.exists(stan_file)) stop("Stan source missing: ", stan_file)
    if (chains > length(fixture$initial_values))
        stop("The fixture contains only ", length(fixture$initial_values), " initial-value lists")
    ## math_backend = "AVX2" compiles the same AVX model with the same flags as "AVX512" plus
    ## -DBAYESMVP_FORCE_AVX2 (make argument CPPFLAGS_OPTIM), which makes the BayesMVP header use its 4-lane AVX2 kernels on an
    ## AVX-512 machine too. (-mno-avx512f in CXXFLAGS would not work here: BridgeStan's make/local APPENDS -mavx512f to the
    ## CXXFLAGS environment variable.) The define is part of the build signature, so the AVX2 and AVX512 builds never share
    ## a cached binary, and four_class_assert_simd_lanes() stops unless the model reports 4 (AVX2) / 8 (AVX512) lanes.
    uses_avx_backend <- math_backend %in% c("AVX512", "AVX2")
    if (uses_avx_backend && !file.exists(avx_header))
        stop("AVX header not found: ", avx_header)
    avx_flags <- if (uses_avx_backend)
        "-O3 -std=c++17 -march=native -mtune=native -mfma -mavx2 -mavx512f -mavx512vl -mavx512dq" else
        "-O3 -std=c++17 -march=native -mtune=native -mfma"
    avx_level_make_args <- if (identical(math_backend, "AVX2")) "CPPFLAGS_OPTIM=-DBAYESMVP_FORCE_AVX2" else character(0)
    expected_simd_lanes <- if (identical(math_backend, "AVX512")) 8 else if (identical(math_backend, "AVX2")) 4 else NA_real_
    build_signature <- if (uses_avx_backend)
        digest::digest(c(list(header = digest::digest(file = avx_header, algo = "sha256"),
                              flags = avx_flags),
                         if (length(avx_level_make_args) > 0) list(level = avx_level_make_args)), algo = "sha256") else NULL
    cache <- four_class_external_model_cache(stan_file, paths, paths$runtime_directory,
                                             build_signature = build_signature)
    output_rds <- four_class_external_output_file(output_rds, cache)
    stan_file <- cache$stan_file
    old_cxxflags <- Sys.getenv("CXXFLAGS", unset = NA_character_)
    if (uses_avx_backend) Sys.setenv(CXXFLAGS = avx_flags)
    on.exit({
        if (is.na(old_cxxflags)) Sys.unsetenv("CXXFLAGS") else Sys.setenv(CXXFLAGS = old_cxxflags)
    }, add = TRUE)
    fit <- NicoStan::MVP_model$new(
        Model_type = "Stan",
        Stan_data_list = fixture$data,
        Stan_model_file_path = normalizePath(stan_file),
        sample_nuisance = TRUE,
        Stan_cpp_user_header = if (uses_avx_backend) normalizePath(avx_header) else NULL,
        make_args = if (uses_avx_backend)
            c("STAN_THREADS=true", paste0("USER_HEADER=", normalizePath(avx_header)), avx_level_make_args) else NULL
    )
    simd_lanes <- if (uses_avx_backend) four_class_assert_simd_lanes(fit, expected_lanes = expected_simd_lanes) else NA_real_
    ## Deliberately no n_nuisance_override: the first u_raw declaration is
    ## recovered from stanc metadata, and its unconstrained dimension is used.
    set.seed(seed)
    fit_started <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
    fit$sample(
        n_burnin = warmup, n_iter = iterations,
        n_chains_burnin = chains, n_chains_sampling = chains,
        n_superchains = chains, init_lists_per_chain = fixture$initial_values[seq_len(chains)],
        burnin_algorithm = "CHESSR", diffusion_HMC = FALSE,
        partitioned_HMC = FALSE, metric_type_main = metric_type_main,
        metric_shape_main = metric_shape_main, metric_type_nuisance = "uniform_diag",
        M_decay_type = M_decay_type,
        n_threads_WCP_burnin = 1, n_threads_WCP_sampling = 1,
        adapt_delta = adapt_delta, n_refresh = 20, seed = seed, stream = seed,
        reorder_cols_MVP = FALSE
    )
    fit_wall_seconds <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - fit_started
    fit$summary(save_log_lik_trace = FALSE, compute_nested_rhat = FALSE,
                compute_generated_quantities = FALSE)
    efficiency <- fit$model_fit_object$summaries$efficiency_info
    main_summary <- fit$model_fit_object$summaries$summary_tibbles$summary_tibble_main_params
    posterior_summary <- posterior::summarise_draws(
        posterior::as_draws_array(fit$model_fit_object$traces$traces_as_arrays$trace_params_main),
        "mean", "sd", "ess_bulk", "ess_tail", "rhat")
    min_bulk_ess <- min(posterior_summary$ess_bulk, na.rm = TRUE)
    max_bulk_rhat <- max(posterior_summary$rhat, na.rm = TRUE)
    gradient_work <- efficiency$L_main_during_sampling * iterations * chains
    main_bases <- c("Omega_unconstrained_vec", "beta_own_absent_free",
                    "beta_own_present_free", "delta_cross_free",
                    "beta_cov_raw", "prev_simplex", "C_raw_vec",
                    "d_raw_present")
    result <- list(
        fit = fit,
        math_backend = math_backend,
        n_nuisance = fit$n_nuisance,
        n_params_main = fit$n_params_main,
        n_params = fit$init_object$n_params,
        n_params_main_unconstrained = fit$n_params_main,
        main_parameter_bases = main_bases,
        main_parameter_count_constrained = nrow(main_summary),
        automatic_nuisance_detection = isTRUE(fit$n_nuisance > 0),
        randomize_tau_burnin = fit$result$randomize_tau_burnin,
        randomize_tau_sampling = fit$result$randomize_tau_sampling,
        divergences = fit$model_fit_object$summaries$divergences$n_divs,
        min_ess_main = min_bulk_ess,
        max_rhat_main = max_bulk_rhat,
        sampling_seconds = efficiency$time_sampling,
        fit_wall_seconds = fit_wall_seconds,
        total_seconds = fit_wall_seconds,
        min_ess_per_sec_sampling = min_bulk_ess / efficiency$time_sampling,
        min_ess_per_sec_total = min_bulk_ess / fit_wall_seconds,
        gradient_work = gradient_work,
        min_ess_per_1000_gradient_work = 1000 * min_bulk_ess / gradient_work,
        gradient_work_basis = "NicoStan L_main_during_sampling times iterations times chains; gradient-work proxy",
        metric_type_main = metric_type_main,
        M_decay_type = M_decay_type,
        phi_type = fixture$data$Phi_type,
        avx_kernel_path_active = uses_avx_backend && fixture$data$Phi_type != 1,
        avx_kernel_path = if (uses_avx_backend && fixture$data$Phi_type != 1)
            "BayesMVP vectorized external branch" else if (uses_avx_backend)
            "Stan exact-CDF branch; external vector functions bypassed" else "Stan built-in math",
        simd_lanes = simd_lanes,
        avx_compile_flags = if (uses_avx_backend) paste(c(avx_flags, avx_level_make_args), collapse = " ") else NA_character_,
        avx_build_signature = if (uses_avx_backend) build_signature else NA_character_
    )
    stopifnot(result$automatic_nuisance_detection,
              is.null(fit$n_nuisance_override),
              identical(result$randomize_tau_burnin, FALSE),
              identical(result$randomize_tau_sampling, TRUE))
    saveRDS(result, output_rds)
    result
}


run_four_class_cmdstanr_smoke <- function(
    paths = four_class_example_paths(),
    fixture_file = paths$fixture_file,
    stan_file = paths$source_Stan_math,
    chains = 2, warmup = 60, iterations = 80, adapt_delta = 0.9, phi_type = NULL, seed = 2026,
    output_rds = file.path(paths$runtime_directory, "cmdstanr_plain_smoke.rds")) {

    if (!requireNamespace("cmdstanr", quietly = TRUE)) stop("cmdstanr is required")
    fixture <- four_class_read_fixture(fixture_file)
    fixture$data <- four_class_add_current_data_fields(fixture$data)
    if (!is.null(phi_type)) fixture$data$Phi_type <- as.integer(phi_type)
    if (chains > length(fixture$initial_values))
        stop("The fixture contains only ", length(fixture$initial_values), " initial-value lists")
    cache <- four_class_external_model_cache(stan_file, paths, paths$runtime_directory)
    output_rds <- four_class_external_output_file(output_rds, cache)
    stan_file <- cache$stan_file
    model <- cmdstanr::cmdstan_model(normalizePath(stan_file),
                                     cpp_options = list(stan_threads = TRUE), quiet = TRUE)
    fit_started <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
    fit <- model$sample(
        data = fixture$data,
        init = fixture$initial_values[seq_len(chains)],
        chains = chains, parallel_chains = chains, threads_per_chain = 1,
        iter_warmup = warmup, iter_sampling = iterations,
        adapt_delta = adapt_delta, seed = seed, refresh = 20,
        output_dir = cache$output_directory
    )
    fit_wall_seconds <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - fit_started
    main_parameters <- c("Omega_unconstrained_vec", "beta_own_absent_free",
                         "beta_own_present_free", "delta_cross_free",
                         "beta_cov_raw", "prev_simplex", "C_raw_vec",
                         "d_raw_present")
    summary <- fit$summary(variables = main_parameters)
    diagnostics <- as.array(fit$sampler_diagnostics())
    gradient_work <- sum(diagnostics[, , "n_leapfrog__"])
    sampling_seconds <- max(fit$time()$chains$sampling)
    total_seconds <- fit$time()$total
    posterior_summary <- posterior::summarise_draws(
        posterior::as_draws_array(fit$draws(variables = main_parameters)),
        "mean", "sd", "ess_bulk", "ess_tail", "rhat")
    min_ess <- min(posterior_summary$ess_bulk, na.rm = TRUE)
    max_rhat <- max(posterior_summary$rhat, na.rm = TRUE)
    result <- list(
        fit = fit,
        math_backend = "Stan",
        n_nuisance = as.integer(fixture$data$N * fixture$data$n_tests),
        n_params_main = 67,
        main_parameter_names = summary$variable,
        n_params_main_unconstrained = 67,
        main_parameter_count_constrained = nrow(summary),
        min_ess_main = min_ess,
        max_rhat_main = max_rhat,
        divergences = sum(diagnostics[, , "divergent__"]),
        sampling_seconds = sampling_seconds,
        fit_wall_seconds = fit_wall_seconds,
        total_seconds = fit_wall_seconds,
        min_ess_per_sec_sampling = min_ess / sampling_seconds,
        min_ess_per_sec_total = min_ess / fit_wall_seconds,
        gradient_work = gradient_work,
        min_ess_per_1000_gradient_work = 1000 * min_ess / gradient_work,
        gradient_work_basis = "CmdStan sum of n_leapfrog__; gradient-work proxy", 
        metric_type_main = "NUTS",
        M_decay_type = NA_character_,
        phi_type = fixture$data$Phi_type,
        avx_kernel_path_active = FALSE,
        avx_kernel_path = "Stan built-in math",
        timings = fit$time()
    )
    saveRDS(result, output_rds)
    result
}

## Portable four-class example runner.
##
## Usage from this directory:
##   Rscript run_four_class_example.R NicoStan Stan 24
##   Rscript run_four_class_example.R NicoStan AVX512 24
##   Rscript run_four_class_example.R NicoStan AVX2 24     (AVX2 kernels; also works on an AVX-512 machine)
##   Rscript run_four_class_example.R cmdstanr Stan 24
## Add a fourth argument to choose the writable output directory.
##
## The default N grid is 24, 48, 96.  The three arms use the same synthetic
## fixture and the same main-parameter registry.  The AVX arm needs the general
## BayesMVP external header from an installed BayesMVP extension package.

script_file <- sub("^--file=", "", commandArgs()[startsWith(commandArgs(), "--file=")])
example_directory <- dirname(normalizePath(script_file, mustWork = TRUE))
source(file.path(example_directory, "four_class_example.R"), local = TRUE)

arguments <- commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE)
engine <- if (length(arguments) >= 1L) arguments[1L] else "NicoStan"
backend <- if (length(arguments) >= 2L) arguments[2L] else "Stan"
N <- if (length(arguments) >= 3L) as.integer(arguments[3L]) else 24L
output_directory <- if (length(arguments) >= 4L) normalizePath(arguments[4L], mustWork = FALSE) else
    file.path(getwd(), "NicoStan_four_class_results")
if (!engine %in% c("NicoStan", "cmdstanr")) stop("engine must be NicoStan or cmdstanr")
if (!backend %in% c("Stan", "AVX512", "AVX2")) stop("backend must be Stan, AVX512 or AVX2")
if (engine == "cmdstanr" && backend != "Stan") stop("CmdStanR uses the Stan::math arm")
if (!N %in% c(24L, 48L, 96L)) stop("N must be one of 24, 48, or 96")

paths <- four_class_example_paths(example_directory = example_directory)
paths$runtime_directory <- output_directory
dir.create(paths$runtime_directory, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
fixture_directory <- file.path(paths$fixture_directory, paste0("N", N))
fixture_file <- file.path(fixture_directory, "fixture.R")
if (engine == "cmdstanr") {
    result <- run_four_class_cmdstanr_smoke(
        paths = paths,
        fixture_file = fixture_file,
        stan_file = paths$source_Stan_math,
        output_rds = file.path(paths$runtime_directory,
                               paste0("cmdstanr_plain_N", N, ".rds"))
    )
} else {
    stan_file <- if (backend == "Stan") paths$source_Stan_math else paths$source_avx
    avx_header <- system.file("include", "BayesMVP", "stan_external_functions.hpp",
                              package = "BayesMVP")
    if (backend %in% c("AVX512", "AVX2") && (!nzchar(avx_header) || !file.exists(avx_header)))
        stop("Install the BayesMVP extension package before running the ", backend, " arm")
    result <- run_four_class_nicostan_smoke(
        paths = paths,
        fixture_file = fixture_file,
        stan_file = stan_file,
        math_backend = backend,
        avx_header = if (backend %in% c("AVX512", "AVX2")) avx_header else NULL,
        output_rds = file.path(paths$runtime_directory,
                               paste0("nicostan_", tolower(backend), "_N", N, ".rds"))
    )
}
print(result[c("math_backend", "simd_lanes", "n_nuisance", "n_params_main", "automatic_nuisance_detection")])

#### =====================================================================================================================================
## random_intercepts.R
##
## A simulated logistic random-intercept example. This is a usage example, not a comparative benchmark.
##
run_random_intercepts <-  function( burnin_algorithm = "CHESSR",
                                     model_file = NULL) {

        ## Compile in a writable temporary directory rather than inside the installed package.
        if (is.null(model_file)) {
                model_directory <-  tempfile(pattern = "nicostan_random_intercepts_")
                dir.create(path = model_directory)
                model_file <-  file.path(model_directory, "random_intercepts.stan")
                stopifnot(file.copy(from = system.file("examples", "random_intercepts.stan", package = "NicoStan"),
                                   to = model_file))
        }
        stopifnot(file.exists(model_file))
        set.seed(seed = 2026)
        n_groups <-  20
        n_observations <-  200
        group <-  rep(x = seq_len(n_groups), each = n_observations / n_groups)
        x <-  rnorm(n = n_observations)
        group_effect <-  rnorm(n = n_groups, sd = 0.6)
        probability <-  plogis(q = -0.4 + 0.8 * x + group_effect[group])
        stan_data <-  list(N = n_observations, J = n_groups, group = group, x = x,
                           y = rbinom(n = n_observations, size = 1, prob = probability))
        ##
        model <-  NicoStan::MVP_model$new(Model_type = "Stan",
                                           Stan_data_list = stan_data,
                                           Stan_model_file_path = model_file,
                                           nuisance_params = "z",
                                           sample_nuisance = TRUE)
        initial_values <-  lapply(X = seq_len(4), FUN = function(chain) {

                list(z = rep(x = 0, times = n_groups), alpha = 0.1 * (chain - 2.5), beta = 0, sigma = 0.6)
        })

        ##
        model$sample(n_burnin = 125, n_iter = 250,
                      n_chains_burnin = 4, n_chains_sampling = 4, n_superchains = 2,
                      init_lists_per_chain = initial_values,
                      burnin_algorithm = burnin_algorithm,
                      diffusion_HMC = TRUE, partitioned_HMC = FALSE,
                      metric_type_main = "Empirical", metric_shape_main = "diag",
                      metric_type_nuisance = "uniform_diag",
                      M_decay_type = "inverse", M_decay_power = 0.5, M_decay_scale = 1.13,
                      ratio_M_main = 0.9, ratio_M_nuisance = 0.9,
                      learning_rate = 0.05, learning_rate_initial = 0.1,
                      n_threads_WCP_burnin = 1, n_threads_WCP_sampling = 1,
                      adapt_delta = 0.80, n_refresh = 25,
                      seed = 2026, stream = 2026, reorder_cols_MVP = FALSE)
        return(model)

}
